title: Deuteronomy 15:11
text: God suffers the poor always to be among us, that compassion may be cultivated by exercise and that we may have opportunity to show whether or not we are disposed to assist them, and thus to imitate our Father in heaven.   Matthew 5:48 Luke 6:31-36

title: Deuteronomy 15:12
text: If thy brother--be sold unto thee; be bound to serve thee for the payment of a debt, according to the custom of that age.

title: Deuteronomy 15:14
text: Liberality to servants and those who have assisted us, and readiness in return to assist them, is an exhibition of excellence, and a source of blessings to both givers and receivers.

title: Deuteronomy 15:16
text:
Because he is well with thee; because, in his estimation, it would be better for him to stay than to go away. 
 
It is well so to treat servants as to secure their confidence, gratitude, and esteem, and that they will rather continue with us than go away.  By so doing, their services may be greatly prolonged, and rendered much more pleasant and useful to us and to themselves.

title: Deuteronomy 15:18
text:
Worth a double hired servant; because he has served without wages. 
 
Kindness and liberality to servants are means of securing not only their good will and fidelity, but also the blessing of God.

title: Deuteronomy 15:22
text:
Within thy gates; at home: not at the tabernacle or temple, as was the case with that which was without blemish.   Deuteronomy 12:15-16  
 
Fidelity to God, in rendering to him what he requires, is the way to secure his favors, and make them the means of the greatest enjoyment to ourselves and others.

title: Deuteronomy 16:1
text: The month of Abib--the passover;  Exodus 12:2 Exodus 12:18 Exodus 34:1

title: Deuteronomy 16:3
text:
Bread of affliction; in remembrance of their afflictions in Egypt. 
 
We should not forget our past trials, nor the goodness of God in our deliverance, but should be encouraged by his kindness to put our trust in him, and with patient continuance in well-doing look to him for all we need.

title: Deuteronomy 16:6
text: Such is the unteachableness of men, that the Lord sees it needful often to repeat his instructions, especially with regard to their guilt as sinners, and their need of pardoning mercy through the atonement of Christ.

title: Deuteronomy 16:9
text: To put the sickle; to reap the sheaf of first-fruits, which was offered on the first day of unleavened bread.

title: Deuteronomy 16:10
text: The feast of weeks;  Exodus 34:1

title: Deuteronomy 16:11
text: True religion is social in its character, and tends to make all who possess it grateful, kind, communicative, benevolent, and joyful.

title: Deuteronomy 16:13
text: The feast of tabernacles;

title: Deuteronomy 16:17
text: Religious joy and gratitude to God may at suitable times be properly expressed by feasting on the bounties of his providence, and giving them liberally to the poor and destitute.

title: Deuteronomy 16:19
text:
Wrest; pervert. 
 
  A gift; a bribe, something given to make a judge partial. 
 
  Doth blind the eyes of the wise; to truth and equity.

title: Deuteronomy 16:20
text: Civil government is God's institution to secure to men those rights and privileges which it is his will that they should enjoy; and magistrates are bound, as far as practicable, to give to all what justly belongs to them.

title: Deuteronomy 16:21
text: Grove; the word in the original rather means a wooden image of Astarte, fixed in the ground.  See  II Kings 17:10 .

title: Deuteronomy 17:1
text: The best we have belongs to God, and it should be our delight cheerfully to render to him whatever he requires.

title: Deuteronomy 17:7
text:
First upon him;  Deuteronomy 13:1 
 
Idolatry in the Jewish commonwealth was treason, and as such, when proved by two or more witnesses, was punished with death; but great care was taken that none should be punished except those who were really guilty.

title: Deuteronomy 17:8
text:
Blood and blood; relating to the killing of a man. 
 
  Plea and plea; concerning property, or civil rights. 
 
  Stroke and stroke; personal quarrel.

title: Deuteronomy 17:9
text:
Come unto the--judge; apply to a higher tribunal, at the head of which was God himself. 
 
  Sentence of judgment; right decision. 
 
It is a great privilege that in cases of doubt and difficulty with regard to duty, we may appeal to an infallible standard, the Scriptures; and look to Him who hath said, If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, and it shall be given him.

title: Deuteronomy 17:12
text:
Do presumptuously; refuse to comply with known law, enacted by God, who was then the chief magistrate of that people. 
 
To turn away and refuse to do the known will of God, is great presumption, wickedness, and folly; and justly exposes those who are guilty of it to his indignation.

title: Deuteronomy 17:15
text:
Shalt thou set king over thee; this did not require them to set a king over them, or imply that it would be right; it only required, that if at any time they would do it, these directions should be followed.  I Samuel 8:4-22  
 
The giving of directions for the regulation of the conduct of men, by no means proves that the conduct which needs such regulation is right. It may be wicked, and the object of the regulations be, to lessen somewhat its evils till it be done away.

title: Deuteronomy 17:18
text: This law; either the book of Deuteronomy, or more probably the five books of Moses, called the law, as containing the laws of Jehovah for the government of Israel.   Matthew 5:17 Matthew 7:12 Luke 16:16 Luke 24:44

title: Deuteronomy 17:19
text: All the days of his life; daily, habitually.

title: Deuteronomy 17:20
text:
Be not lifted up; do not become proud. 
 
God gives the people power to choose their own rulers and form of government; and rulers are bound to take the Bible as their guide, and govern according to its precepts.

title: Deuteronomy 18:5
text: Often and in a variety of ways the Lord shows that, while it is not his will that his ministers should be rich, or engage in worldly business for gain, it is his will that they should receive a support for themselves and their families, and devote themselves cheerfully and faithfully to their appropriate work.

title: Deuteronomy 18:8
text: Patrimony; other property besides what he received officially as a Levite.

title: Deuteronomy 18:12
text: Pretended conversation with evil spirits, and all seeking of information or any good from those who pretend to have such conversation, are an abomination in the sight of God.

title: Deuteronomy 18:13
text: Be perfect; sincerely, heartily, and wholly devoted to God.  Job 1:1 Matthew 5:43-48

title: Deuteronomy 18:15
text:
A Prophet; referring to Jesus Christ.   Deuteronomy 18:18-19 Acts 3:22-23  
 
  Of thy brethren; one who shall have the same human nature with them.  Compare  Hebrews 2:11-12 Hebrews 2:14 . 
 
  Like unto me; standing, as Moses did, at the head of a new dispensation, and being, like him, a mediator between God and his people.  Compare  Hebrews 3:2-6 .

title: Deuteronomy 18:16
text: Thou desiredst;  Exodus 20:19 Hebrews 12:1

title: Deuteronomy 18:18
text: Moses was in various respects an eminent type of Christ, especially in acting as mediator between God and the people, and making known to them his will.

title: Deuteronomy 18:19
text:
Require it of him; call him to account and punish him for his neglect. 
 
If he who rejected the testimony of Moses and despised his law died without mercy, of how much sorer punishment will he be thought worthy who rejects the testimony of Christ and despises his commands?  Hebrews 10:28-29

title: Deuteronomy 18:22
text:
Speaketh in the name of the Lord; pretends to do it, and to foretell future events. 
 
God has given to men, in the holy Scriptures, the means of judging, and by these they are bound to judge whether those who profess to speak in his name, do or do not declare his truth.   Acts 17:11

title: Deuteronomy 19:2
text: Separate three cities; to be cities of refuge on the west side of Jordan, as he already had done on the east side.   Deuteronomy 4:41-43

title: Deuteronomy 19:7
text: Great care should be taken that men do not suffer for that of which they are not guilty.

title: Deuteronomy 19:12
text: Deliver him into the hand of the avenger; after he had been proved guilty of murder.

title: Deuteronomy 19:13
text:
Shall not pity him; in any such way as to prevent his execution. 
 
If men are proved to be guilty of murder, no pity or compassion should save them from the punishment which God requires to be inflicted on them.

title: Deuteronomy 19:14
text:
Landmark; that which showed the division line between the property of one man and another. 
 
Every attempt of men to appropriate to themselves what belongs to others is a sin against God, and exposes those who are guilty of it to his wrath.

title: Deuteronomy 19:15
text: One witness shall not rise; a man shall not be condemned on the testimony of one witness only.

title: Deuteronomy 19:18
text: Inquisition; inquiry.

title: Deuteronomy 19:19
text: Do unto him; he shall receive the punishment which he sought to bring on another.

title: Deuteronomy 19:21
text: Few crimes are more offensive to God than bearing false witness; and whether false accusers meet due punishment or not in this world, continuing impenitent they will not escape it in the world to come.

title: Deuteronomy 20:1
text:
Thine enemies; foreign nations who should make war upon the Israelites, or against whom God should call the Israelites to make war. 
 
Men should not go to war except when God requires it; and when he does, their dependence should be not on themselves or their fellow men, but on him; and their object not their own gratification or aggrandizement, but the promotion of his glory and the highest good of mankind.

title: Deuteronomy 20:5
text:
Dedicated it; by acknowledging the goodness of God in giving it, feasting on the bounties of his providence, and seeking his blessing. 
 
The Lord is disposed to gratify all the innocent and useful affections of men, and not to call them ot arduous, self-denying, and dangerous duties, except when his glory and their good require it.

title: Deuteronomy 20:7
text: Betrothed a wife; engaged to marry her.

title: Deuteronomy 20:8
text: Return unto his house; to free the army from all who were unwilling to go into the battle.

title: Deuteronomy 20:10
text: Proclaim peace; propose terms of peace.   Deuteronomy 20:11

title: Deuteronomy 20:11
text: Peace, wherever it can consistently be maintained, is desired by God, and should be by all men.   Matthew 5:9 Matthew 5:43-48 Romans 12:18 Romans 14:19 Hebrews 12:14

title: Deuteronomy 20:13
text: Smite every male; this was directed by God as a punishment for their sins, and was designed so to weaken the nation that they would not be likely to make war upon the Israelites in future.

title: Deuteronomy 20:16
text: These people; the Canaanites, who were by God devoted to destruction, and whose land the Israelites were to possess.

title: Deuteronomy 20:18
text: As it is wicked to kill any human being unless God require it, so it is wicked to spare any whom he requires to be slain.  I Samuel 15:3 I Samuel 15:8 I Samuel 15:11 I Samuel 15:23

title: Deuteronomy 20:19
text:
Not destroy the trees; the fruit-trees. 
 
  The tree--is man's life; it's fruit is the means of his support.

title: Deuteronomy 20:20
text: Not trees for meat; not fruit-trees.

title: Deuteronomy 21:4
text:
A rough valley; or, a valley with a continually flowing stream. Compare  Deuteronomy 21:6 . 
 
  Eared; ploughed.   Genesis 45:7  
 
The great doctrine of atonement by the substitution of the death of the innocent for that of the guilty, is taught often, and in various ways, throughout the Bible, showing the great importance of the right understanding and use of this truth.

title: Deuteronomy 21:6
text: Shall wash their hands; a profession of their innocence by actions.  Deuteronomy 21:7-8

title: Deuteronomy 21:9
text:
The guilt of innocent blood; these transactions strikingly showed God's abhorrence of murder and the guilt of committing it, and were designed as a safeguard to human life. 
 
The guilt of murder rests upon every land in which it is committed, if proper measures are not taken to acquit the innocent and punish the guilty.

title: Deuteronomy 21:12
text: Pare her nails; the word rendered pare signifies to make or dress, and may mean to let them grow, as persons did in mourning.

title: Deuteronomy 21:14
text: Not sell her--for money; conquerors were accustomed to sell those whom they took in war, but God in this case forbade the Israelites to do it; not to sanction as right in any case the practice here forbidden, but in some measure to lessen its evils while it continued; and open the way for it, under increasing light and love, to be ultimately done away.

title: Deuteronomy 21:15
text: One beloved, and another hated; this regulation did not imply that it was right for a man to have two wives, or to hate either; but, like the regulation in  Deuteronomy 21:14 , was designed to lessen the evils of a wrong practice, while men were so ignorant, wicked, debased, and cruel as to continue it.

title: Deuteronomy 21:17
text: Though all wrong practices among the Israelites, on account of their wickedness and hardness of heart, were not at once discontinued, or in the course of providence abolished, God was kind and gracious in giving them regulations which, while those practices continued, lessened in some measure their evils.

title: Deuteronomy 21:20
text:
Say unto the elders; concerning their son, that and that only which was true. 
 
Rebellion of children against the wise and good instruction and authority of parents is highly offensive to God, and exposes those who are guilty of it to be abandoned of him, and given up to vice, infamy, and ruin.

title: Deuteronomy 21:21
text: The men of his city shall stone him; to show God's abhorrence of the son's conduct, and prevent others from imitating his example.

title: Deuteronomy 21:23
text: He that is hanged is accursed of God; he is set forth as the object of God's curse.  For this reason the degradation of such an act ought not to be prolonged beyond the necessary ends of justice.  Compare the use which the apostle Paul makes of this passage in  Galatians 3:13 .

title: Deuteronomy 22:1
text: Hide thyself from them; pass by as if you did not see them; refuse to care for them.

title: Deuteronomy 22:2
text: The Old Testament as well as the New requires men to do to others as in like circumstances they ought to wish others to do to them.

title: Deuteronomy 22:3
text: Things which others have lost, and which we find, are not ours if by using suitable means we can find the owner.

title: Deuteronomy 22:4
text: The law of God requires us to exercise compassion not only towards our fellow men, but also towards animals in distress, and to make all proper efforts to relieve them.

title: Deuteronomy 22:5
text:
Shall not wear that; because it tended to impurity and wickedness. 
 
All practices which tend to impurity of heart of or life, in ourselves or others, should be avoided.

title: Deuteronomy 22:6
text:
Shalt not take the dam; it would be cruel, and tend to sanction cruelty, and also to extirpate that species of birds. 
 
The directions of God are suited to lessen, and should they be perfectly followed, to do away the selfishness and cruelty of the human heart, and lead it to delight in the happiness of the whole sensitive creation.

title: Deuteronomy 22:7
text:
Take the young; that is, the young only: not a command to take young birds from the nest, but a prohibition of their being taken with the parent bird. 
 
  Prolong thy days; by showing a tender and kind spirit, even to the brute creation. 
 
The manifestaton of a kind and compassionate disposition is favorable to the continuance of life, prosperity, and happiness.

title: Deuteronomy 22:8
text:
A battlement for thy roof; a wall or railing around the roof, to keep persons from falling off; as their roofs were flat, and were often resorted to for air and exercise. 
 
Carelessness as well as cruelty is offensive to God, and tends to bring numerous evils upon men.  If others suffer through our neglect, we shall be held responsible at the divine tribunal.

title: Deuteronomy 22:9
text:
vv 9-12. 
 
  Divers sorts; these directions may have been designed to prevent the Israelites from imitating the heathen, and keep them a separate people.  Some think that they have also a symbolical meaning, and forbid the mixture of things that are incongruous in morals and religion.  Compare  II Corinthians 6:14-16 . 
 
Jehovah delights in harmony, propriety, decency, and order.  Every thing contrary to these, and tending to corrupt the imagination, pervert the judgment, or deprave the heart, is offensive in his sight.

title: Deuteronomy 22:13
text:
vv 13-21. 
 
  Occasions of speech against her; these directions were designed to prevent unjust accusations, to protect the innocent, and punish the guilty.

title: Deuteronomy 22:21
text: Marriage is an institution of God, established at the creation, and to continue to the end of time.  Its obligations are most sacred, and those who violate them are exposed to his awful curse.

title: Deuteronomy 22:22
text: They shall both of them die; this was on the ground that both were consenting to the wickedness.

title: Deuteronomy 22:25
text: By the penalty which God under the Jewish dispensation affixed to adultery, he showed his deep and unchanging abhorrence of that crime, and the sore punishment which, without repentance awaits the guilty in the future world.

title: Deuteronomy 23:1
text: Not enter into the congregation of the Lord; not be admitted to worship in the temple.  This was designed to prevent Israelitish parents from mutilating their children, as was often done among the heathen.

title: Deuteronomy 23:2
text: Every thing should be avoided by parents which tends to deprive children of any of the privileges and blessings of the people of God.

title: Deuteronomy 23:3
text:
Ammonite--Moabite; these nations bordered upon that part of Canaan which lay east of the Jordan. 
 
Sins committed by parents may, long after they are dead, entail great evils on their children--and sins committed by rulers, great evils on the people.

title: Deuteronomy 23:7
text: Brother; relative, being descended like themselves from Abraham and Isaac.

title: Deuteronomy 23:8
text: Shall enter into the congregation; become entitled to all the privileges of an Israelite, if they embrace his religion.

title: Deuteronomy 23:9
text:
The host; the army of Israel. 
 
vv 9-14 
 
The individuals of an army, even when going forth to battle, are all, from the commander-in-chief to the lowest subaltern, sacredly bound to be holy in body and spirit; to indulge no feelings and allow no actions which shall not be pleasing to God, and tend to fit them for the purity, the employments, and the bliss of heaven.

title: Deuteronomy 23:10
text:
vv 10-14. 
 
  Wash himself; these regulations were designed to promote cleanliness and a conviction of the necessity of internal as well as external purity.

title: Deuteronomy 23:16
text: The oppression of servants, depriving them of their rights, or in any way injuring them, is forbidden by Jehovah.

title: Deuteronomy 23:18
text:
The hire; the wages of iniquity must not be offered to the Lord, as was done by the heathen. 
 
  A dog; a male prostitute, a sodomite. 
 
The gains and the practices of iniquity are an abomination to the Lord; and no offerings are acceptable to him but those of honest, upright, believing, and affectionate hearts.

title: Deuteronomy 23:19
text: Usury; interest.  This was designed to inculcate and increase the habit of assisting and doing good to one another as the people of God.

title: Deuteronomy 23:20
text: Proper compensation for the use of money or any other property is not in itself wrong; but we should kindly assist the poor, and as we have opportunity and ability do good to all, especially to the friends of God and those who will use our kindness in honoring him.

title: Deuteronomy 23:23
text: What we promise, if it is not wicked or impracticable, we should be very careful to do: it is better not to promise, than to promise and not perform.

title: Deuteronomy 23:24
text:
Eat grapes thy fill; enough to satisfy present want. 
 
  Not put any in thy vessel; to carry it away.

title: Deuteronomy 23:25
text: Corn; grain.   Matthew 12:1-2

title: Deuteronomy 24:1
text:
vv 1-4. 
 
  Send her out of his house; this was not a command, and it was a practice contrary to the original institution of marriage.  God always abhorred it.  But on account of the wickedness and hardness of their hearts it was for a time suffered, and regulations were adopted to lessen its evils.   Malachi 2:14-16 Matthew 5:31-32 Matthew 19:3-9 Mark 10:2-12  
 
God, as civil ruler among the Jews, suffered, and in his providential government he now suffers some things which are contrary to his moral law, which it is wicked for men to do, and which, if they do, will draw down upon them his curse.

title: Deuteronomy 24:5
text:
Free a home one year; this was suited to increase and render more permanent conjugal affection, and thus render the family state more useful and happy. 
 
Great care should be taken not to interrupt or weaken affection between man and wife, but it should by all proper means be cherished and perpetuated.   Ephesians 5:25-33

title: Deuteronomy 24:6
text:
Nether; lower. 
 
  A man's life; that which was needful to prepare his food, and thus enable him to live.  Each family then had a mill in their house, and ground their grain by hand.   Exodus 11:5 Matthew 24:41  
 
Nothing should be taken from a poor man for debt which is needful to his subsistence.

title: Deuteronomy 24:7
text: That thief shall die; he that stole an ox was to restore double, but he that stole a man was to die; so much more wicked was it to steal a man than an ox.   Exodus 21:16 Exodus 22:4

title: Deuteronomy 24:8
text: As I commanded;  Leviticus 14:1

title: Deuteronomy 24:10
text: Not go into his house; this was designed to protect the poor debtor against the violence of the creditor.

title: Deuteronomy 24:12
text: Not sleep with his pledge; it might be some covering which at night the poor man would need.

title: Deuteronomy 24:13
text: It shall be righteousness; doing what would be right; and when done with right motives, accepted of God.

title: Deuteronomy 24:15
text:
At his day; at the close of his day's service, or the time he had agreed to work. 
 
The oppression of the poor, and withholding from hired laborers what is due to them, is an aggravated offence not only against them, but against God.

title: Deuteronomy 24:16
text:
Every man; who commits crimes for which death is the prescribed penalty. 
 
No criminal should be punished except for his own sins.

title: Deuteronomy 24:18
text:
Do this thing; refrain from wronging the laborer, the stranger, the widow, or the fatherless. 
 
The kindness of God to us should lead us to be kind to others, especially to the poor, the stranger, the widow, and the fatherless.

title: Deuteronomy 24:20
text: It; what is left on the trees.

title: Deuteronomy 25:1
text: The acquitting of the guilty, and the condemning of the innocent, are both an abomination to the Lord.

title: Deuteronomy 25:4
text:
Muzzle the ox; to prevent his eating.  The usual way of threshing grain at that time, was treading it out with oxen. 
 
The withholding of needful support and comfort even from oxen, is a sin against God; much more is the withholding of them from servants and other human beings who labor for our good, and especially from those who labor for our spiritual good.   I Corinthians 9:9-11 I Timothy 5:17-18

title: Deuteronomy 25:6
text: Succeed--his brother; to his inheritance, and to his name in the genealogical records.

title: Deuteronomy 25:10
text:
Hath his shoe loosed; a sign of disgrace in view of the people. 
 
Various regulations were adopted by God to make the Israelites a peculiar people, and keep them separate from other nations.  These regulations were binding on them till the introduction of the gospel dispensation, when they were abolished, and the Jews freed from all obligations to observe them.

title: Deuteronomy 25:13
text: A great and a small; so as to get more than just weight when he bought, and give less when he sold.

title: Deuteronomy 25:16
text: Strict honesty in buying and selling, and a sacred regard to what is just and right in all our dealings with men, are essential to acceptance with God.

title: Deuteronomy 25:17
text: What Amalek did;  Exodus 17:8 Numbers 24:1

title: Deuteronomy 25:18
text: Taking advantage of those who are in distress, and wronging such as have not power to protect themselves, is mean and wicked.  Those who do it incur the wrath of God, and may expect to be visited with his curse.

title: Deuteronomy 25:19
text: Shall blot out the remembrance; utterly destroy them.  I Samuel 15:1-3

title: Deuteronomy 26:2
text: The place which the Lord thy God shall choose; as the place of his worship, and of the visible manifestation of his presence.

title: Deuteronomy 26:3
text: However long the fulfilment of divine promises may be delayed, and however great the obstacles, they will in due time all be accomplished.

title: Deuteronomy 26:5
text: A Syrian ready to perish; or, a wandering Syrian, in reference to the nomade life of Jacob.  In a wider sense Mesopotamia, the birthplace of Abraham, was reckoned to Syria, so that Jacob was of Syrian descent, in respect to his fathers Abraham and Isaac, as well as his mother Rebecca.

title: Deuteronomy 26:7
text: Those who are oppressed, and with humble, believing, and affectionate hearts, seek help from God, may expect that in due time he will deliver them.

title: Deuteronomy 26:10
text: As God is the author of all our blessings, we should as such acknowledge him; and should honor him with our substance and with the first-fruits of all our increase.   Proverbs 3:9

title: Deuteronomy 26:12
text: The year of tithing; this was the second tithing, or the tithing of the remaining nine parts, after one tenth had been given to the Levites.  Every third year this second tithing was to be given to the poor.   Deuteronomy 14:22-29

title: Deuteronomy 26:13
text: The hallowed things; those which God required to be set apart for the Levites, for the poor, and for religious purposes.

title: Deuteronomy 26:14
text:
Thereof; of the hallowed things,  Deuteronomy 26:13 . 
 
  In my mourning; which was unlawful, as the food of mourners was regarded as unclean.   Hosea 9:4  
 
  For the dead; for funeral feasts, a use to which it was unlawful to put these hallowed things.  There is probably an allusion here to a heathenish custom. 
 
Obedience to the commands of God is a good preparation for seeking his favor with acceptance, and receiving his blessing on all our enjoyments.   Nehemiah 5:19 Nehemiah 13:7-31

title: Deuteronomy 26:16
text: As God gives to men, heart, soul, mind, strength, and all mercies, it is reasonable that they should be devoted to his service.

title: Deuteronomy 26:17
text: Avouched; affirmed, declared.

title: Deuteronomy 26:19
text: Devotion to God, is the way to be truly great, noble, excellent, useful, and happy.

title: Deuteronomy 27:3
text:
The words of this law; supposed to be the law or declaration which follows,  Deuteronomy 27:14-26 . 
 
All proper methods should be adopted to make the law of God familiar to all the people, and to set before them the motives which God has revealed to induce them to keep it.

title: Deuteronomy 27:4
text: Ebal;  Genesis 12:1

title: Deuteronomy 27:10
text: Whenever God makes any his peculiar people, he lays them under special obligations to obey him; and if they do not, they incur peculiar guilt and expose themselves to an aggravated punishment.   Deuteronomy 28:14-68

title: Deuteronomy 27:12
text:
Gerizim;  Genesis 12:1 
  Bless the people; add their Amen, in token of their concurrence, when the Levites should pronounce blessings on the obedient.

title: Deuteronomy 27:13
text: To curse; add their Amen when the Levites should pronounce curses on the disobedient.   Deuteronomy 27:14-26

title: Deuteronomy 27:15
text:
Graven or molten image; for the purpose of worshipping it.  Exodus 20:4-6  
 
By adding their solemn Amen to what is uttered, people profess to believe its truth.  If it is a curse, they acknowledge its justice; and if a blessing, their desire to receive it.

title: Deuteronomy 27:16
text: Setteth light; disregards and dishonors.   Exodus 20:12

title: Deuteronomy 27:17
text: Landmark;  Deuteronomy 19:1

title: Deuteronomy 27:19
text: Perverteth the judgment of; commits injustice towards those mentioned.

title: Deuteronomy 27:26
text: All the revelations and declarations of God are suited to deter men from transgression, and persuade them to obedience, showing that he has no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but great pleasure in their turning from their wickedness, that they may live.  Deuteronomy 28:1-68 Ezekiel 33:11 Luke 15:10

title: Deuteronomy 28:2
text:
These blessings; the blessings enumerated in  Deuteronomy 28:3-14 . 
 
No tongue can express nor finite mind conceive the number, greatness, variety, richness, or duration of the blessings which flow from obeying God.

title: Deuteronomy 28:7
text: Seven; used for many.

title: Deuteronomy 28:10
text: Called; Jehovah's people.

title: Deuteronomy 28:15
text: The miseries comprehended in the curses which flow from continued disobedience to God, as much surpass all finite conception as the blessings which flow from his favor.

title: Deuteronomy 28:23
text: Be brass, and--iron; the heaven would not give any more rain than if it were brass, nor the earth yield any more fruit than if it were iron.

title: Deuteronomy 28:24
text: As all the elements are under the control of God, he can at any time arm them against his foes, and pursue them with wrath till they perish.

title: Deuteronomy 28:26
text:
Thy carcass shall be meat; many of their dead bodies would be left unburied. 
 
  Fray; frighten, scare.

title: Deuteronomy 28:27
text: Botch; painful ulcers.   Deuteronomy 28:35

title: Deuteronomy 28:28
text: Diseases of body and mind are God's servants.  They go and come at his bidding, and fasten their deadly fangs on such as he commissions them to torment and destroy.

title: Deuteronomy 28:32
text:
No might; no power to escape the evils or to prevent them. 
 
Few calamities are more dreadful than to see the misery of children and be unable to help them.

title: Deuteronomy 28:40
text: Cast his fruit; it would drop off unripe.

title: Deuteronomy 28:42
text: Thy trees; their leaves.

title: Deuteronomy 28:45
text: What renders calamities vastly more dreadful is, a conviction that we by our own wickedness have occasioned them.

title: Deuteronomy 28:46
text: For ever; so long as they should continue as a people to transgress his commands.

title: Deuteronomy 28:48
text: A yoke of iron; afflict them with grievous bondage.

title: Deuteronomy 28:49
text: Swift as the eagle; rapid in their conquests.

title: Deuteronomy 28:57
text: The horrors of famine can be but faintly conceived; and if the sufferings occasioned by sin are so great in this world, what must thy be in the world to come?

title: Deuteronomy 28:63
text: Plucked from off the land; they were by the Romans carried off from their land and scattered among all nations; and were forbidden again to come within sight of Jerusalem.

title: Deuteronomy 28:67
text: The history of the Jews for more than eighteen hundred years demonstrates the truth of the predictions contained in this chapter, and conclusively proves that in uttering them Moses spoke by the direction, and under the guidance of the Holy Ghost.

title: Deuteronomy 28:68
text: Ye shall be sold--and no man shall buy you; many were sold into perpetual bondage, and many more were offered for sale for whom their conquerors could not find a market, so great were their numbers; and multitudes were slain or left to perish.

title: Deuteronomy 29:1
text:
The covenant; the declarations of God with regard to the duty of the Israelites, his blessings on the obedient, and his curses on the disobedient. 
 
  In Horeb;  Exodus 19:3-5

title: Deuteronomy 29:2
text: Ye have seen; many of the older ones had seen, and the rest had heard.

title: Deuteronomy 29:4
text:
To perceive; the spiritual beauty, excellence, and glory of God, and the supreme blessedness of loving, believing, and obeying him. This perception no one has without receiving it from God.  The great body of the Israelites did not feel their need of this, did not seek it, nor desire it, nor obtain it.  They rebelled against God, and nearly all who when they came out of Egypt were over twenty years old, died in the wilderness. 
 
So long as men continue to neglect what they know to be right and do what they know to be wrong, God will not give them hearts to perceive his spiritual glory, or to enjoy his infinite love.

title: Deuteronomy 29:5
text: Your clothes--thy shoe; these God so provided and preserved as to keep them from want.

title: Deuteronomy 29:6
text: Not eaten bread, neither--drunk wine; they lived on manna, and drank water from the rock.

title: Deuteronomy 29:9
text: A faithful survey of the past dealings of God with us and our friends, is well adapted to lead us to do his will, and thus to secure all needed good.

title: Deuteronomy 29:12
text:
Enter into covenant; by engaging to obey him; on the fulfilment of which engagements he promised to bless them. 
 
The course taken by parents deeply affects their children for both worlds, and may be a means of their salvation or of their destruction.

title: Deuteronomy 29:14
text: Neither with you only; God made this covenant not only with them, but with their posterity and with all who should obey him.  Hebrews 6:13-20

title: Deuteronomy 29:18
text:
Gall and wormwood; bitter and poisonous plants, here representing the effects of sinful practices. 
 
Apostasies from God begin in the heart; and in order to escape destruction, men must with all diligence keep their hearts in the love of God, with them believe unto righteousness, and from them make profession of their faith and love to salvation.

title: Deuteronomy 29:19
text: For a man to think that he shall be happy in a course of sinning, or can continue in it and escape destruction, is one of the surest ways to ruin.

title: Deuteronomy 29:20
text: Blot out his name; destroy him.

title: Deuteronomy 29:22
text: That land; the land of Canaan.

title: Deuteronomy 29:23
text:
Brimstone, and salt; utterly barren. 
 
The past and present state of Palestine, as well as of the Jews its ancient inhabitants, is a fulfilment of the word of God by Moses, uttered and recorded more than three thousand years ago; and a proof that none of his declarations will fail, but all in due time come to pass.

title: Deuteronomy 29:24
text: This great anger; of God against Canaan, in turning it from fertility to barrenness, and visiting its inhabitants with such awful calamities.

title: Deuteronomy 29:26
text: Whom he had not given; who had not done and could not do any thing for them.

title: Deuteronomy 29:28
text: Men of various nations, characters, and countries now say, concerning the Jews and the land of Canaan, what Moses here predicted that they would say; and thus show that he was inspired by Him who sees the end from the beginning, and can describe things thousands of years before, with as much accuracy as after they have taken place.

title: Deuteronomy 29:29
text:
Secret things; things not revealed, and which we do not and need not know. 
 
  Things--revealed; those which God makes known, or has given us the means of knowing, and which we need to know. 
 
God gives us the means of knowing all that we need to know; and for us to strive or wish to know what we cannot, ought not, and need not know, is foolish, hurtful, and wicked.  The more content we are without such knowledge the better; while by the revelation of God, to know him in such a manner as to love and obey him, is the whole of man's duty, excellence, blessedness, and glory.

title: Deuteronomy 30:1
text: These things; the things mentioned in the previous chapters.

title: Deuteronomy 30:3
text: However great or long continued the calamities which any suffer in this world on account of their sins, if they think upon their ways, repent, and turn heartily to the Lord, he will forgive them and bestow upon them freely, for Christ's sake rich and lasting blessings.  Proverbs 1:23 Isaiah 55:7

title: Deuteronomy 30:6
text:
Circumcise thy heart; turn it from the love and practice of sin to the love and practice of holiness. 
 
  Mayest live; live a life of holiness and prosperity on earth, and of blessedness and glory in heaven.   Romans 2:29 Colossians 2:11-13  
 
vv 6-10 
 
When men turn heartily to the Lord, it is because he by his Spirit turns them.   Jeremiah 52:34   Of the necessity of this turning, circumcision under the Old Testament was a sign.  Hence the reason why to love the Lord and to keep his commandments is spoken of as the circumcision of the heart.   Deuteronomy 30:6 Romans 2:28-29

title: Deuteronomy 30:11
text: It is not hidden--neither is it far off; not difficult, but easy to be understood.  What was wanted was humble, docile, obedient, and affectionate hearts.   Romans 10:6-11 II Timothy 3:14-17

title: Deuteronomy 30:14
text: The way of salvation revealed in the Old Testament is the same as that revealed in the New.  Hence Paul, in describing it, employed the language used by Moses, and to persuade men to embrace it, reasoned with them out of the Old Testament scriptures.

title: Deuteronomy 30:15
text:
Life and good; temporal and eternal, to be obtained as the gracious gift of God, by obeying him. 
 
  Death and evil; which they would bring upon themselves by disobeying him.   Deuteronomy 30:16-18

title: Deuteronomy 30:19
text:
Choose life; by choosing to obey God, and thus obtain it.  Deuteronomy 30:20  
 
To be saved, men must choose to obey God; and what is most efficacious in leading them to do this, will do the most towards their salvation.  Joshua 24:15 Proverbs 1:29

title: Deuteronomy 31:2
text:
Go out and come in; perform the duties of leader of Israel. 
 
As the limit of human life is set, the aged, even if they enjoy good health, must soon die; this they should feel, and endeavor so to live as to be prepared at any time to leave this world and enter heaven.

title: Deuteronomy 31:3
text: He will go over; in his visible presence on the mercy-seat.  Deuteronomy 31:8

title: Deuteronomy 31:5
text: In destroying the Canaanites and taking possession of their country, the Israelites were only doing what God commanded them.  Their example gives no authority to any nation to destroy another, take their country, or make war upon them, without a command from God.

title: Deuteronomy 31:8
text: With the presence and favor of God men may safely and properly undertake any service, however difficult, dangerous, or trying, to which he calls them.

title: Deuteronomy 31:9
text: This law; according to some, the book of Deuteronomy.  But there seems to be no valid ground for thus limiting the words.  Better, the whole law.  See note,  Deuteronomy 17:18 .

title: Deuteronomy 31:13
text:
Not known any thing; not witnessed what God had done for his people. 
 
The laws of God should be made known and be often inculcated upon all the people, young and old, rich and poor, bond and free, that all may understand them, and the reasons for obeying them which he has revealed.

title: Deuteronomy 31:17
text: Hide my face; withdraw tokens of favor.

title: Deuteronomy 31:18
text: God is perfectly acquainted with all the sins which any will ever commit; and their iniquities alone lead him ever to withdraw from them the manifestations of his favor.

title: Deuteronomy 31:19
text: This song; as in the following chapter.

title: Deuteronomy 31:21
text: Prosperity often leads men to forget God, turn from him, and draw down upon themselves his desolating judgments.  But their own consciences will testify against them, and if they turn not to him will mar their enjoyments and ere long make them wretched.

title: Deuteronomy 31:26
text: For a witness against thee; when they should rebel against God.

title: Deuteronomy 31:29
text: A good man knows that no trust can safely be placed in the human heart; that without the constant keeping of God, however great its mercies or trials, it will show itself to be deceitful above all things and desperately wicked; and that there is no hope for the cause of God and holiness on earth but in the riches of his grace.

title: Deuteronomy 32:1
text:
Give ear--hear; this mode of address was designed to awaken attention, and impress on the hearers the importance of the subject. 
 
The instructions of God through his inspired servants, as recorded in the Scriptures, are worthy of universal attention.

title: Deuteronomy 32:2
text:
Drop as the rain; be copious and refreshing. 
 
  Distil as the dew; be gentle, penetrating, and efficacious. 
 
As the rain and the dew, so the truths of the Bible are perfectly adapted to produce their appropriate effects.   Isaiah 55:10-13

title: Deuteronomy 32:3
text:
Publish the name; proclaim those perfections by the manifestation of which God makes himself known. 
 
  Ascribe ye greatness unto our God; treat him according to his true character.

title: Deuteronomy 32:4
text:
The Rock; this is the first time God is called a rock, in the Bible.  It expresses his durable and unchanging perfection, and the safety of trusting in him and reposing on him our hopes for eternity.  Deuteronomy 32:15 Deuteronomy 32:18 Psalms 31:2-3 Matthew 7:24-25 Matthew 16:18  
 
  Judgment; just and right. 
 
Nothing could be added to or taken from the character of God, which would make it more perfect; and no change in his dealings could make them in any respect better.

title: Deuteronomy 32:5
text:
Not the spot of his children; do not possess their character, nor appear as his people. 
 
Men are the authors of all their own wickedness, and they are wholly to blame for it.  The more they have of it the more unlike they are to God, and the more guilty in his sight.

title: Deuteronomy 32:6
text:
Requite; repay, recompense. 
 
  Thy father; one who treated them as children. 
 
  Bought thee; by delivering them from Egyptian bondage. 
 
  Made thee; made them a great people. 
 
  Established thee; as an independent nation, with a regular and good government. 
 
To live in sin, after all that God has done to deliver us from it, is the vilest and basest ingratitude, and exposees to the most fearful retribution.

title: Deuteronomy 32:7
text: Remember the days of old; what God has done for your ancestors, and through them, for you.

title: Deuteronomy 32:8
text:
He set the bounds of the people; so ordered events in his providence, when he divided the earth among the nations, that the Canaanites, who for their sins were to be destroyed, should inherit the land that was to be possessed by the Israelites; and thus prepare for them houses, cities, cultivated fields, and all needful things. 
 
  According to the number of the children of Israel; a land just large and good enough for the best accommodation of the twelve tribes of Israel.   Genesis 10:32 Genesis 11:9  
 
The consideration that God thought kindly and graciously of us before we were born, and so ordered things that our wants of body and soul may all be supplied, is suited to impress our obligation to love and serve him, and to show our utter inexcusableness and great guilt if we neglect it.

title: Deuteronomy 32:9
text:
The Lord's portion; those whom he set apart especially for himself, treated as his peculiar treasure, and from whom he might rightfully expect a special revenue of glory. 
 
  Jacob; who represents his descendants.

title: Deuteronomy 32:10
text:
He found him in a desert land; he went, as it were, to look after his people in the wilderness, found them there, entered into covenant with them, and consecrated them as his people.   Deuteronomy 8:11-18  
 
  Led him about;  Numbers 33:3-36:13

title: Deuteronomy 32:11
text:
Stirreth up her nest; that is, her young brood, exciting them to fly. 
 
  Fluttereth over her young; in cherishing and defending them. 
 
  Spreadeth abroad her wings; to protect her young, assist them in flying, and if need be carry them, as a parent would a feeble or weary child. 
 
God takes a variety of ways to influence men to work out their own salvation, and renders their efforts effectual to their mounting up on wings as eagles, going from strength to strength and holding on their way, till in heaven they stand, trophies of grace, perfect before God, to his infinite and everlasting joy.  So should parents and ministers do, with regard to the young; and if in this they imitate the divine example, or are as true to parental instinct as the eagle, they may hope that the objects of their affection will much oftener fly upward towards heaven, and not downward towards hell.   Deuteronomy 6:7 Proverbs 22:6

title: Deuteronomy 32:12
text:
So the Lord; excited his people to leave their bondage in Egypt, and protected and assisted them on their on their way to the promised land. 
 
  No strange god with him; none had assisted the Israelites or bestowed upon them any blessings except Jehovah. 
 
The tenderness of God to his people, his unceasing care for them, and the variety and wisdom of the methods he takes to lead them to himself, demand their gratitude and renewed devotion to his service.

title: Deuteronomy 32:13
text:
Ride on the high places; expressive of their prosperity. 
 
  Honey out of the rock, and oil; from the most rocky parts of the country, where these things would abound.

title: Deuteronomy 32:14
text:
The breed of Bashan; in Bashan was found excellent pasturage, and its cattle and flocks were celebrated for their strength and fatness. 
 
  Fat of kidneys of wheat; a figurative description of wheat whose kernels are plump and of a fine quality.

title: Deuteronomy 32:15
text:
Jeshurun; that is, Israel; a term of endearment, meaning upright. 
 
The facts that increasing prosperity so often occasions increasing wickedness, and that the more outward blessings God bestows upon a people the more they forget him and become worldly, proud, sensual, and devilish, are conclusive proofs of the awful wickedness of the human heart.   Deuteronomy 32:17-18

title: Deuteronomy 32:16
text: Provoked him to jealousy; greatly offended him.

title: Deuteronomy 32:19
text:
The provoking; the provocation which his rebellious children gave him. 
 
  His sons, and--his daughters; by birth and privileges.  Yet they rebelled against him.   Isaiah 1:2-4  
 
For those who have experienced most of God's goodness, and especially for his redeemed people to rebel against him, is peculiarly wicked, and he will pursue them with his indignation till they repent or perish.

title: Deuteronomy 32:21
text:
That which is not God; that is, by the worship of idols. 
 
  Vanities; a common term for the heathen gods, which are nothing, and which disappoint the hopes of those who trust in them. 
 
  Those which are not a people--a foolish nation; these words describe the heathen nations as being ignorant of God and having no covenant with him, and thus not deserving the name of peoples.  Since God's people have provoked him to anger by worshipping the gods of the heathen, he will provoke them to anger by taking away their privileges, and giving them to the heathen.  This he has done, first, by setting heathen rulers over them, as the Babyonians and Romans; secondly, by bringing the Gentiles into their place as his peculiar people.  Romans 10:19 Romans 11:11-36

title: Deuteronomy 32:22
text: A fire is kindled--set on fire the foundations of the mountains; a figurative description of the awful effect of God's wrath, which nothing can withstand, and which follows the sinner to the eternal world.

title: Deuteronomy 32:27
text:
The wrath of the enemy; the anger of the enemies of Israel manifesting itself in blasphemous reproaches against the God of Israel. They would ascribe the destruction of Israel to the weakness of Jehovah and to their own strength.  God fears not the power of the enemy to injure his people, but is concerned for the honor of his own name. Compare  Exodus 32:12 Numbers 14:13-16 Deuteronomy 9:28 II Samuel 1:20 .  From regard to his own glory, in which the highest welfare of his church is involved, he will not utterly destroy his ancient covenant people, but will keep them, as he is now doing, distinct, with a view, when they shall repent and turn to him, of bringing them again into his church and adopting them, with all believing Gentiles, as his people. 
 
  Our hand is high; our high, strong hand, and not Jehovah, hath done this.

title: Deuteronomy 32:28
text: Void of counsel; they did not so understand their true interests as to take the way to secure them, but took that which ruined them.  Matthew 27:25 Luke 13:34-35

title: Deuteronomy 32:29
text:
Consider their latter end; in such a manner as to shun the course that will make it wretched, and take the course that will make it blessed.   Deuteronomy 30:19  
 
God desires that men should consider what will be the end of their continuing in sin, and that they should turn from it and live.  Ezekiel 33:11 Matthew 23:37

title: Deuteronomy 32:30
text: One chase a thousand; one of the enemies of Israel put to flight a thousand Israelites.  Had they remained obedient to God, the opposite of this would have been true.  Compare  Deuteronomy 28:7 Leviticus 26:8 Joshua 23:10  with  Deuteronomy 28:25 Leviticus 26:36-37 .

title: Deuteronomy 32:31
text: Their rock; the gods of the heathen.

title: Deuteronomy 32:32
text:
vv 32-33. 
 
  Their vine--their grapes--their clusters--their wine; all their works, proceeding from their wicked hearts, are corrupt; as if the vine should bear only poisonous and bitter fruit, and the wine that comes from its clusters should be filled with deadly venom.  There seems to be an allusion here to certain fruits growing on the borders of the Dead sea, which are without fair to the eye, but within empty and worthless, yielding no food that can be eaten.

title: Deuteronomy 32:34
text: This; the Lord's indignation against their sins, and his purpose to punish them.

title: Deuteronomy 32:36
text:
Judge his people, and repent himself for his servants; turn from his fierce anger, and be merciful to them. 
 
  When he seeth; when God sees their helplessness, and they repent of their sins and turn to him.

title: Deuteronomy 32:37
text: Their gods; false gods, in whom they had trusted.

title: Deuteronomy 32:38
text:
Eat the fat of their sacrifices; idols to whom they had sacrificed. 
 
  Let them rise; if they can; but they cannot, and there is no help but in Jehovah.

title: Deuteronomy 32:42
text: From the beginning of revenges upon the enemy; rather, from the head of the leaders of the enemy.

title: Deuteronomy 32:43
text:
With his people; in their repentance and deliverance from their oppressors, and in their restoration again in due time to the privileges of his chosen and redeemed people.  Zechariah 12:10 Romans 11:15  Others prefer to render, Rejoice, ye nations who are his people. 
 
The mercy of God to those who repent, and the good which he bestows upon them, ought to occasion universal joy, and will give joy to all the good throughout the universe.

title: Deuteronomy 32:44
text: Instruction conveyed in poetry is often more impressive, more easily remembered, and more extensively useful, than when conveyed in prose. God has therefore manifested his wisdom and kindness in using it so much in the Bible.

title: Deuteronomy 32:46
text: To be benefited by God's ocmmunications, men must attend to them, treasure them up in their memories, and apply them to the regulation of their feelings, thoughts, words, and actions.

title: Deuteronomy 32:47
text:
Your life; that on which their continuance and prosperity would depend. 
 
On the manner in which men treat the commands of God, and the book which contains them, depends their best good and that of their children, for this life and the life to come.

title: Deuteronomy 32:49
text: Abarim;

title: Deuteronomy 32:50
text:
In mount Hor;  Numbers 20:22-29:1 
 
Death is always the fruit of sin.  By one man sin entered, and death by sin.  But to those who forsake sin and serve God, he turns it into a blessing.  Often, as death approaches, the land of promise, the heavenly city, opens before them with a beauty, a grandeur, a glory which surpass all conception.  Earth and its glories they joyfully relinquish, though to live on it were Christ; because to die and be with Christ, like Christ perfectly and for ever, is unspeakable gain.  Philippians 1:21 I John 3:2

title: Deuteronomy 32:51
text: Meribah-Kadesh;

title: Deuteronomy 33:1
text: Ministers of God delight in proclaiming the blessings which will come on his people; and though in faithfulness they must point out the destruction that will come on the wicked, they do it with earnest desires that they may turn from their wicked ways and live.

title: Deuteronomy 33:2
text:
Came from Sinai--Seir--Paran; these mountains in and around the Arabian desert are here taken collectively, as the place whence God manifested himself in a special manner, first to Moses, and afterwards to the whole people. 
 
  Saints; his ministering angels are meant.   Psalms 68:17 Acts 7:53   Galatians 3:19   We may render more literally, He came from the myriads of his holy ones; that is, from his secret dwelling-place, where he is surrounded by myriads of angels.

title: Deuteronomy 33:3
text: All his saints; all the holy ones of Israel his people.

title: Deuteronomy 33:4
text: Even the inheritance; the law is itself the inheritance of God's covenant people.

title: Deuteronomy 33:6
text: Reuben; his posterity; the tribe of Reuben, which had an ample and fertile territory on the east of the Jordan.  Simeon is passed over in silence.

title: Deuteronomy 33:7
text:
Bring him unto his people; bring him home safe from his conflicts with his enemies. 
 
  Be sufficient for him; or, as some render, strive for him; that is, let his hands, strengthened by thee, fight his battles successfully. 
 
Those who have God for their helper will at last triumph over all their foes.

title: Deuteronomy 33:8
text:
With thy holy one; the high-priest is meant, who bore the Urim and Thummim, and was of the tribe of Levi. 
 
  Massah--Meribah;  Exodus 17:7

title: Deuteronomy 33:9
text: Not seen--acknowledge--nor knew his own children; he did not spare his own relatives, or favor any who were guilty, but executed divine justice upon them.   Exodus 32:26-29

title: Deuteronomy 33:12
text:
By him; the Lord.  Jerusalem was in the tribe of Benjamin. 
 
  Between his shoulders; as a father bears a child upon his shoulders.  God would be near him and protect him. 
 
It is a great blessing to enjoy religious privileges, and dwell near the house of the Lord; and those who delight in worshipping him on earth are preparing for the worship of heaven.

title: Deuteronomy 33:13
text: The deep that coucheth beneath; the subterranean waters, which break forth in springs.

title: Deuteronomy 33:14
text: By the sun, and--the moon; their influence in ripening the products of the earth.

title: Deuteronomy 33:16
text: Him that dwelt in the bush;  Exodus 3:2-6:1

title: Deuteronomy 33:17
text:
Horns of unicorns; see note on  Numbers 23:22 . 
 
  Ephraim, and--Manasseh; the two tribes which descended from Joseph. Thus he foretells to Ephraim a more numerous posterity than to Manasseh.   Genesis 48:1 Genesis 48:17-19  
 
The fidelity of parents is often followed by rich and lasting blessings on their children.

title: Deuteronomy 33:18
text:
In thy going out; for traffic.   Genesis 49:13   Zebulun would be a commercial and enterprising tribe. 
 
  In thy tents; abiding in quietness at home.

title: Deuteronomy 33:19
text:
Treasures hid in the sand; or, hid treasures of the sand.  The sand here represents the seashore, and then, generally, the wealth that comes to it through commerce. 
 
Sacrifices of righteousness offered in love to God, will be rewarded with all needed abundance on earth, and with endless and inexhaustible treasures in heaven.

title: Deuteronomy 33:21
text:
The first part for himself; in the country which the Israelites first conquered, on the east of Jordan. 
 
  A portion of the lawgiver; that which Moses, their lawgiver, assigned to them. 
 
  He came with the heads of the people; went over Jordan with the rest of the Israelites and assisted them in the conquest of Canaan. 
 
In executing just punishments on the wicked, when called to it by God, men may be acceptably serving him and securing his blessings.

title: Deuteronomy 33:22
text: Leap from Bashan; Bashan was a country east of Jordan, between the mountains of Hermon and Gilead. From this country the Danites made successful warlike excursions.   Joshua 19:47 Judges 18:27-29

title: Deuteronomy 33:23
text:
West and--south; west and south of that which was conquered by the Danites. 
 
For all temporal as well as spiritual favors, men are dependent on the blessing of the Lord.

title: Deuteronomy 33:25
text:
Thy shoes; or, thy bars. 
 
  Iron and brass; invincible to the power of the enemy. 
 
  As thy days, so shall thy strength be; thy strength shall endure as long as thy days.  Some render, As thy days, so shall thy quietness be. 
 
The Lord communicates to those who trust in him, all which they need to secure in the end their highest good.

title: Deuteronomy 33:27
text:
The enemy; the Canaanites. 
 
To have God for our refuge is the best security from fear, and the safest protection from danger.

title: Deuteronomy 33:28
text: Alone; not incorporated with other nations.

title: Deuteronomy 33:29
text: Be found liars unto thee; rather, shall crouch to thee from fear; shall be forced to submit themselves to thee.

title: Deuteronomy 34:1
text:
Dan; this was in the north part of the country.   Judges 18:29  
 
However long or faithfully the people of God may serve him, they must die.  As they approach that momentous and solemn event, the Lord can, and sometimes does give them such views of the glorious things which he has promised, as not only to take away fear, but to lead them in peace and with delight to yield up their spirit to Him who gave it.

title: Deuteronomy 34:2
text: Utmost sea; the Mediterranean, forming the western boundary.

title: Deuteronomy 34:3
text: Zoar; near the southern boundary of Canaan.

title: Deuteronomy 34:5
text: Though it is ordinarily a blessing, when called to die, to be surrounded with kind, sympathizing friends, yet if we die among strangers, or even alone, with no kind hand to smooth a pillow or wipe away a tear, God can so manifest himself, that without aid from creatures we shall be filled to overflowing with the fulness of God.

title: Deuteronomy 34:6
text: Beth-peor;  Deuteronomy 3:1

title: Deuteronomy 34:8
text: When friends, especially such as have been eminently useful, die, it is proper to mourn; but it should be with cheerful acquiescence in the will of God, deep loathing of sin the cause of death, and earnest prayer that all the living may be so saved from its power, that when absent from the body they shall be present with the Lord.

title: Deuteronomy 34:9
text:
Laid his hands upon him;   
 
God is not dependent for the accomplishment of his work on any of his servants, but they are constantly and entirely dependent on him.  He raises up one, fits him for his work, sustains him till it is accomplished, and then, in his own way and time, removes him.  With equal ease he can raise up others and fit them for what remains to be done, so tha not one jot or tittle of what he has promised shall fail, till all be accomplished.

title: Deuteronomy 34:10
text:
Knew face to face; conversed familiarly with him, as a man with his friend. 
 
Moses was an example of true greatness.  The more we imitate him in meekness, humility, faith in God, courage, and perseverance in duty, the more free will be our access to God, and the greater our likeness to him; the more useful and blessed will be our life, the richer our prospect in death, and the more glorious our condition and inheritance in eternity.

title: Joshua 1:1
text: Minister; assistant, agent.

title: Joshua 1:2
text: When the servants of God die and enter into rest, those who survive should be aroused to increasing efforts to carry forward the good works which they had begun.

title: Joshua 1:4
text:
The wilderness; of Zin, on the south. 
 
  Lebanon; on the north. 
 
  Euphrates; on the east. 
 
  The great sea; the Mediterranean, on the west.

title: Joshua 1:7
text: The highest and noblest courage is shown by the most faithful discharge of duty, and no real coward makes it his great object to obey the known will of God.

title: Joshua 1:8
text:
This book of the law;  Deuteronomy 17:18-19 Deuteronomy 31:1 
 
The grand means of inspiring and increasong true courage, is daily attention to the principles and precepts of the Bible, for the purpose of understanding and obeying them.

title: Joshua 1:11
text: The certainty that God will bestow upon his people the blessings he has promised them, does not in the least lessen the necessity of their using all appointed means to obtain them.

title: Joshua 1:13
text: Remember the word;  Numbers 32:1-36:13

title: Joshua 1:18
text: Rebellion against rightful authority requiring what is right, is rebellion against God.

title: Joshua 2:1
text: Shittim; a place in the plains of Moab, a few miles east of the Jordan.   Numbers 25:1

title: Joshua 2:4
text:
vv 4-5. 
 
  Wist; knew. 
 
  Wot; know.

title: Joshua 2:6
text: The roof of the house; their roofs were flat, and were places often resorted to for air, meditation, and rest.   Deuteronomy 22:8

title: Joshua 2:7
text: The fords; where they expected that the spies would cross over Jordan.

title: Joshua 2:9
text: The providences of God, as well as his word, often terrify the wicked; yet those terrors which do not lead them to repentance will do them no good, but will be forerunners of their destruction.

title: Joshua 2:12
text: Kindness to the people of God, and assistance rendered to them for his sake, are well pleasing to him, and secure his blessing.  Matthew 10:41-42 Hebrews 11:31

title: Joshua 2:14
text:
Our life for yours; may God take our life if we do not save yours. 
 
We should be careful to promise only what is practicable and right; and when we make such promises, should conscientiously and faithfully fulfil them.

title: Joshua 2:15
text: She dwelt upon the wall; so that from her window she could let the men down outside of the city wall.

title: Joshua 2:17
text: We will be blameless; not under obligation to fulfil their engagement to her, unless she should do as they mentioned,  Joshua 2:18 .

title: Joshua 2:19
text: His blood shall be upon his head; his death will be his own fault.

title: Joshua 2:24
text: When God abandons a people on account of their sins, all things conspire to work out their ruin.

title: Joshua 3:1
text: They who are earnest, diligent, and persevering in the discharge of their appropriate duties, may expect to be rendered eminently useful, and advanced to distinguished honor and glory.   Joshua 3:7

title: Joshua 3:2
text: After three days; from the time mentioned in  Joshua 1:10-11 .

title: Joshua 3:3
text: To follow the directions of God as indicated by his word, his Spirit, and his providence, is the way of safety, happiness, and success.

title: Joshua 3:4
text: Two thousand cubits; about one thousand yards, or two thirds of a mile.

title: Joshua 3:5
text:
Sanctify yourselves;  Exodus 19:10-14  
 
Sanctification of body and spirit is a preparation for seeing the glory of God, and experiencing the manifestations of his power and grace.

title: Joshua 3:7
text: Magnify thee; show by miracle that he had appointed Joshua, and clothed him with authority as the leader of Israel.   Joshua 4:14

title: Joshua 3:10
text:
Hereby; by what he would do in dividing the waters of Jordan.  Joshua 3:16  
 
However dark the path before us, God can make it plain; and however great the difficulties in the way of duty, he can remove them, and cause us in obeying him to triumph.

title: Joshua 3:12
text: Twelve men; these were to be selected for a special purpose.  Joshua 4:2-3

title: Joshua 3:13
text:
Be cut off; the waters below would separate from the waters above, leaving the channel of the river dry.   Joshua 3:16  
 
Multitudes of things which are impossible with men are possible with God.  It is therefore reasonable and a duty to believe whatever he declares, and show that belief by our conduct.

title: Joshua 3:15
text: The time of harvest; the people crossed on the tenth of the first month Abib, or early in April.   Joshua 4:19   Then, as now, the harvest occurred during April and early in May, the barley preceding the wheat harvest by two or three weeks.

title: Joshua 3:16
text: Whatever difficulties may be in the way of believing God, living and strong faith will overcome them; and those who exercise it will in due time see the complete fulfilment of his declarations.

title: Joshua 4:3
text: All proper care should be taken to keep in mind the mercies of the Lord; and to transmit a knowledge of them to our children and all coming generations.

title: Joshua 4:4
text: Prepared; previously selected.   Joshua 3:12

title: Joshua 4:6
text:
A sign; a monument to commemorate the dividing of the river Jordan, and to transmit the knowledge of it to future generations.  Joshua 4:7  
 
It is wisely ordered that children should be inquisitive.  It opens the way to communicate instruction in a form most interesting and useful. Such opportunities should be diligently improved by parents and all intrusted with the education of the young.

title: Joshua 4:7
text: For ever; as long as the knowledge of this event should continue.

title: Joshua 4:10
text: When in obedience to God we have taken the place and engaged in the service which he has assigned us, we should patiently abide in it till he in his providence bids us leave it, and then we should go to any other place and engage in any other service to which he calls us.

title: Joshua 4:12
text: The friends of God should remember that they belong to one family, and have one common cause.  Most gladly, therefore, should each portion pursue the course which is best for the whole, and in so doing they will subserve their own best interests.

title: Joshua 4:14
text:
The Lord magnified Joshua; by the manner in which he led the Israelites over the Jordan.   Joshua 3:7  
 
They who most heartily and faithfully follow the directions of god, will in due time be most highly honored.   Matthew 19:28

title: Joshua 4:18
text: What are called laws of nature, are stated modes of God's operation, which he can continue or change, as he sees best.

title: Joshua 4:19
text: The tenth day of the first month; forty years, wanting five days, from the time they left Egypt, and on the day that the paschal lamb was to be set apart for sacrifice.   Joshua 5:10 Exodus 12:3-42

title: Joshua 4:20
text: Pitch; literally, rear up; that is, into a conspicuous heap.

title: Joshua 4:23
text: The Red sea;  Exodus 14:21-22:1

title: Joshua 4:24
text: When God words wonders, they are not for any particular people or period merely, but for all people in all ages, and are designed and adapted to make known his character to the universe for ever.

title: Joshua 5:1
text:
The sea; the Mediterranean. 
 
However much those who continue in sin may see of their own approaching ruin, they take no proper measures to escape it.

title: Joshua 5:2
text:
The second time; not that any who had been circumcised were to be circumcised again, but that the rite of circumcision, which had been neglected in the wilderness, was to be, as it were, established a second time as it had been the first time in Abraham's day. 
 
If under special and peculiar circumstances the ordinances of God have been for a time neglected, the earliest opportunity should be embraced to observe them, and thus to secure the benefits they are suited to impart.

title: Joshua 5:3
text: Whatever be the circumstances of men, it is safe, wise, and best for them to obey God.  He can protect them from all harm, or overrule what they may suffer for their highest good.

title: Joshua 5:6
text: By the dispensations of his providence, God fulfils the declarations of his word.

title: Joshua 5:8
text: Whole; healed.

title: Joshua 5:9
text:
The reproach of Egypt; according to some, the reproach of their having been bondmen in Egypt.  According to others, the reproach cast upon them by the Egyptians, as a race out of favor with God, and left by him to wander in the wilderness.  Compare  Exodus 32:12 Numbers 14:13-16   Deuteronomy 9:28 .  This reproach God had removed by receiving them again into covenant with himself by circumcision, and by giving them possession of the promised land. 
 
  Gilgal; that is, rolling away. 
 
Reproach may for a season rest upon the people of God, but in due time it shall be done away, and they shall be crowned with honor and glory.

title: Joshua 5:10
text: Fourteenth day; just forty years from the time of their keeping it on the evening before their departure from Egypt.   Exodus 12:6-14

title: Joshua 5:12
text: When one source of support ceases, God opens another, and instead of leaving his people destitute, he will abundantly supply them with all real good.

title: Joshua 5:13
text: A man; One in the form and appearance of a man.  He was that "Angel of the Lord" who showed himself to be the Lord himself.  Genesis 18:1-33

title: Joshua 5:14
text:
Captain;  Hebrews 2:1 
  Did worship;  Matthew 4:10 Revelation of John 19:1 
 
Jehovah, who took the form of man, is the Captain of salvation to his people.  Those whom he saves worship him on earth, and will for ever worship him in heaven.   Matthew 14:33 Acts 7:59 Revelation of John 5:8-14

title: Joshua 5:15
text: Loose thy shoe;  Exodus 3:5

title: Joshua 6:1
text: If men continue in known transgressions, they will bring themselves into difficulties and dangers from which they cannot escape.

title: Joshua 6:2
text: And the Lord said; this is a continuation of the narrative begun in  Joshua 5:13 ; the first verse of  Joshua 6:1  being thrown in simply by way of explanation.  "The Lord" here is the same as "the Captain of the host of the Lord,"  Joshua 5:14-15 .

title: Joshua 6:3
text: Shall compass the city; this is a sign of its being given by Jehovah into the power of Israel.  The number seven, here as elsewhere, denotes completeness.

title: Joshua 6:5
text: God gives success to his people in such a way as to try their faith, and to show them that their victories come not from themselves, but from him alone.

title: Joshua 6:8
text: Before the Lord; before the ark, the visible manifestation of his presence.

title: Joshua 6:9
text: The armed men; the Hebrew term used here being that which is repeatedly applied to the warriors of the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, some have thought that these warriors were designated as those who should go before the ark, the rest of the armed men following it.  It was only the men of war that compassed the city.  Joshua 6:3

title: Joshua 6:10
text: Silence is often conducive to that serious meditation and solemn reflection upon the character, works, and ways of God, which prepare his people to see his glory and experience his salvation.

title: Joshua 6:14
text: Careful attention to the directions of God, and patient perseverance in following them, whether we see any immediate effects or not, is the highest wisdom, and the surest way of securing success.

title: Joshua 6:17
text: Accursed; wholly devoted to destruction in God's name and by his authority.  Jericho being the first-fruits of the conquest of Canaan, the Israelites were required to devote every thing in it to God, reserving no spoils to themselves.  In the manner in which they obtained possession of the city they were taught that it was by God's might, not their own, that they were to conquer Canaan.  In the utter devotion of the city and its spoils to Jehovah, they were further taught that he was the sovereign proprietor of the promised land, and had an absolute right to dispose of it and its wealth as he saw good.

title: Joshua 6:19
text:
Into the treasury of the Lord; to be employed in the service of the sanctuary and the support of public worship. 
 
The silver and gold and treasures of every description which men have accumulated, belong to the Lord, and he has a perfect right to the disposal of them.

title: Joshua 6:21
text: The manner in which the Israelites passed over Jordan and took the city of Jericho, showed that while men obey God they have no good reason to distrust his willingness or his power to do for them all which they need.

title: Joshua 6:25
text: Faith in God meets his approbation, and secures, for those who exercise it, the richest blessings.   Hebrews 11:30 Hebrews 11:34

title: Joshua 6:26
text:
Adjured them; commanded them, under the penalty of a curse, not to build again the city of Jericho. 
 
  In his first-born, and in his youngest son; this is supposed to mean, that all his sons would die while he was building the city; his first-born when he laid the foundation, and his youngest when he set up the gates.   I Kings 16:34

title: Joshua 7:1
text:
The children of Israel; Israel is regarded as constituting one people consecrated to God's service; and the sin of a single member pollutes the whole body, and brings it under God's displeasure. 
 
Sins known only to those who commit them and to God may occasion calamities to a nation, and be the means of bringing many to an untimely grave.

title: Joshua 7:2
text: Ai; a city north-west of Jericho; the same as Hai.  Genesis 12:8 Genesis 13:3

title: Joshua 7:3
text: Great prosperity often tempts men to be self-confident, and leads them to neglect those means which are essential to their continued success.

title: Joshua 7:4
text: When men undertake plans in reliance on their own judgment or that of others, without inquiring of God, or seeking his direction, they will be likely to fail, and instead of success meet with speedy and sore disappointment.

title: Joshua 7:5
text:
Became as water; were utterly discouraged. 
 
Men are prone to go to extremes, and after being highly elated, to sink into despair.

title: Joshua 7:6
text: Put dust upon their heads; in token of deep distress.

title: Joshua 7:7
text: In trouble we should humble ourselves on account of our sins, and implore pardoning mercy; especially inquiring why it is that God contendeth with us, and seeking to know his will, that we may do it.

title: Joshua 7:9
text:
What wilt thou do? how would God secure his honor as faithful to his promises and able to fulfil them. 
 
When we truly desire the honor of God, and wish for success in our efforts that he may be glorified, our prayers will be accepted and answered in rich mercy.

title: Joshua 7:11
text: The cause of all trouble is sin; and so long as it is indulged, however secretly, we cannot expect deliverance, or the protection and blessing of God.

title: Joshua 7:13
text: All iniquity is perfectly known to God, and it is a solemn thing to stand before him and have it brought to light and spread out before the sun.

title: Joshua 7:14
text: The Lord taketh; designates by lot as presently explained.

title: Joshua 7:15
text: The punishment which God sometimes brings upon the workers of iniquity here, is a premonition of the more dreadful woes which will come upon them hereafter.

title: Joshua 7:18
text: The idea of keeping sin a secret is vain: those who commit it may be sure that, sooner or later, their sin will find them out.  Numbers 32:23 Matthew 10:26

title: Joshua 7:19
text: Give--glory to the Lord; by confessing the truth.

title: Joshua 7:21
text: I saw, I coveted, and I took, describes the course with regard to forbidden objects, of multitudes of transgressors; and their condition, when their sins are brought to light, is in total contrast to what they expected when they committed them.   Proverbs 13:15 James 1:15

title: Joshua 7:24
text: His sons, and his daughters; the lives of all are at God's disposal, and he has an absolute right to take them when and how he pleases.  In the present case he saw good to direct that all Achan's family, as well as his possessions, should perish with him.  We may reasonably suppose that one design of this was to impress more deeply upon the minds of the Israelites the malignant nature of sin, and its tendency to involve in ruin not only the transgressor himself, but all connected with him.  For the administration of justice by human judges he gave a different rule: "The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin."  Deuteronomy 24:16

title: Joshua 7:25
text: There are cases where God requires transgressors to be put to death, and his anger will not be turned away from a people unless they execute this punishment.   Genesis 9:6 Numbers 35:16-21 Deuteronomy 19:11-13

title: Joshua 7:26
text: Achor; meaning trouble.

title: Joshua 8:1
text: When sin is heartily put away, and men are disposed to hear and obey God, there is no reason to be discouraged, or to fear to undertake any service to which he calls them.

title: Joshua 8:2
text: By coveting what does not belong to them, and making haste to be rich, men often bring themselves to an untimely end; when, had they waited with patience and faithfully done their duty, they would in due time have had an abundance and been able to enjoy it.

title: Joshua 8:4
text: Ye shall lie in wait; from  Joshua 8:12 , it seems probable that only five thousand of these were actually placed in ambush between Bethel and Ai.

title: Joshua 8:8
text: If men would secure the blessings of the Lord, they must not shrink from any service to which he calls them.

title: Joshua 8:12
text: About five thousand; see note to  Joshua 8:4 .

title: Joshua 8:13
text: To accomplish things which God has foretold, and which are beforehand certain, it is as needful to use means as it would be if they were not foretold, or their accomplishment depended wholly upon human efforts.

title: Joshua 8:16
text: All the people; the men of war.   Joshua 8:24

title: Joshua 8:17
text: When the measure of a people's iniquity is full, they are given up, in hardness of heart and blindness of mind, to pursue a course which ends in their ruin.

title: Joshua 8:19
text: Set the city on fire; they began the work of burning the city, but its destruction was not completed till after Joshua and the men of war with him entered the city, spoiled it, and slew all its inhabitants.  Joshua 8:24-27

title: Joshua 8:25
text: In punishing men for their sins, God uses such instruments as he sees best, and it was no more wrong for him to destroy the men of Ai by the hand of the Israelites, than it would have been to destroy them by pestilence, famine, or an earthquake.

title: Joshua 8:29
text:
As the sun was down;  Deuteronomy 21:22-23
