Men of great influence, who have been leaders in transgression, will be distinguished in their punishment, and the righteous Judge will award to all who persevere in iniquity according to their works.

title: Joshua 8:30
text:
Mount Ebal;  Deuteronomy 11:29-30  
 
We should ever feel and acknowledge that all our blessings come through the atonement of Christ, and should engage in nothing which will unfit us to acknowledge and adore him.

title: Joshua 8:31
text: Whole stones;  Exodus 20:1

title: Joshua 8:33
text: Mount Gerizim;

title: Joshua 8:34
text: All the words of the law;  Deuteronomy 28:1

title: Joshua 8:35
text: The minds of all classes of people should be habitually directed to the will of God as revealed in the Scriptures, and all suitable means be perseveringly used to lead them to obey it.

title: Joshua 9:1
text:
This side Jordan; the west side, where the Israelites then were. 
 
  The great sea; the Mediterranean.

title: Joshua 9:2
text: No combination or power of wicked men, if they continue in sin, sill save them from ruin.

title: Joshua 9:3
text: Gibeon; a large city of the Hivites, a few miles north-west of Jerusalem.   Joshua 10:2

title: Joshua 9:4
text:
Wilily; craftily, deceitfully. 
 
  Wine-bottles; these were made of the skins of animals.

title: Joshua 9:6
text: A league; an agreement not to destroy them.

title: Joshua 9:8
text: A knowledge of the truth, the will, and purposes of God, leads some to oppose and others to submit themselves to him.   Joshua 9:25

title: Joshua 9:14
text: If men do not ask counsel of God, and seek his direction, they may expect to be habitually and grossly deceived.

title: Joshua 9:18
text: Sworn unto them; that their lives should be preserved.  Joshua 9:15 Joshua 9:20

title: Joshua 9:19
text: Solemn engagements to do things which are practicable, and not wicked, should be sacredly observed.  He that changeth not, when he sweareth even "to his own hurt," shall dwell in God's holy hill, and "shall never be moved."   Psalms 15:4 Ecclesiastes 5:4-6

title: Joshua 9:21
text: Hewers of wood and drawers of water; especially for the services of religion.   Joshua 9:23 Joshua 9:27

title: Joshua 9:27
text:
In the place which he should choose; for the sanctuary and for public worship. 
 
The sins of men are sometimes overruled for their good; but this does not lessen the evil of such sins, or the guilt of those who commit them.

title: Joshua 10:3
text: Hebron; south of Jerusalem.  The other places named are south-west of Jerusalem, in that part of Canaan which afterwards fell to the tribe of Judah.

title: Joshua 10:4
text: When sinners desert the cause of Satan and join with the people of God, those who continue to be Satan's slaves often unite against them, and would, if they could, utterly destroy them.

title: Joshua 10:8
text: Those who oppose their fellow men because they join the cause of God, oppose him, and thus often bring upon themselves utter ruin.

title: Joshua 10:10
text:
vv 10-11. 
 
  The way that goeth up to Beth-horon; literally, the way of the ascent of Beth-horon. 
 
  The going down to Beth-horon; the descent of Beth-horon.  There was an upper and lower Beth-horon, north-west of Jerusalem; and the pass between the two was called the ascent and the descent of Beth-horon. 
 
  Azekah; in the western plain of Judah.

title: Joshua 10:11
text: All the elements are under God's control, and when he directs will fight against his foes, as in the days of Moses, Barak, etc.  Exodus 14:21 Judges 5:20 Job 20:14-29 Isaiah 45:9 Hebrews 2:3

title: Joshua 10:12
text: Ajalon; a town and valley west of Gibeon.

title: Joshua 10:13
text: The book of Jasher; this is supposed by many to be a collection of poems, referring to the wonderful events in the history of Israel.  II Samuel 1:18

title: Joshua 10:14
text: Those who take the side of God, and follow his directions, will experience his aid, and through his grace will ultimately triumph.

title: Joshua 10:15
text: And Joshua returned--to Gilgal; these words are repeated in  Joshua 10:43 .  The best explanation of them here is, that they stand at the close of a general summary of Joshua's victory, to which is immediately added a more particular account of the same proceedings. From  Joshua 10:19 , it is manifest that it was in the midst of the pursuit that the report concerning the five kings was brought to Joshua.

title: Joshua 10:16
text: Makkedah; south-west of Jerusalem.

title: Joshua 10:18
text: Places to which the wicked flee for safety may become their prisons; and measures which they take to escape destruction, may be the occasion of bringing it upon them.

title: Joshua 10:19
text: The hindmost; such of them as they could overtake.

title: Joshua 10:20
text: Fenced; fortified.

title: Joshua 10:22
text: Those who have been most distinguished by the means of doing good, but have employed them in doing evil, will be most distinguished in their punishment.   Luke 12:47-48

title: Joshua 10:24
text: Upon the necks of these kings; in token of the complete victory of the Israelites over them and over all their foes.

title: Joshua 10:29
text: Libnah; a city south of Makkedah.

title: Joshua 10:30
text: Many things which are accomplished by human agency, are in the Bible ascribed to God.  In one sense man is the author, and in another sense God.   Acts 2:23 Acts 3:18

title: Joshua 10:31
text: Lachish; still further south.

title: Joshua 10:33
text: Gezer; in the territory that afterwards fell to the tribe of Ephraim, about fifteen miles north-west of Jerusalem.

title: Joshua 10:34
text: Eglon; a few miles west of Lachish.

title: Joshua 10:36
text: Hebron; a city east of Lachish, and twenty miles south of Jerusalem.

title: Joshua 10:38
text: Debir; southwest of Hebron.

title: Joshua 10:40
text:
Country of the hills; the hill country of Judea and the southern part of Canaan.   Luke 1:39 Luke 1:65  
 
By commanding the Israelites to destroy the Canaanites and take possession of their country, God laid them under obligation to do it; but no individual or nation, without his command, is authorized to do as they did.   Deuteronomy 2:4-9 Deuteronomy 2:19 Deuteronomy 2:30-33

title: Joshua 10:41
text:
Kadesh-barnea; near the south-east border of Canaan. 
 
  Gaza; near the Mediterranean and the south-west border of Canaan. 
 
  Goshen; lying south, in the mountainous region of Judea.  Joshua 15:51

title: Joshua 11:1
text:
Hazor; a strong and chief city in the north part of Canaan.  Joshua 11:10  
 
  Madon; not far from Hazor. 
 
  Shimron; called,  Joshua 12:20 , Shimron-meron.  It was afterwards in the tribe of Zebulun. 
 
  Achshaph; west of Zebulun, in the tribe of Asher. 
 
The wicked in their distress often pursue courses which, instead of relieving them, hasten their destruction.

title: Joshua 11:2
text:
The mountains; probably the mountains of Naphtali north-west of the sea of Tiberias. 
 
  Chinneroth; on the lake of Gennesareth, or sea of Tiberias. 
 
  Dor; on the Mediterranean, not far from mount Carmel.

title: Joshua 11:3
text:
Hermon;  Deuteronomy 3:1 
  Mizpeh; called,  Joshua 11:8 , "the valley of Mizpeh eastward." Hermon, under which it lay, was in the eastern range of Lebanon.

title: Joshua 11:5
text: The waters of Merom; a collection of waters in the upper part of Canaan, from which flows the river Jordan.  It is about twelve miles above the sea of Galilee, and is about five miles long, with a level region north of it partially overflowed in the spring.  Its present name is Bahr-el-Huleh.

title: Joshua 11:6
text:
Hough their horses; hamstring them; cut the great cord of their hind legs. 
 
However numerous the enemies within and without, or however mighty the combinations against the people of God, if in obedience to him they rightly use the means which he gives them, they have no reason to fear, for at which he gives them, they have no reson to fear, for at his appointed time he will cause them to triumph over all their foes.

title: Joshua 11:7
text: The aid which God gives is not designed to supersede or render needless human efforts; but to encourage men to make efforts, and to render them successful.

title: Joshua 11:8
text:
Great Zidon; a city on the Mediterranean, about twenty-five miles north of Tyre, fifty south of Beyroot, and sixty-six west of Damascus. It is called great on account of its numerous people and abundant wealth. 
 
  Misrephoth-maim; north of Zidon.

title: Joshua 11:9
text: The whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain.  Even the brute creation suffer in consequence of the sins of men.  Though these sufferings are under the direction of an infinitely wise, holy, and benevolent God, they are the effects of sin, and a just expression of his indignation against it.

title: Joshua 11:11
text: Men are often called to most self-denying duties, and those from which the most wise, holy, and benevolent minds would, if consistent, gladly be excused.   Matthew 26:39

title: Joshua 11:12
text: As Moses--commanded; this is often mentioned to show that for destroying the Canaanites the Israelites were not to be blamed but commended, because that in doing it they were obeying God.  Joshua 11:15 Joshua 11:20 Joshua 11:23

title: Joshua 11:13
text: Stood still in their strength; rather, "stood upon their hill."  It was the custom to build cities on them.  These cities the Israelites, after destroying their inhabitants, reserved for their own use.

title: Joshua 11:15
text: Resolute, determined, and habitual obedience to God's commands, is the only course of wisdom, safety, usefulness, and bliss.

title: Joshua 11:16
text:
The hills; the mountainous region of the south. 
 
  The land of Goshen; see note to  Joshua 10:41 . 
 
  The valley; the low regin bordering on the Mediterranean. 
 
  The plain; the long narrow vale through which the Jordan flows and in which the Dead sea lies.  The southern portion of it opposite to "the south country" is meant.

title: Joshua 11:17
text:
The mount Halak; that is, "the bald mountain."  The writer probably means a line of naked chalk hills running across the valley from the west to east about eight miles south of the Dead sea; the same as "the ascent of Akrabbim," which formed the southern boundary of Canaan.  Numbers 34:4  
 
  Mount Hermon; the southern part of Anti-Lebanon.   Deuteronomy 3:8

title: Joshua 11:18
text:
A long time; about seven years. 
 
We must not cease in our efforts to conquer the spiritual enemies of God and our own souls, till they are so effectually subdued as never again to rise up against us.

title: Joshua 11:20
text:
To harden their hearts; by leaving them, as a punishment for their sins, to pursue their own chosen way to ruin.   Exodus 4:21  
 
When God has determined to destroy men, he lets them pursue their chosen way of folly and sin to their ruin.

title: Joshua 11:21
text: Hebron--Debir--Anab; in the southern part of the country.

title: Joshua 11:22
text: Gaza--Gath--Ashdod; cities of the Philistines in the south-west part of Palestine, and near the Mediterranean.

title: Joshua 11:23
text:
Took the whole land; not absolutely every city and region of it, for there remained yet very much land to be possessed,  Joshua 13:1 ; but he conquered the whole country so as to be able to divide it by lot to the Israelites. 
 
Perseverance in humble, hearty, courageous obedience to God, will end in sure and most glorious triumph.

title: Joshua 12:1
text:
From the river Arnon; on the south. 
 
  Unto mount Hermon; on the north. 
 
  All the plain on the east; that is, the eastern half of the valley through which the Jordan flows. 
 
It is useful to recount what God has done by human instrumentality, and not only by men who are now living, but by those who have gone to their rest and are enjoying the reward of their labors.

title: Joshua 12:2
text:
vv 2-3. 
 
  Sihon--Ashdoth-pisgah; these verses may be thus rendered: Sihon, king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, ruling from Aroer, which is upon the bank of the river Arnon, and from the middle of the river; and over half of Gilead, unto the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon; and [over] the plain [northward] to the sea of Chinneroth on the eastern side, and [southward] to the sea of the plain, the salt sea, on the eastern side, the way to Beth-jeshimoth, and, on the south under Ashdoth-pisgah. 
 
The upper Jabbok divided the kingdom of Sihon from the Amonites; the lower Jabbok divided Gilead into two parts.  Beth-jeshimoth seems to have marked the south-eastern corner of that part of the plain which belonged to Sihon, and Ashdoth-pisgah its southern extremity.

title: Joshua 12:4
text: Ashtaroth and--Edrei; places in Bashan.

title: Joshua 12:5
text:
Salcah; in the eastern border of Bashan. 
 
  Geshurites--Maachathites; north of Bashan. 
 
  Half Gilead; that half, namely, that lay north of the Jabbok, the southern half belonging to the kingdom of Sihon,  Joshua 12:2 .

title: Joshua 12:7
text: We are greatly indebted to men of past generations.  Other men have labored, and we enter into their labors; and the good works which they began, but were not able to finish, we should endeavor in the strength of the Lord, and by his aid, to accomplish.

title: Joshua 12:8
text:
In the mountains--valleys--plains; in the original, these words are in the singular number--the mountain, the valley, the plain.  "The mountain" is the mountainous region of Palestine; "the valley" is the low region bordering the Mediterranean; "the plain" is the valley of the Jordan and the Dead sea. 
 
  Springs; or low places at the foot of the mountains.

title: Joshua 12:9
text:
vv 9-24. 
 
The places here mentioned are those which Joshua conquered during the wars described in the previous chapters.

title: Joshua 13:1
text:
Was old; about one hundred years old. 
 
  Much land; that belonged to the Canaanites, and was promised to Israel, but was not yet taken. 
 
If life is prolonged, old age with its attendant infirmities will soon come, and death will follow.  All should therefore be diligent in the discharge of their appropriate duties.  When unfitted for one kind of labor, they should, if practicable, engage in another; and spend life in the discharge of duty, that they may be fitted to close it and enter into rest.

title: Joshua 13:2
text:
The borders of the Philistines; a region of country in the south-west part of Canaan, and extending on the Mediterranean about sixty miles. 
 
  Geshuri; a country south of the Philistines and on the borders of the wilderness of Shur.   I Samuel 27:8   There was another country of the same name on the north-east border of Canaan. 
 
However diligent and successful any may be in extending the kingdom of God, much will remain to be accomplished by their successors.  Each generation has its appropriate work, and no part of what belongs to it should be left to be performed by others.

title: Joshua 13:3
text:
Sihor; probably the eastern arm of the Nile; but some suppose it was in the valley El-Arish, and ran into the Mediterranean south-west of Gaza.   Numbers 34:5  
 
  Ekron; the northern district of the Philistines, about ten miles north-east of Ashdod, and thirty-four west of Jerusalem. 
 
  The Avites; they were the original inhabitants of this country, but were dispossessed by the Philistines, called Caphtorim,  Deuteronomy 2:23 Genesis 10:13-14 .  Some Avites still continued in that region.

title: Joshua 13:4
text: Aphek; supposed to be a city in the north part of Canaan.  Judges 1:31

title: Joshua 13:5
text: Giblites; inhabitants of Gebal, near Zidon.

title: Joshua 13:6
text:
Divide thou it; Joshua was by lot to divide the whole land of Canaan on the west side of Jordan among the nine and a half tribes, although it was not yet all conquered. 
 
Men may be sure before the promises of God are fulfilled that he will perform them, and may with perfect propriety act accordingly.

title: Joshua 13:9
text:
vv 9-32. 
 
These verses describe the countries conquered by Moses on the east side of Jordan.  The south part was allotted to the tribe of Reuben, the central part to the tribe of Gad, and the north part to the half-tribe of Manasseh.

title: Joshua 13:13
text: Geshurites--Maachathites; people inhabiting districts east of the sources of the Jordan, north of Bashan, and near mount Hermon.

title: Joshua 13:14
text: Though the ministers of Christ have not opportunities to acquire wealth, yet, if faithful to him, he will provide for them all things needful in this world, and will himself be their portion for ever.  Joshua 13:33

title: Joshua 13:21
text: All the kingdom of Sihon; that is, all that part which lay within the limits of the region assigned to Reuben; for "the rest of the kingdom of Sihon," constituting its northern part, was given to the tribe of Gad,  Joshua 13:27 .

title: Joshua 13:22
text: Those who love the wages of unrighteousness and tempt others to sin, may for a time escape punishment; yet their sins are not forgotten, and in due time they will receive the just reward of their deeds.

title: Joshua 13:25
text: Half the land of the children of Ammon; that portion, namely, lying between the Arnon and the Jabbok, which Sihon had previously taken from Ammon, as we gather from the narrative in  Judges 11:12-23 .  The Israelites were not allowed to take any of the territory which they found in possession of the Ammonites.   Deuteronomy 2:19

title: Joshua 13:32
text: God places men in such countries and conditions as he sees best.  They should all receive their blessings as gifts, and use them for his honor and their own highest good.

title: Joshua 13:33
text: The Lord God of Israel was their inheritance; they received their support in conducting his worship from the tithes and offerings of the people.   Numbers 18:1-32

title: Joshua 14:2
text:
By lot was their inheritance; and yet God so ordered the lot that each tribe obtained the inheritance which it was predicted by Jacob and Moses that they should possess.   Genesis 49:1-33 Deuteronomy 33:1-29  
 
Those things which appear to men to be casual, which are sometimes spoken of as happening or coming by chance, are nevertheless under the direction and control of God.   Proverbs 16:33

title: Joshua 14:5
text: If men do as the Lord commands, they will see the truth of his declarations and experience the fulfilment of his promises.

title: Joshua 14:6
text: The thing that the Lord said;  Numbers 14:24 Numbers 14:30 Deuteronomy 1:36

title: Joshua 14:7
text:
As it was in my heart; he gave a sincere, honest, faithful report. 
 
Sincerity, honesty, uprightness, and fidelity to God and men are the surest course to long life, usefulness, respectability, and the greatest enjoyment of blessings for this life and the life to come.

title: Joshua 14:8
text: The ways of transgressors are hard, and those who decline the path of duty to avoid its trials or obtain some temporary good, take a course that is often most fatal to themselves and to others.

title: Joshua 14:12
text:
This mountain; the mountainous country about Hebron. 
 
  How the Anakim were there; the presence of the Anakim, instead of discouraging Caleb, is an incitement to him to undertake the conquest of the region, for he has faith in God's presence and help. 
 
If the Lord be with us, and we conduct in such a manner as to secure his blessing, we shall be victorious in our conflicts, and gain possession of the inheritance which he has promised to his people.

title: Joshua 14:13
text: Hebron; the district in which Hebron lay; the city itself was given to the Levites.   Joshua 21:12-13

title: Joshua 14:15
text:
Kirjath-arba;  Genesis 23:2 
  Had rest; rest from general wars.

title: Joshua 15:1
text: God will peculiarly bless those who are faithful in his service, and bestow upon them all needed good.

title: Joshua 15:2
text:
vv 2-4. 
 
  And their south border--south coast; these verses contain an accurate description of the south border of Judah, which was also the southern limit of Canaan west of the Arabab, a long narrow valley running south from the Dead sea.  Beginning from the southern bay of the Dead sea, it ran south about eight miles to Maaleh-acrabbim, a line of chalk hills running east and west across the Arabah.  Thence it passed south and west to Kadesh-barnea.  Thence it was carried in a general westerly direction to "the river of Egypt" at Rhinocolura.

title: Joshua 15:5
text: End of Jordan; its mouth, at the Dead sea.

title: Joshua 15:6
text:
vv 6-11. 
 
These places lay along a line from near the north end of the Dead sea west, by Jerusalem, to Ekron in the land of the Philistines.

title: Joshua 15:7
text: En-rogel; a well in the valley of Kidron a little distance south of Jerusalem.

title: Joshua 15:8
text: Valley of the son of Hinnom; this valley begins on the west of Jerusalem, and sweeps around its south-west corner--the ancient Zion-- entering the valley of Kidron just below the city.  Thus Jerusalem itself belonged not to Judah, but to Benjamin.   Joshua 18:16

title: Joshua 15:13
text: God never forgets his promises, and in due time those who trust in him will experience their fulfilment.

title: Joshua 15:15
text: Debir; a city west of Hebron, and south-west of Jerusalem.

title: Joshua 15:17
text: It is a great privilege to be connected in marriage with pious families; and where the will of God is duly regarded in forming this connection, it may be expected to promote the respectability, usefulness, and comfort of all concerned.

title: Joshua 15:19
text:
A south land; one that was warm and comparatively without water. 
 
  The upper springs, and the nether; high and low grounds that were well watered.

title: Joshua 15:21
text:
vv 21-62. 
 
The places here mentioned lay in the south part of Canaan, in that portion which was allotted to Judah; a part of which was afterwards given to the tribe of Simeon.

title: Joshua 15:32
text: Twenty and nine; thirty-eight are mentioned; but nine, it is supposed, were given to Simeon, leaving twenty-nine for Judah.

title: Joshua 15:36
text: Fourteen cities; fifteen names are mentioned, but two are supposed to belong to one city, or to it and its suburbs.

title: Joshua 16:1
text:
The children of Joseph; Ephraim and Manasseh.  The inheritance of Ephraim was north of that of Simeon, Judah, Dan, and Benjamin.  It extended from the river Jordan across the whole land to the Mediterranean.  The inheritance of that half-tribe of Manessah which was not provided for on the east of Jordan, was north of that of Ephraim, and had the Mediterranean on the west, Asher and Zebulun on the north, and Issachar on the east. 
 
The lot of all is appointed to them in the providence of God.  For its blessings they should be thankful, under its trials submissive, and in all its duties guided by the revealed will of God.

title: Joshua 16:2
text:
vv 2-10. 
 
The places mentioned in these verses are in the districts of country above described in  Joshua 16:1 .

title: Joshua 16:10
text: The more faithfully men follow the will of God, the greater real good will they enjoy, both in this life and that to come.

title: Joshua 17:1
text:
Gilead and Bashan; countries on th east of Jordan and north of those allotted to the tribes of Gad and Reuben. 
 
The various talents of men come from God, and he allots to them such situations as are suited to the duties to which he calls them.

title: Joshua 17:2
text: The rest of the children of Manasseh; those not provided for on the east of Jordan.   Joshua 17:5

title: Joshua 17:4
text:
The Lord commanded;   
 
It is proper that daughters should have an inheritance as well as sons, and so far as is consistent be provided for according to their wants.

title: Joshua 17:5
text: Ten portions; after the children of Machir had received Gilead and Bashan, there remained the six other sons to be provided for on the west side of Jordan.  Five of these received one portion each; and for the daughters of Zelophehad the son of Hepher were provided five portions more, making ten in all.

title: Joshua 17:9
text: The river Kanah; a small stream which formed the boundary between Manasseh and Ephraim, and empties into the Mediterranean south of Caesarea.

title: Joshua 17:11
text: In Issachar--Asher; within the limits of those tribes.

title: Joshua 17:12
text:
Could not; for want of faith and the use of due means. 
 
It is often said in the Bible that men "cannot" do that which they will not try to do, nor use the means by which, through the blessing of God, they can do it.

title: Joshua 17:13
text:
Tribute; an annual tax, in token of submission. 
 
Through sloth and inactivity, men will often sacrifice great future good for the sake of a little present ease.

title: Joshua 17:14
text: One lot and one portion; they claimed a double portion on account of their number.

title: Joshua 17:15
text:
Get thee up; take possession of those portions of the country allotted to you, which have not yet been subdued. 
 
Men are often in want because they neglect to use proper means to obtain relief, and the best way to help such persons is to put them in a way to help themselves.

title: Joshua 17:16
text: The valley of Jezreel; these words seem to include both the large plain south-east of mount Carmel, and south-west from mount Tabor, called by the Greeks Esdraelon, and also the valley of the Jordan.

title: Joshua 17:18
text:
The mountain; the hilly country before spoken of. 
 
  Drive out; this they could do in reliance on God.

title: Joshua 18:1
text:
Shiloh; in the tribe of Ephraim, about twenty-five miles north of Jerusalem, and about fifteen south of Shechem. 
 
The place for public worship should be central, and such as will best accommodate those who are expected there to assemble.

title: Joshua 18:2
text: Seven tribes; Simeon, Benjamin, Dan, Issachar, Zebulun, Asher, and Naphtali.

title: Joshua 18:3
text: Men often long remain destitute of many things which it is the will of God that they should enjoy, and which with the right use of means they might enjoy.

title: Joshua 18:4
text: Give out; choose, or appoint.

title: Joshua 18:5
text: Their coast; the place already assigned them.

title: Joshua 18:9
text:
Described it by cities--in a book; they gave a description of the country, as divided by them into seven parts, one for each tribe that had not yet received its inheritance. 
 
In dividing estates, great care should be taken that the boundaries be so fixed as to avoid all future contention about them.

title: Joshua 18:11
text: Between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph; Judah was on the south, and Ephraim on the north.  Jerusalem was in Benjamin, and thus, as predicted of him, he dwelt in safety by the Lord.  Deuteronomy 33:12

title: Joshua 18:12
text:
vv 12-28. 
 
The places here mentioned were on the borders of Benjamin's inheritance, which was bounded by the Jordan on the east and Dan on the west.

title: Joshua 18:20
text: Families are the appointment of Jehovah, and for them he provides with infinite wisdom and goodness.  They are designed and adapted to be sources of great enjoyment on earth adn to be nurseries for heaven.

title: Joshua 19:1
text: Within the inheritance of--Judah; on the survey of the whole land, it was found that what had been allotted to Judah was too large for one tribe,  Joshua 19:9 ; the south-west part of it was therefore allotted to Simeon.  His inheritance was bounded on the north and east by that of Judah, on the south by the desert of Zin, and on the west by the land of the Philistines.

title: Joshua 19:2
text:
vv 2-9. 
 
These places were within the district mentioned in note  Joshua 19:1 .

title: Joshua 19:9
text: If through mistake persons have obtained more than rightfully belongs to them, they should, on its being known, promptly and cheerfully restore it.

title: Joshua 19:10
text: The children of Zebulun; their inheritance was bounded on the east by the river Jordan and the sea of Galilee, on the north by Asher and Naphtali, on the west by Asher and Manasseh, and on the south by Issachar.

title: Joshua 19:11
text:
vv 11-15. 
 
These places were in or on the borders of the territory mentioned in note on  Joshua 19:10 .

title: Joshua 19:17
text: The children of Issachar; their inheritance was bounded on the east by the Jordan, on the north by Zebulun, on the west by Manasseh, and on the south by Ephraim.

title: Joshua 19:18
text:
vv 18-22. 
 
Places in or on the borders of Issachar.

title: Joshua 19:24
text: The children of Asher; their inheritance was in the north-west part of the country towards Tyre, and was bounded on the east by Naphtali, on the north by Syria, on the west by Phenicia, and on the south by Zebulun.

title: Joshua 19:25
text:
vv 25-31. 
 
Places in or on the borders of Asher.

title: Joshua 19:32
text: The children of Naphtali; their inheritance was in the north-east part of the country, and was bounded on the east by the Jordan, on the north by Syria, on the west by Asher, and on the south by Zebulun and the sea of Galilee.

title: Joshua 19:33
text:
vv 33-38. 
 
Places in, or on the borders of Naphtali. 
 
  Judah upon Jordan toward the sunrising; we are probably to understand the cities of Jair in the land of Gilead east of the Jordan,  I Chronicles 21:23 .  Though these properly belonged to the half-tribe of Manasseh, they might well have been called "Judah upon Jordan," because Jair was a descendant of Judah.

title: Joshua 19:40
text:
The children of Dan; their inheritance was bounded by Benjamin on the east, by Ephraim on the north, by the Mediterranean and the Philistines on the west, and by Judah on the south. 
 
Although the land of Canaan was divided by lot among the several tribes of Israel, yet their inheritance and condition were such as was predicted, and as it was beforehand certain that they would be.

title: Joshua 19:41
text:
vv 41-46. 
 
Places in or on the borders of Dan.

title: Joshua 19:47
text: Leshem; the same as Laish, a city near the foot of mount Lebanon and the sources of the Jordan.   Judges 18:1-29

title: Joshua 19:50
text:
Timnath-serah; a place in the hilly country of the tribe of Ephraim, called, in  Judges 2:9 , Timnath-heres.  It was here that Joshua lived, died, and was buried. 
 
They who have been eminent benefactors of their fellow men, should be remembered with gratitude, honored, and if need by, provided for, by those whose interests have been secured by their sacrifices and efforts.

title: Joshua 20:2
text: Whereof I spake;  Exodus 21:13 Numbers 35:3-34

title: Joshua 20:3
text: Unwittingly; without design.

title: Joshua 20:5
text: Our lives are always uncertain, and are liable to be suddenly taken away, either by design or through our own carelessness or mistakes, or those of our fellow men.

title: Joshua 20:6
text:
Judgment; a fair trial and a righteous decision. 
 
As life may be destroyed through carelessness as well as by design, carelessness is a sin which should be most conscientiously avoided, and if it is not, should be visited with its appropriate punishment.

title: Joshua 20:7
text:
Mount Naphtali; the hilly region in the tribe of Naphtali, in the north part of the country. 
 
  Shechem; this was in the central part, and Hebron in the south part of the country.

title: Joshua 20:8
text: Bezer; a city in the south part of the country, east of the Jordan; Ramoth was in the central, and Golan in the north part of the country.

title: Joshua 20:9
text: No person accused of murder should be acquitted or condemned till after a full and fair trial; nor should he suffer death unless proved to be guilty.

title: Joshua 21:3
text: It is not left merely to the inclinations of men whether they will provide for the comfortable support of the ministers of religion, but it is the command of God that those who preach the gospel should live of the gospel, and their hearers cannot withhold from them needful support wihtout depriving them of what is justly their due.  I Corinthians 9:13-14

title: Joshua 21:4
text:
Judah--Simeon--Benjamin; thus the priests had their cities in the tribes that were near to Jerusalem and the temple afterwards built there.   Joshua 21:9-19  
 
It is a great convenience for the ministers of religion to live near the place of public worship, and generally it will be found to be most conducive to their good and the good of the people.

title: Joshua 21:5
text:
The rest; those of the family of Kohath who were not priests.  Joshua 21:20-26  
 
There should be ministers of religion in all parts of the country, that all the people may have the benefit of their good instructions and example.

title: Joshua 21:27
text: The children of Gershon; these were Levites, but not priests.

title: Joshua 21:34
text: The children of Merari; Levites, but not priests.

title: Joshua 21:41
text:
Forty and eight cities; according to the direction of Moses,  Numbers 35:7 . 
 
The Lord in his providence appoints to ministers their various fields of labor, and wherever they are placed it should be their great object to honor him and be most useful to men.

title: Joshua 21:42
text: Suburbs; adjacent territory to the extent of two thousand cubits on every side, according to the direction in  Numbers 35:5 .

title: Joshua 21:43
text:
They possessed it; they possessed all that they then needed; and the rest the Lord would give them, according to his promise,  Exodus 23:30 . 
 
Whatever may be the promises of God, and however great the difficulties in the way of their accomplishment, in due time they will all be fulfilled.

title: Joshua 22:1
text: The Reubenites--Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh; their men of war, who had left their homes on the east side of Jordan to assist their brethren in the conquest of Canaan.

title: Joshua 22:2
text: Just commendation is due to those who do well, and true gratitude should be exercised towards all who make sacrifices, endure hardships, and perform labors for the good of their fellow men.

title: Joshua 22:4
text: Fidelity in obeying God's commands will receive his approbation and blessing, and a glorious reward.

title: Joshua 22:5
text: The true greatness, glory, and blessedness of a people consist in their loving the Lord, observing his ordinances, and walking in his ways.

title: Joshua 22:7
text: Bashan; the north part of the country possessed by the Israelites on the east of Jordan.

title: Joshua 22:10
text:
By Jordan; on its east bank. 
 
Suitable care should be taken, in providing against future evils, not to awaken needless suspicions, nor occasion unnecessary anxiety and trouble to our fellow men.

title: Joshua 22:16
text:
Builded you an altar; to offer sacrifice in any place except at the tabernacle, was expressly forbidden.   Leviticus 17:8-9  
 
We may be blamed, even by good men, for our best actions.  But we should not be disconcerted, should listen to them with patience, and when we thoroughly understand their mistakes, should endeavor kindly to remove them.

title: Joshua 22:17
text: Iniquity of Peor;  Numbers 25:3 Deuteronomy 4:1

title: Joshua 22:19
text:
If the land--be unclean; if they thought it unclean because there was in it no altar for sacrifice, and no place for public religious worship, they were invited to come over and live on the west side of Jordan where was the tabernacle, rather than to set up separate worship and thus rebel against God. 
 
When those who are disturbed at the conduct of others, go to them and frankly state their difficulties, and manifest a readiness to make sacrifices and even to give up their own rights, rather than to have God dishonored or his cause injured, it may be expected that with reasonable explantions they will be satisfied.

title: Joshua 22:20
text: Not alone;  Joshua 7:5 Joshua 7:24-24:33

title: Joshua 22:22
text: A consciousness of being and doing right tends to prevent undue excitement under unjust accusations, and to lead to such explanations as will remove needless apprehensions and be satisfactory to all concerned.

title: Joshua 22:23
text: The Lord--require; let him punish us, if we designed to rebel against him.

title: Joshua 22:25
text: Make our children cease from fearing the Lord; by refusing to let them come over the Jordan to worship him.

title: Joshua 22:26
text: It is proper to take all suitable measures to guard our children against evils to which from the selfishness of men they will be exposed, and to enable them to know what are their rights, especially their religious rights, and successfully to maintain and permanently enjoy them.

title: Joshua 22:28
text: A witness; that they had a right to go over Jordan.

title: Joshua 22:29
text: To build an altar;  Deuteronomy 12:13-14:1

title: Joshua 22:30
text: A disposition to enjoy religious rights ourselves, and to secure them to coming generations, is pleasing to all intelligent and right-minded men, especially to pious rulers and ministers of the gospel.

title: Joshua 22:31
text: Ye have delivered the children of Israel; not exposed them to punishment as they feared, by sinning against the Lord, but taken measures to perpetuate his worship.

title: Joshua 22:33
text: Good men, enlightened by the Spirit of God, will not make war upon others for maintaining their just rights, especially their right to hearken to the voice of God in the Scriptures, to judge of his meaning, and to worship him according to his directions.

title: Joshua 22:34
text: Ed; a witness.

title: Joshua 23:1
text: No fidelity to God, or usefulness to men, can keep off the approach of age, infirmity, or death.  This should be borne in mind, and incite all to do with their might what they are hastening, there is no work.

title: Joshua 23:3
text: The aged may recount the mercies of the Lord with great advantage to themselves and to their fellow men.

title: Joshua 23:4
text:
The great sea; the Mediterranean, which formed the western boundary of Canaan. 
 
Faith in God produces a permanent conviction of the truth of his promises, and leads men to act as if they knew that they would be fulfilled.

title: Joshua 23:6
text: The fact that God will do for us what we need, instead of leading us to neglect appropriate means, or to feel that they are less important, should lead us with fidelity to use them, because that is the only way effectually to secure his aid.

title: Joshua 23:7
text:
Neither make mention; the familiar mention of the names of idols would tend to lessen their abhorrence of them. 
 
Intimate connections with the wicked greatly increase the danger of becoming like them.

title: Joshua 23:9
text: Things are done by the Lord which are accomplished by human instrumentality.  Men use the means, and God renders them successful.

title: Joshua 23:10
text:
One man of you shall chase a thousand; however few they might be, and however numerous their enemies, they, in obeying God, would be able to overcome them. 
 
When God is on our side and works for us, we need fear no enemies, however numerous or strong, but we may go forward in duty, with assured confidence of final and complete victory.

title: Joshua 23:11
text:
Take good heed; be very careful. 
 
If we love and obey God, we shall be in all good efforts in the highest and best sense successful; but if we disregard his laws, and are governed by the principles and practices of the wicked, we may expect calamity and ruin.

title: Joshua 23:14
text:
Going the way of all the earth; about to die.   Genesis 3:19  
 
The fulfilment of God's declarations in times past, should assure us of their fulfilment in time to come.

title: Joshua 24:1
text:
Shechem; a city north of Shiloh, and nearer to Timnath-serah, where Joshua lived.   Joshua 18:1  
 
It is good for all people at times to appear before God, look back on the way through which he hath led them, recount his goodness, renew their engagements to serve him, and seek that grace which they need to do it in spirit and in truth.

title: Joshua 24:2
text:
The flood; the river; meaning the Euphrates. 
 
  Other gods; idols. 
 
Aged men may to great advantage give the young a history of God's dealings with past generations, point out the instructions it affords and the duties it inculcates, and exhort all to fidelity in the service.

title: Joshua 24:4
text: Seir; a country south of the Dead sea.

title: Joshua 24:6
text:
The sea; the Red sea. 
 
Things accomplished by human instrumentality and the persevering use of appointed means, are in the Bible ascribed to God as really as if no instrumentality or means had been employed.

title: Joshua 24:7
text: A long season; about forty years.

title: Joshua 24:10
text:
His hand; the hand of Balak. 
 
Those measures which men take to injure God's people and stop the progress of his cause, he often overrules for its advancement.

title: Joshua 24:13
text: The mercies by which the friends of God are distinguished from his enemies, spring from his unmerited goodness, and are given not as the fruit of ther worthiness, but of the abounding riches of his grace.

title: Joshua 24:14
text: Peculiar mercies lay men under peculiar obligations to put away all sin, and to perfect holiness in the fear and love of God.

title: Joshua 24:15
text: True religion is a matter of choice with all who heartily embrace it, and no man ever does or can serve God, in spirit and in truth, without choosing to do so.  Of course ministers should present to men the motives which are best suited to lead them to do this, and to their preaching should add the influence of their example.

title: Joshua 24:19
text:
Ye cannot serve the Lord; they could not without renouncing all idols, as Joshua exhorted them to do, loving God with supreme affection, and obeying his commands; and for disposition to do this, they must depend not on themselves merely, or on their own goodness, but on the influences of his Spirit. 
 
  He will not forgive your--sins; unless they should repent of and forsake them.  Therefore Joshua urged them to do this. 
 
As Jehovah is holy, it is impossible acceptably to serve him without becoming holy; and as the cause of holiness in men is the influence of the Holy Spirit, all should feel their need of this, and sincerely, heartily seek it.

title: Joshua 24:21
text: Wherever there is a willing mind men can truly serve God, and for Christ's sake be accepted in doing it; and as a willing mind is the fruit of the Spirit, all who possess it should give to him the glory.

title: Joshua 24:23
text: It is the duty of men to incline their hearts to serve the Lord.  They should avoid those things which tend to hinder them, and do the things which tend to aid them in this.

title: Joshua 24:24
text: Persons may, adn it is right that they should determine, resolve, and engage to serve the Lord; and they may freely and heartily trust in him for what they need rightly to do this, adn to be accepted in it.

title: Joshua 24:26
text:
These words; the engagements into which the people had entered to serve the Lord. 
 
  By the sanctury; near the place where the tabernacle stood.

title: Joshua 24:27
text:
It hath heard; a strong figure of speech, expressive of the solemnity of the transaction, and of their guilt and danger should they break their engagements. 
 
It is so perfectly reasonable that all to whom Jehovah is known should love and obey him, and they are under such strong and indispensable obligations immediately to do this, that if they do not, all their mercies and every thing around and within them will testify to their ingratitude, baseness, and guilt.

title: Joshua 24:31
text: Aged men and men of influence, especially rulers, magistrates, and all in authority, are under peculiar obligations to serve God, and to set holy examples.  If they do, many others will be likely to follow them and obtain eternal life.  But if they do not, they will be instrumental in bringing destruction not only on themselves, but on multitudes of others.

title: Joshua 24:32
text: Which Jacob bought;  Genesis 33:19 Genesis 50:25 Exodus 13:1

title: Joshua 24:33
text: Rulers and ministers of religion, as well as other men, will soon die, but their influence for good or evil will live and go down to the end of time.

title: Judges 1:1
text: However great may have been their past successes, the people of God should not rest till fully triumphant over all their foes.

title: Judges 1:3
text: The union of all classes of pious men in doing good, is greatly promotive of success.

title: Judges 1:4
text: Bezek; a place in the territory of Judah.

title: Judges 1:5
text: Adoni-bezek; the lord or king of Bezek.

title: Judges 1:6
text: Pride and cruelty are forerunners of disaster; and the peculiar sins of men may often be read in their punishment.

title: Judges 1:7
text:
Threescore and ten; these seventy kings were evidently petty princes, ruling each over a small territory. 
 
A true conviction of the evil of sin will lead all who suffer to feel that their punishment is just.

title: Judges 1:9
text: The south; the south part of Canaan.

title: Judges 1:10
text: Hebron; a city twenty miles south of Jerusalem.  Genesis 13:18 Joshua 15:13

title: Judges 1:11
text: Debir;  Joshua 15:1

title: Judges 1:14
text: A wise and affectionate wife wishes the temporal propserity as well as the eternal good of her husband, and will use all suitable means to promote it.

title: Judges 1:15
text:
A south land;  Joshua 15:16-19:1 Jos 15.16-19. 
 
A wise and affectionate father will take great pleasure in complying, as far as may be consistent, with the requests of his children.

title: Judges 1:16
text:
The Kenite; Jethro.   Exodus 3:1 Numbers 10:29-32  
 
  Arad; a city on the south border of Canaan.   Numbers 21:1

title: Judges 1:17
text:
Zephath; a place near the south part of Judah. 
 
  Hormah; that is, utter destruction.

title: Judges 1:18
text: Gaza--Ashkelon--and Edron; cities of the Philistines.

title: Judges 1:19
text:
Could not; because, terrified by the chariots, they did not trust in God and use the proper means. 
 
Viewing difficulties with an eye of sense only, men often despond, when, should they use proper means in dependence on God, he would render them successful.

title: Judges 1:21
text:
Jerusalem; this city was on the border between Judah and Benjamin, though in the division of the land it was assigned to the latter tribe.  Joshua 15:63  
 
Love of ease, and aversion to great and self-denying efforts, often keep men from receiving the variety and fulness of good which they might otherwise obtain, and leave them to suffer much evil which they might otherwise avoid.

title: Judges 1:22
text: House of Joseph; that is, the tribe of Ephraim and the half-tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan, though what is here said seems to pertain only to the territory of Ephraim.

title: Judges 1:23
text:
Descry; examine and ascertain the state of the city. 
 
  Bethel; a place north of Jerusalem.   Genesis 28:19

title: Judges 1:25
text: Assisting the people of God in doing his will, may be the means of delivering us from many trials and bringing on us great blessings.

title: Judges 1:27
text:
Beth-shean; a place in the valley of the Jordan near the east end of the valley of Jezreel. 
 
  Taanach; on the south border of the plain of Esdraelon. 
 
  Dor; on the sea, south of Carmel. 
 
  Megiddo; near the Kishon.

title: Judges 1:29
text:
Gezer; north-west of Jerusalem. 
 
vv 29-33. 
 
Towns within the bounds of the tribes, in connection with whose names they are mentioned.

title: Judges 1:34
text:
The valley; the plain bordering on the Mediterranean, where the Amorites had chariots of iron.  Compare  Judges 1:19 . 
 
When men neglect their duty, they may expect to meet with trouble; and if they are not led to repentance and reformation, their troubles will never end.

title: Judges 1:35
text:
Mount Heres; the mountainous regions about Dor. 
 
  Ajalon; a place between Jerusalem and Ekron.   Judges 1:18  
 
  The house of Joseph; his descendents.

title: Judges 1:36
text:
The Amorites; these stand here for the Canaanites generally. 
 
  Akrabbim; a line of hills running across the valley about eight miles south of the Dead sea, here mentioned as the southern border of Palestine. 
 
  The rock; probably Petra, in the mountains of Edom. 
 
  Upward; northward.

title: Judges 2:1
text:
Angel of the Lord; supposed to be the same who appeared to Joshua,  Joshua 5:13  
 
  Bochim; meaning, the weepers, or place of weeping.   Joshua 2:5

title: Judges 2:2
text: Ye have not obeyed; they had not done it fully, or to the extent which he commanded.

title: Judges 2:3
text:
I will not drive them out; as he would have done, had they obeyed him. 
 
The rich and lasting blessings which God promises to the obedient, men often forfeit by their sins.

title: Judges 2:5
text: Sin is the cause of our sorrows, and no tears will remove them, unless we forsake it.

title: Judges 2:7
text: The pious instruction, example, and influence of the aged are of great service to the young, and often keep them from sins that would cause their ruin.

title: Judges 2:9
text: Timnath-heres; called Timnath-serah in  Joshua 24:30 .

title: Judges 2:10
text:
Knew not the Lord; they had not seen his wonders in Egypt, and had not that knowledge of him which led them to love and obey him. 
 
Children, when deprived of the pious influence of parents, often become openly vicious; and nothing but the grace of God is a safeguard against abandonment in wickedness.

title: Judges 2:11
text: Baalim; images of Baal.

title: Judges 2:13
text: Ashtaroth; images of Astarte, a Phenician goddess.

title: Judges 2:14
text:
Sold; delivered. 
 
The woes which sin occasions in this life, are a warning to men not to continue in it, lest it bring upon them woes which will be eternal.

title: Judges 2:16
text:
Judges; rulers and deliverers. 
 
The blessings which God bestows upon men in this world show that he desires that they should repent of their sins, and thus be prepared for endless blessings in the world to come.

title: Judges 2:18
text: It repented the Lord; the meaning is, that he changed his course of conduct towards the Israelites, and instead of keeping them longer in bondage, delivered them.

title: Judges 2:19
text: If men are not led by the mercies of the Lord to repentance, they will become more hardened in sin, and ripen for aggravated ruin.

title: Judges 2:22
text: All the dealings of God with men in this world have a tendency to reveal their true character, show whether they will serve him or not, and prepare them for the retributions of eternity.

title: Judges 2:23
text: Therefore; on account of the sins of the people.

title: Judges 3:3
text:
The Canaanites; those that lived about Zidon. 
 
  Baal-hermon; a region of country near the sources of the Jordan. 
 
  Entering in of Hamath; the pass north through Lebanon, leading to Hamath.

title: Judges 3:5
text:
Among the Canaanites; those of them that were not destroyed. 
 
vv 5-7. 
 
Intimate connections with the wicked increase the temptation to adopt the sentiments and to imitate their example.   Psalms 1:1 Proverbs 1:10-19   I Corinthians 5:9-11

title: Judges 3:6
text: Gods; idols.

title: Judges 3:7
text: The groves; rather, images of Astarte.  See note on  Deuteronomy 16:21 .

title: Judges 3:8
text:
Mesopotamia; the country between the Euphrates and the Tigris. 
 
The calamities which men suffer are expressions of God's displeasure against sin; and when they duly humble themselves before him, and seek his pardoning mercy, their trials while continued will be overruled for good, and in due time will be removed.

title: Judges 3:10
text: Judged; the judges were often military as well as civil governors.

title: Judges 3:13
text:
And he gathered unto him; the king of Moab gathered to himself; that is, took into alliance with himself. 
 
  Ammon and Amalek; Ammon bordered on Moab on the north-east, and Amalek on the south and south-west. 
 
  The city of palm-trees; Jericho.   Deuteronomy 34:3   Though the walls of Jericho were not built till a much later period, it seems to have been early inhabited by the Israelites as an unwalled town.

title: Judges 3:22
text: So that he could not draw; more literally, "for he did not draw." He thrust in the dagger over the haft, and left it there.

title: Judges 3:25
text: They tarried till they were ashamed; were ashamed to wait any longer, lest they should appear to neglect their duty.

title: Judges 3:27
text: Blew a trumpet; as a signal of war.

title: Judges 3:28
text: Fords of Jordan; by which the Moabites in the land of Israel must pass to reach their own land.  Thus he cut off their retreat.

title: Judges 3:29
text: Though the wicked may for a time be successful, and even be used as instruments of correcting and punishing the people of God, yet if they continue in their sins, they will come to a dismal end.  Isaiah 10:5-9

title: Judges 3:30
text: Fourscore; eighty.

title: Judges 3:31
text: Oxgoad; a staff six or eight feet long, with a sharp point of iron on one end for pricking the oxen, and a kind of spade on the other for cleaning the plough.

title: Judges 4:1
text: When restraint is removed, notwithstanding all divine favors men will continue in sin, and often be guilty of the grossest transgressions.

title: Judges 4:2
text: Hazor--Harosheth; cities in the north part of Canaan in and around which many of the remaining Canaanites lived.   Joshua 11:1-11

title: Judges 4:3
text: Oft-repeated iniquities bring upon their perpetrators greatly increased calamities.

title: Judges 4:5
text: Mount Ephraim; the hill country of Ephraim.

title: Judges 4:6
text:
Kedesh-naphtali; so called to distingush it from two other cities called Kedesh, one in Issachar and one in Judah. 
 
  Mount Tabor; on the north-east border of the plain of Jezreel.

title: Judges 4:7
text:
The river Kishon; which rises at the base of mount Tabor, runs through the plain of Jezreel, and empties into the Mediterranean at the bay of Acre. 
 
When men cry unto the Lord in their trouble, he can, and often does grant them relief; and in receiving it they should hear his voice saying, Sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.   John 5:14

title: Judges 4:9
text:
Sell Sisera;  Judges 4:1 
 
Want of confidence in God, and of readiness to undertake that to which he calls, brings dishonor, and deprives men of many blessings which they might otherwise enjoy.

title: Judges 4:10
text:
Called Zebulun and Naphtali; the men of war from those tribes. 
 
  Went up; to mount Tabor.

title: Judges 4:11
text: Had several himself; the Kenites lived in the south part of the country, but Heber had left them and removed to the north.  Judges 1:16 Numbers 21:1 .

title: Judges 4:13
text: Men, from pride and the indulgence of wicked passions, often engage in projects which God designs shall be for their ruin.

title: Judges 4:15
text: Though men are the means, God is the author of success, and to him belongs the glory.

title: Judges 4:16
text: Upon; by.

title: Judges 4:21
text:
Nail of the tent; a large spike or pin, which was driven into the ground to fasten the cords of a tent. 
 
When the enemies of God and the oppressors of his people say, Peace and safety, sudden destruction may come upon them from which there can beno escape.

title: Judges 4:23
text: Things which God in his providence accomplishes through the instrumentality of men, are in the Bible ascribed to him as really as if no agency but his had been employed; and they are also inscribed to men as really as if men alone had performed them; thus showing that divine and human agency harmoniously cooperate, and that men are workers together with God when they obey him and thus work out their salvation, he working in them to will and to do of his own good pleasure.   Philippians 2:12-13

title: Judges 5:2
text:
Offered themselves; to fight against their oppressors. 
 
When delivered from great troubles, or in any way specially favored of the Lord, we should without delay acknowledge his goodness, and render that praise and thanksgiving which are his due.

title: Judges 5:4
text:
Wentest out of Seir--Edom; the mountains of Edom or Seir lay on the north-east of the peninsula of mount Sinai, Paran on the north of it, and Horeb--of which Sinai is a summit--in its bosom.  It was in the region which these mountains represent that God first revealed himself to Moses, and afterwards to the children of Israel.  Hence it is here considered as his dwelling-place, whence he now marches forth in majesty and glory, as he did of old, when he came to deliver Israel from the Egyptians.  Compare  Deuteronomy 33:2 Psalms 68:7-8 Habakkuk 3:3  
 
  The heavens dropped; God's presence is accompanied by tempests of rain, as well as by thunder and earthquakes.  There may be here an allusion to the storm which flooded the Kishon, and swept away the hosts of Sisera.   Judges 5:20-21  
 
Present mercies should remind us of those which are past, and lead us to praise Jehovah for his goodness.

title: Judges 5:6
text:
Shamgar;  Judges 3:1 
  The highways were unoccupied; on account of the danger of travelling.

title: Judges 5:7
text: The villages ceased; were deserted; or, as some render, leaders ceased in Israel; which agrees well with what follows.  And so in  Judges 5:11 .

title: Judges 5:8
text:
New gods; idols as objects of worship. 
 
  Then was war; as a punishment for their idolatry. 
 
  A shield or spear; of these the Israelites were very destitute. 
 
If men forsake God and worship idols, or place their dependence on creatures to the neglect of their Creator, they may expect to be visited with trials, and unless they repent and turn to him, to be overwhelmed in ruin.

title: Judges 5:9
text: The Lord is the author of the good we receive from men as really as what we receive directly form him; and to him pious and grateful minds will give the praise.

title: Judges 5:10
text:
White asses; the kind often used by judges. 
 
  Sit in judgment; or sit upon garments or carpets, as it the manner of oriental judges in administering justice. 
 
The good desire that all, high and low, rich and poor, should unite in praising God for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men.

title: Judges 5:11
text:
From the noise of archers; many prefer to render this verse thus: At the noise [triumphal shout] of those that divide [the spoil,] at the watering-troughs, there shall they rehearse, etc.  The places of drawing water, or watering-troughs, are mentioned as places where the people would naturally assemble. 
 
  Go down to the gates; into the gates of their own cities in peace, after celebrating their victory and deliverance. 
 
The liberty and power to go in and out at pleasure when and where we choose, with none to molest or make us afraid, is a great and precious privilege, for which we are bound to be specially grateful, and which we should earnestly desire may soon be enjoyed by all people.

title: Judges 5:12
text: Lead thy captivity captive; lead forth in triumph the captives whom thou hast taken.

title: Judges 5:13
text:
Him that remaineth; those who remained in Israel. 
 
  The nobles; the chief men of the Canaanites.

title: Judges 5:14
text:
Out of Ephraim--thy people; we may render, Out of Ephraim [came] they whose dwelling is in Amalek; after thee [Ephraim] came Benjamin among thy people; that is, among thy mustered warriors.  By those whose dwelling is in Amalek, we are probably to understand Ephraimites from a region occupied before the conquest of Canaan by Amalekites.  Judges 12:15  
 
  Out of Machir; from the tribe of Manasseh. 
 
  The pen; or rod used by those who mustered men for the army.

title: Judges 5:15
text:
The valley; of Jezreel.   Judges 4:6 Judges 4:14  
 
  For the divisions of Reuben; In the divisions of Reuben, is most literal.  This, in the Hebrew, most naturally signifies the divisions of the water-courses, that is, the brooks, where the Reubenites deliberated and inquired about the war, but did not go to it.

title: Judges 5:17
text:
Remain in ships; Dan, a seafaring people, stayed away from the war to take care of their merchandise.  So with Asher. 
 
  Breaches; rents in the coast, making bays and harbors; hence, simply havens or harbors.

title: Judges 5:19
text: Taanach; a place in the plain of Jezreel.

title: Judges 5:20
text:
From heaven; by pouring down floods of water to destroy the enemy.  Judges 5:21  
 
Human and divine agency, in the production of events, often cooperate; and both should be acknowledged.   Philippians 2:13

title: Judges 5:21
text: Strength; strong and mighty ones.

title: Judges 5:22
text:
Were the horse-hoofs broken; or, the horses' hoofs beat the ground. 
 
  Prancings; their swift running.

title: Judges 5:23
text: Meroz; its location is not now known.

title: Judges 5:25
text: Butter; curdled milk.

title: Judges 5:26
text: Smote off; beat or crushed in.

title: Judges 5:28
text:
The lattice; a blind of open wood-work. 
 
  In coming; in coming back, as she expected he would, victorious over his foes.

title: Judges 5:30
text:
Sped; succeeded in obtaining the victory. 
 
Worldly minds, which relish no enjoyments except those that spring from worldly things, when these are gone will be destitute and wretched.

title: Judges 5:31
text: So; as had Sisera and his host.

title: Judges 6:1
text:
Midian; the Midianites lived east of the south part of Palestine. 
 
Unless the grace of God prevent, men naturally incline to sin, showing that in them, without the grace of God, there is no spiritually good thing.

title: Judges 6:3
text: Amalekites, and the children of the east; neighboring tribes to the Midianites.  By the "children of the east" Arabian tribes seem to be especially intended.

title: Judges 6:4
text:
Gaza; a city of the Philistines in the south-west part of Palestine, on the Mediterranean. 
 
Sin tends to misery, and all the calamities which men suffer are tokens of God's displeasure against it.

title: Judges 6:5
text: To destroy it; take away the means of sustenance.   Judges 6:6

title: Judges 6:7
text: The only hope of deliverance from sin and its consequences is in the Lord; and when men feel this, and cry unto him, he for Christ's sake often appears for their help.

title: Judges 6:10
text:
Fear not the gods; not worship or serve them. 
 
When God is about to grant deliverance to his people, he first convinces them that sin is the cause of their troubles and leads them to forsake it.

title: Judges 6:11
text:
Angel of the Lord; this is supposed to have been the Angel of the covenant, who brought Israel out of Egypt, Jehovah-Jesus.  Judges 6:14 Judges 6:16 Judges 6:23  
 
  Ophrah; a city in the tribe of Benjamin. 
 
  By the wine-press; a retired and covered place, where the Midianites would not be likely to find it.

title: Judges 6:12
text: Providence developes human character.  Many who have been buried for a time in obscurity, have afterwards, by peculiar circumstances, been raised to elevated positions of influence, usefulness, and honor.

title: Judges 6:14
text:
Looked; looked efficaciously.   Luke 22:61  
 
A look from the Lord can nerve the self-diffident for the most perilous services; and fit them, notwithstanding all difficulties, to go on in his name and strength from conquering to conquer.

title: Judges 6:16
text: As one man; as easily and effectually as if there were but one man.

title: Judges 6:17
text: Show me a sign; evidence that it is Jehovah who speaks to me, and that his word will be accomplished.

title: Judges 6:18
text: God is ready to give evidence of his truth to all sincere inquirers who wish to understand his will for the purpose of doing it.

title: Judges 6:24
text:
Shalom; meaning peace. 
 
All the manifestations of God to his believing, obedient people will lead them anew to adore and bless him.

title: Judges 6:25
text: Strong faith in God's word will be tried, and thus fit the believer, by patient continuance in well-doing, to be made victorious and perfect.

title: Judges 6:28
text: The grove; here, as often elsewhere, the Hebrew word rendered "grove" seems to mean a wooden image of Astarte, fixed by a post in the ground.

title: Judges 6:31
text:
Joash said; though he seems to have been a worshipper of Baal, his views may have been changed by what Gideon had told him. 
 
  Whilst it is yet morning; his folly in pleading for Baal, who, if really a God, ought to take care of himself.  Joash said this to dissuade the people from their purpose. 
 
Idolatry so debases men, and renders them so foolish, that they will worship, and sometimes try to help gods that have no power to help themselves.

title: Judges 6:32
text: Jerubbaal; that is, let Baal plead.

title: Judges 6:34
text:
Abi-ezer; the family of his father, and his relatives. 
 
If men are to be fitted for good, great, and noble deeds, it must be through the influences of the Spirit of God.  Wisdom, strength, courage, energy, and perseverance are his gifts, and to him they should, by all who possess them, be heartily devoted.

title: Judges 6:37
text: Evidence of the presence and favor of God, and a conviction of being engaged in his work, support the soul under trials, arm it for conflicts, and prepare it, notwithstanding all difficulties and dangers, in his name to triumph.

title: Judges 7:1
text:
Jerubbaal;  Judges 6:1 
  Harod; on the borders of Issachar, not far from mount Gilboa. 
 
  Moreh; near the valley of Jezreel. 
 
To obtain the blessings which God has promised, men must not only rely on him, but must employ those means which he has appointed, and in the use of which alone they have reason to expect success.

title: Judges 7:2
text:
Vaunt; boast. 
 
The means by which, and the manner in which God accomplishes the purposes of his grace, are adapted to show men that the glory of their successes belongs not to them, but to him.

title: Judges 7:3
text: Mount Gilead; the range of mountains usually so called was on the east of Jordan, but some have supposed that there might be an eminence called by this name on the west of Jordan, where Gideon was.

title: Judges 7:5
text: Lappeth of the water; from his hand, having raised it to his mouth.  Judges 7:6

title: Judges 7:7
text: The power of God's visible people depends not so much on their number as on their character; and sometimes a diminution of their number may give them increased strength.

title: Judges 7:8
text: The valley; the valley of Jezreel.

title: Judges 7:10
text: When God has a work for any one to accomplish, he will prepare him to perform it.

title: Judges 7:13
text: Tumbled into the host; it is represented as rolling down from the hill Moreh, where Gideon was, into the valley where were the Midianites, overturning their tents and prostrating all that was in its way.

title: Judges 7:14
text: This is--the sword of Gideon; meaning, it represents it, showing that the literal meaning of words is often not their true meaning.

title: Judges 7:15
text:
Worshipped; bowed himself in grateful reverence before God for giving him this encouragement to go down against the Midianites. 
 
If by a dream, or any other means, one is encouraged to obey the revealed will of God, and strengthened for the performance of known duty, he has reason to be grateful and anew to acknowledge and adore God.

title: Judges 7:16
text: Lamps; torches.  These were often made of pitchwood, which was easily kindled, and gave a brilliant light.

title: Judges 7:18
text: The agency of God and that of men are both employed in the accomplishment of his designs.  There is therefore no good reason to imagine that there is any inconsistency between them.   Judges 7:22

title: Judges 7:19
text: The middle watch; they divided the night into three equal parts called watches.  The Jews afterwards divided it into four.

title: Judges 7:22
text: Beth-shittah--Tabbath; supposed to be places towards Jordan, which the Midianites must cross to get into their own country.  Judges 7:24

title: Judges 7:24
text:
Beth-barah; supposed to be the same as Beth-abara,  John 1:28 . It means, a place of passage, and lay on the east side of Jordan where they crossed the river. 
 
  Took the waters; guarded the fording-places where they expected the Midianites would cross.

title: Judges 7:25
text: The rock Oreb; so called, it is supposed, from the fact of his having been killed upon it.  So with the wine-press.

title: Judges 8:1
text: Those who neglect their duty are often disposed to cast the blame on others; and those who refuse to engage in great and important services, are often most anxious to have the credit of them.

title: Judges 8:2
text:
The gleaning--the vintage; Gideon, of the house of Abi-ezer, and his men, who had struck the first blow, are compared to those who gather the vintage; while the Ephraimites, who came after him, are compared to gleaners.  But here Gideon tells them that the gleaning of the grapes is more than the original vintage.  This was a soft answer, designed to appease the wrath of the Ephraimites.  Proverbs 15:1 Ecclesiastes 10:4  
 
A command of one's temper, and a disposition to give full credit to the worthy actions of others, are likely means of appeasing envy, abating wrath, and causing contentions to cease.

title: Judges 8:5
text: Succoth; a city in the tribe of Gad, on the east of Jordan, below the sea of Galilee.   Genesis 33:17

title: Judges 8:6
text:
Now in thy hand; have you already taken them?   Judges 8:15   They were men of worldly prudence, but without either faith in God or devotion to his cause; and would not assist Gideon till they were first sure of his success. 
 
It is unwise to refuse aid to brethren in distress, and foolish as well as wicked to upbraid them.

title: Judges 8:7
text: Tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness; a mode of punishment not uncommon in those days.

title: Judges 8:8
text: Penuel; east of Succoth, and near the river Jabbok.   Genesis 32:30

title: Judges 8:9
text: This tower; one to which the men of Penuel trusted for their defence.

title: Judges 8:10
text:
Karkor; supposed to have been eastward of Penuel, and near the borders of Gad. 
 
The multitudes who have fallen in wars by the hands of their fellow men, and in the indulgence of the most hateful passions, present an impressive view of the evil of sin, and of the horrible state of those who are abandoned to its everlasting power.

title: Judges 8:11
text:
Nobah is the same as Kenath, and is supposed to be the same as the modern Kanatha in Hauran. 
 
  Jogbehah was in its neighborhood.

title: Judges 8:14
text: Described unto him; literally, wrote for him; probably gave him their names.

title: Judges 8:16
text:
Taught the men; showed them the folly of their course by punishing them. 
 
Sin often brings misery in this world of mercy, as it will, to all who continue in it, in the world of retribution.

title: Judges 8:21
text:
So is his strength; as his age was mature, so was his strength. 
 
The dread which men have of a lingering and dishonorable temporal death, should prompt them to immediate, earnest, and persevering efforts to avoid the disgrace and torment of that which is eternal.

title: Judges 8:23
text:
The Lord shall rule; he was their chief magistrate, and Gideon would not be instrumental in changing that form of government. 
 
A wise man will not covet an increase of power, care, and responsibility; nor, unless it appears to be manifestly the will of God, will he consent to receive it.

title: Judges 8:24
text:
Ear-rings of his prey; those which they had taken from their enemies. 
 
  Ishmaelites; the Midianites are sometimes confounded with Ishmaelites; they lived near, and often mingled together.  Genesis 37:28

title: Judges 8:27
text:
An ephod; a very rich and costly garment, such as was worn by the high-priest.   Exodus 28:4  
 
  A whoring after it; it became a means of superstition and idolatry. 
 
The consequences of men's actions may be very different from what they anticipate; they should not, therefore, at any time lean to their own understandings, but should in all their ways acknowledge God, that he may direct their paths.

title: Judges 8:31
text: A departure from the design and will of God in the institution of marriage, has in some form ever been the easily besetting sin of men, and the source of innumerable and most distressing calamities.

title: Judges 8:33
text:
Baalim and--Baal-berith; idol-gods. 
 
No sooner are restraints removed, than men show their wickedness by voluntarily engaging in known sin, and the manifestation of awful ingratitude towards both God and men.

title: Judges 9:1
text: Shechem; a city in the tribe of Ephraim, lying between mount Gerizim on the south, and mount Ebal on the north.

title: Judges 9:2
text:
Your bone; a Shechemite and a relative.   Judges 8:31  
 
Men who earnestly desire power, and flatter their fellow men to obtain it, are not worthy to be trusted, and should not be chosen to rule over others.

title: Judges 9:3
text: Men are easily flattered, and their judgment, feelings, and conduct often biassed towards those who are related to or connected with them.

title: Judges 9:4
text:
House of Baal-berith; the place of their idol-worship. 
 
Vain and light persons, the vicious and the worthless of all descriptions, will prostitute their political influence to the support of those flatterers who like themselves are vicious, and who will furnish them with money.

title: Judges 9:5
text: Ambitious men, who are given up of God to the gratification of their lusts, will commit any crime to secure their selfish objects.

title: Judges 9:6
text:
House of Millo; a tower or castle in the city.  It seems to have been the same as "the tower of Sechem,"  Judges 9:46-47 .  The men of Shechem and the house of Millo are separately mentioned in Jotham's curse, and, in like manner, the destruction of the men of Shechem and the men of the tower of Shechem is separately recorded. 
 
When a people choose immoral men as their rulers, they will generally be made instruments of mutual punishment to each other.

title: Judges 9:7
text: Gerizim; a mountain on the south side of Shechem.

title: Judges 9:8
text:
The trees went forth; this is the commencement of a parable, representing the folly of the Shechemites in making Abimelech king. 
 
Parables may be a most effective and useful method of inculcating divine truth, and he who wisely employs them be an eminent benefactor of mankind.

title: Judges 9:9
text:
Olive-tree; a tree yielding oil, used not only in food, but also in the worship of God and in the consecration of men to public office. 
 
Wise men will not be anxious to leave the safe, quiet, and useful pursuits and enjoyments of private life, for the sake of becoming rulers, especially over the wicked.

title: Judges 9:13
text: Wine, which cheereth God; it was employed in his worship, and thus pleased him.

title: Judges 9:14
text: The bramble; one of the meanest and most worthless shrubs.  Gideon, who like the olive, fig-tree, and vine, was useful, refused; but Abimelech, who like the bramble was worthless, consented to be made king.

title: Judges 9:15
text:
Let fire come out; this expressed the trouble which Abimelech would bring upon the chief men of Shechem, represented as cedars. 
 
Those who are most unfaithful and worthless in private life, are often most anxious for promotion to public life; and those who thus promote them, may expect through them to reap the fruit of their folly.

title: Judges 9:16
text: Truly; rightly, in a proper manner.

title: Judges 9:19
text: Teachers of divine truth in all ages have maintained that godliness is profitable unto all things, and that the way of transgressors is hard; that righteousness tendeth to life; and that those who continue in wickedness do it to their own death.

title: Judges 9:20
text: Let fire come out; fire will come out; expressive of the mutual calamities which Abimelech and the men of Shechem would bring on each other.

title: Judges 9:21
text: Beer; a place south of Shechem.

title: Judges 9:23
text:
God sent; suffered, through the temptation of Satan to arise in their own hearts. 
 
The wicked have no permanent bond of union, safety, or peace; and those who have been treacherous and cruel to others, will ordinarily meet with others who will be treacherous and cruel to them.

title: Judges 9:25
text: Liers in wait; to kill Abimelech, who was then absent from the city, or to take him prisoner on his return.

title: Judges 9:26
text:
Gaal; supposed to be a Canaanite, pretending to have descended from Hamor the father of Shechem, and former prince of that country.  Judges 9:28 Genesis 34:2  
 
Men may rebel against one set of wicked rulers, and yet choose another who are no better; and, by so doing, may only increase their distress and hasten their ruin.

title: Judges 9:27
text:
Their god; their idol-god.   Judges 8:33  
 
Dissipation, rioting, and licentiousness are not true liberty, and those who indulge in them can never enjoy it.

title: Judges 9:28
text:
Who is Abimelech; that he should reign over the ancient and renowned city of Shechem. 
 
  Zebul; the governor of Shechem during Abimelech's absence.  Judges 9:30  
 
Boasting, pride, and self-esteem are forerunners of defeat, degradation, and contempt.

title: Judges 9:29
text:
Said to Abimelech; that is, by messengers, for Abimelech himself was absent from the city. 
 
  Increase--come out; a challenge to Abimelech to make his army as strong as possible, and meet him on the field of battle.

title: Judges 9:31
text: Sent messengers--privily; because he was not strong enough to offer direct resistance to Gaal, who had won over the people of the city to his side.

title: Judges 9:37
text:
Middle of the land; rather, height of the land; that is, from the high hills bordering Shechem.  See note to  Judges 9:1 . 
 
  The plain of Meonenim; rather, the oak of Meonenim; that is, in English, the enchanters' oak.

title: Judges 9:38
text: Those who pretend to despise their enemies when at a distance, are often afraid of them when they come near; and the most reproachful in time of safety, are often most cowardly in time of danger.

title: Judges 9:41
text: Arumah; a place near Shechem.

title: Judges 9:43
text:
He; Abimelech. 
 
  Took; had taken.

title: Judges 9:45
text:
Sowed it with salt; in token of its desolation. 
 
The men who aid and exalt the wicked, are often the men who are injured and destroyed by them.

title: Judges 9:46
text: The courses which wicked men take to secure their safety not unfrequently accelerate their ruin; and often by those whom they have aided in slaying others, they are themselves slain.

title: Judges 9:48
text: Zalmon; meaning shady; supposed to be so called from its being covered with forests.

title: Judges 9:50
text: Thebez; a city of Ehpraim, a few miles north-east of Shechem.

title: Judges 9:51
text: A strong tower; such towers in or near cities, to which the people fled in time of danger, were common.

title: Judges 9:52
text: Success often renders men reckless, and when they are most confident they are nearest to destruction.  They may escape the greatest apparent dangers, and then fall by such as are not thought of.

title: Judges 9:53
text:
A millstone; the upper stone of a hand-mill, in which the women ground their grain.   Matthew 24:41  
 
  All-to; an old English term meaning, wholly, entirely.

title: Judges 9:54
text:
A woman slew him; to be slain by a woman was considered disgraceful. 
 
Men, especially warriors, think much about an honorable death and sometimes are peculiarly sensitive of their reputation when sinking into shame and everlasting contempt.

title: Judges 9:56
text:
