Rendered; requited or punished.   Judges 9:5 Judges 9:18 Judges 9:24  
 
Jehovah is a God that judgeth in the earth, and often here proclaims the sins of men in their punishment.

title: Judges 9:57
text: The curse of Jotham;  Judges 9:1

title: Judges 10:1
text:
He dwelt in Shamir; after he became judge; as this was a more central part of the country, and a more convenient place for a judge than any in his own tribe. 
 
Good rulers are the gift of God, and are designed, through the enactment and execution of good laws, to be for the protection and defence of the people.

title: Judges 10:3
text: A Gileadite; he was the first judge from the east side of Jordan.

title: Judges 10:4
text: Havoth-jair; the villages of Jair.

title: Judges 10:6
text: Though a course of sinning has often been tried, and always found to lead in the end to misery, yet such is the folly and wickedness of men, that they will try it again with as much eagerness and confidence of success, as if the experiment had never been made.

title: Judges 10:7
text: Philistines; they lived on the west of the Israelites, and the children of Ammon on the east.

title: Judges 10:8
text:
That year; the oppression of both began about the same time.  That part of the Ammonites lasted eighteen years, and that of the Philistines forty.   Judges 13:1  
 
  Other; east.

title: Judges 10:10
text: Men who in prosperity cast off the fear of the Lord, and openly rebel against him, in adversity, and when suffering the effects of their sins, often feel their need of his help.

title: Judges 10:12
text: The Moabites; probably an Arabian tribe.

title: Judges 10:13
text: I will deliver you no more; he would not, unless they should repent of their sins.

title: Judges 10:14
text: Cry unto the gods; this was designed to make them feel more deeply the worthlessness of their idols, and their need of help from Jehovah.

title: Judges 10:15
text: Though God might justly leave men to the consequences of their transgressions and never again deliver them, yet when they feel and acknowledge his righteousness, and turn heartily to him, he has compassion on them and opens the way for their relief.

title: Judges 10:17
text:
In Gilead; on the east of Jordan. 
 
  Mizpeh; near mount Gilead.   Judges 11:29

title: Judges 11:2
text:
A strange woman; not the lawful wife of his father. 
 
As the sins of parents may greatly injure and distress their children, this should be a motive to induce them to govern all their appetites and passions, and to regulate their whole conduct according to the revealed will of God.

title: Judges 11:3
text: The land of Tob; supposed to be in or near Syria.

title: Judges 11:7
text: In prosperity men often despise and reject those to whom in adversity they are glad to apply for help.

title: Judges 11:9
text: Arrangements in which different parties are concerned should be plainly and correctly stated beforehand, that there may be afterwards no misunderstandings and contests about them.

title: Judges 11:10
text: The Lord be witness; this was a solemn engagement that they would make Jephthah their ruler.

title: Judges 11:11
text: All his words; the words of the engagement between him and the elders of Gilead, that the people might all hear, understand, and ratify them.

title: Judges 11:12
text: For the wicked courses which wicked men pursue they can give no good reason; and a correct statement of facts shows that for their pretended reasons there is no just foundation.

title: Judges 11:13
text: Israel took away my land;  Numbers 21:21-35:1

title: Judges 11:21
text: The agency of God should never be excluded in our contemplations of the affairs of men, and his goodness should always be acknowledged as the source of all the blessings which we enjoy.

title: Judges 11:22
text: The coasts of the Amorites; the Amorites had dispossessed the Ammonites and taken their country, from Arnon to Jabbok, before the children of Israel came out of Egypt; and the Israelites took it not from the Ammonites, to whom they ascribed their successes.

title: Judges 11:24
text: Chemosh; the idol-god of the Ammonites, to whom they ascribed their successes.

title: Judges 11:25
text: Better than Balak; had they any better claim to the lands than had Balak, who was king of Moab when Israel took them?  He did not take them back; and as the Ammonites had not attempted it, but suffered the Israelites to possess it unmolested for three hundred years, it was evident that they had lost all title to it, and the Israelites did not wrong them in possessing it.

title: Judges 11:27
text:
The Lord--be judge; decide, by giving the victory to those who were right. 
 
A disposition in the use of proper means to commit all our concerns to the guidance and disposal of God, is a good preparation for obtaining his favor, and receiving from him all needed aid.

title: Judges 11:29
text:
The Spirit--came upon Jephthah; furnishing him with wisdom, courage, and all needful qualifications to conduct the war. 
 
  Over; through the places mentioned, to collect his army.

title: Judges 11:31
text:
Be the Lord's; devoted especially to his service. 
 
  And; some have translated this, or; supposing that what should come to meet Jephthah was to be a burnt-offering, if it were an object which the law allowed for that purpose; and if not, that it was to be devoted to God in some other way. 
 
We should be careful to promise nothing but what is practicable, lawful, and right, that all we promise may be faithfully performed.

title: Judges 11:33
text:
Aroer; a town near the river Arnon. 
 
  Minnith; a place north of Aroer, in the tribe of Reuben.

title: Judges 11:35
text:
Opened my mouth; made a vow.   Judges 11:30  
 
This life is a mixed scene of trials and mercies.  Great blessings are often followed by great distresses; and if uncalled of God and without good reason we have brought them upon ourselves, the poignancy of them is thereby increased.

title: Judges 11:37
text:
My virginity; that she was to live and die without being married and having children, which Jewish women very much regreted.  If, as some suppose, she was not literally offered to the Lord as a burnt-offering, it is plain, from the language of the sacred writer, that she was devoted to God in such a way as required her to remain unmarried and childless. 
 
  Fellows; female companions.

title: Judges 11:39
text:
According to his vow; he devoted her to the Lord in a manner consistent with his promise, whatever that was. 
 
  She knew no man; was never married, and had no children; a thing bewailed and lamented both by herself and her companions.

title: Judges 11:40
text: Lament; this word in the original means, to celebrate, or rehearse, and is so translated in  Judges 5:11 .  The daughters of Israel, from year to year, commemorated the case of Jephthah's daughter.

title: Judges 12:1
text:
Went northward; towards Mizpeh, on the east side of Jordan, where Jephthah lived. 
 
Persons who have refused to engage in great and difficult services themselves, often most bitterly envy those who have successfully performed them.

title: Judges 12:2
text: Ye delivered me not; did not attempt it.

title: Judges 12:3
text:
Put my life in my hands; took on myself the work and danger of attempting to obtain deliverance. 
 
Men are sometimes called, instead of depending on others, to take themselves the responsibility, meet the dangers, and perform the labors of great and trying emergencies.  In such cases they should not shrink, but in dependence on God go forward in duty, and leave the result to him.

title: Judges 12:4
text:
Fugitives of Ephraim; the Gileadites belonged to the tribe of Manasseh.   Joshua 17:1   The Ephraimites reproach them as a remnant who had fled before themselves across the Jordan, and who were unworthy to be ranked with their brethren of Ephraim and Manasseh. 
 
Family contentions are most bitter and disastrous.  The beginning of them should be most carefully avoided, for when once begun no one can tell where they will end.

title: Judges 12:6
text:
Forty and two thousand; supposed by many to mean two thousand and forty, as the Ephraimites when numbered amounted only to thirty-two thousand five hundred.   Numbers 26:37   But this reason cannot be regarded as conclusive, since the numbering referred to took place three hundred years before. 
 
Those who wickedly begin a quarrel, would often be struck with horror should they foresee all its consequences.

title: Judges 12:7
text: As death is to all persons near, and after death is the judgment, the great object of all should be so to live as to be fitted, through grace, to give up their account with joy, and enter into that rest which remains for the people of God.

title: Judges 12:10
text: Bethlehem; there were two places of this name, one in Zebulun, and one in Judah where our Saviour was born.

title: Judges 12:13
text: A Pirathonite; so called from Pirathon the place where he lived.

title: Judges 12:14
text: Nephews; in the original, sons' sons, or grandsons.

title: Judges 12:15
text: Mount of the Amalekites; supposed to be a place in Ephraim called by that name.   Judges 5:14

title: Judges 13:1
text: Forty years;  Judges 10:1

title: Judges 13:2
text: Zorah; a city in the south part of the tribe of Dan.

title: Judges 13:3
text:
The angel of the Lord; supposed to be the Angel-Jehovah, in the form of man, and the same who appeared to Moses, Joshua, and Gideon.  Judges 13:21-23  
Our mercies and our trials are perfectly known to God, and he can so adapt his favors as in the best way and time to supply our wants.|

title: Judges 13:4
text: Children are the gift of God, and parents should take such a course as is best adapted to fit them for his service.

title: Judges 13:5
text: Nazarite; for the law of the Nazarite, which Manoah's wife was herself to observe till the birth of the child, see  Numbers 6:2-21 .

title: Judges 13:6
text: Husbands and wives should avail themselves of each other's counsel, and thus unite their efforts, especially in every thing pertaining to the temporal and eternal welfare of their children.

title: Judges 13:8
text: One of the most important and difficult duties of parents is the right education of children; and no one will ever properly perform it, unless in the habit of daily seeking wisdom from God.

title: Judges 13:9
text: When parents ask direction from God how to treat their children, in order most to honor him, to benefit them, and, make them useful to others, God is ready to hear and to aid them in training their children in the way the should go.

title: Judges 13:12
text: How shall we order the child? or, what shall be the manner of the child?  The question relates to the mother's deportment before his birth, as immediately explained by the angel.

title: Judges 13:13
text: To be successful in the right education of children, parents must give heed to the directions of God on this subject; and if they would lead their children to obey him, they must be careful to set them the example.

title: Judges 13:15
text: The mercies of God bestowed on our children should increase our sense of obligation, and lead us to offer to him the sacrifices of praise and thanksgiving.

title: Judges 13:18
text:
Secret; wonderful; the same in the original as in  Isaiah 9:6 . 
 
God manifest in the flesh is indeed, The Wonderful; and while we should receive with implicit confidence all that he reveals concerning himself, we should not seek to know what we cannot and do not need to understand.

title: Judges 13:20
text: The Lord is wonderful, not only in his nature and perfections, but in his operations; and they should inspire us not only with reverence and awe, but with admiration, confidence, and love.

title: Judges 13:25
text:
In the camp of Dan; or, in Mahaneh-dan, the name of a certain place, the origin of which is given in  Judges 18:12 . 
 
  Zorah--Eshtaol; in the south part of Dan.

title: Judges 14:1
text:
Timnath; then held by the Philistines. 
 
On no subject connected with human welfare does a young man need divine guidance more than in selecting a wife.

title: Judges 14:2
text: It is ordinarily wise for a young man, before engaging to marry any one, to consult his parents and avail himself of the benefits of their advice.

title: Judges 14:3
text: All wise parents will desire that their children should marry those who are pious and who are connected with religious families.

title: Judges 14:4
text:
Of the Lord; to overrule this transaction for avenging the wrongs inflicted by the Philistines, and beginning to deliver the Israelites from their power.   Judges 13:5  
 
While parents should advise their children and give them good counsel on the subject of marriage, yet after they become of age they should not undertake to control them.  They do not know enough about the designs of God with regard to such connections, to render such control either safe or proper.

title: Judges 14:5
text: When the course of children with regard to marriage is settled, parents should endeavor to make the best of it, and to render it as useful and comfortable as possible.

title: Judges 14:6
text: If a young man is under the direction of the Spirit of God, and is aided by him, though he may meet with great difficulties and dangers, he will be enabled to overcome them.

title: Judges 14:8
text: It is often useful to review the scenes in which God has especially favored us and enabled us to overcome the dangers to which we were exposed.

title: Judges 14:9
text: A generous mind does not wish to enjoy its blessings alone, and its happiness is increased by imparting them to others, especially to parents, relatives, and friends; but there are some things the knowledge of which a wise man will keep to himself and not impart to any other.

title: Judges 14:10
text: Marriage is a joyful occasion, and it is proper gratefully to notice it by feasting.  But in feasting there is peculiar danger, not only of being betrayed into excesses, but of forgetting God and sinning against him.  All therefore, when so exposed, should seek his protection and guidance.

title: Judges 14:11
text:
They; the people of Timnath. 
 
Virtuous companions are great blessings, and vicious ones are great curses.

title: Judges 14:12
text:
Put forth a riddle; this was a common amusement on such occasions. 
 
  Thirty sheets; the word in the original means shirts or linen, worn next the body. 
 
  Garments; the outer garments, worn over the shirts. 
 
When in company with the frivolous and wicked we are tempted, especially after feasting, to become like them, and to engage in their frivolous or even wicked sports.  But nothing should receive the sanction of our example, except what is moral in its nature and useful in its effects.

title: Judges 14:13
text: The pledging of property on contingencies the results of which we cannot foresee, and which render us liable to give or receive an amount without an equivalent, is wrong.  By encouraging idleness, and leading men to the wide extremes of high expectation and sore disappointment, it tends greatly to injure them, and should be conscientiously avoided.

title: Judges 14:15
text:
Called us; invited us to the feast. 
 
The hope of gain without laboring or rendering an equivalent, the fear of loss, and the desire to prevent it, have tempted many to the commission of enormous crimes.

title: Judges 14:17
text:
The seven days; that is, the rest of the seven days of the feast that remained after the third. 
 
We cannot be sure that others will keep a secret which we cannot keep ourselves, as their temptation to divulge it may be greater than ours. If we would therefore not have a thing known, we should not reveal it.

title: Judges 14:18
text:
Ploughed with my heifer; persuaded his wife to tell them. 
 
Intimate companionship with the wicked exposes to the most disastrous results, and by it, from the highest mirth, men may be plunged into the deepest sorrow.

title: Judges 14:19
text: Ashkelon; a city of the Philistines, southwest of Timnath and north of Gaza.

title: Judges 14:20
text:
His friend; the person who had the direction at the marriage-feast; called by way of eminence the friend of the bridegroom.   John 3:29  
 
One wrong step opens the way for another, and when a woman betrays her husband, he has no security that she will not forsake him.  There is no safety but in avoiding the beginning of evil.

title: Judges 15:1
text:
The time of wheat-harvest; in May. 
 
  A kid; as a present, and in token of reconciliation. 
 
Those who have been wronged or offended should ever be ready to forgive, and take all suitable measures for reconciliation with those who have wronged or offended them.   Matthew 6:12-15

title: Judges 15:2
text: The friendship of the wicked is sometimes more hazardous than their enmity, and the course they propose to remove one difficulty often plunges those who follow it into a greater.

title: Judges 15:3
text: If there must be a contest, we should be careful not ourselves to be the sinful cause of it.

title: Judges 15:4
text: Foxes; the original word includes also jackals, which are abundant in Palestine, and easily caught.

title: Judges 15:6
text: By doing wrong to avoid an evil, we take a course which will bring upon us either that or something worse.

title: Judges 15:8
text:
Top; fissure, cleft, or cavern. 
 
  Etam; supposed to be south of Timnath, in the tribe of Judah.

title: Judges 15:9
text: Lehi; the place where Samson with a jawbone smote the Philistines, and on that account called Lehi, which means, in Hebrew, jawbone.  Judges 15:15-17

title: Judges 15:11
text: The professed friends of God may be so besotted and debased by sin as to join with his enemies, and oppose those who would save them and their children from degradation and ruin.

title: Judges 15:14
text: The triumph of the wicked is short, and when they are most confident of success they are often nearest to destruction.

title: Judges 15:16
text: The weakest and most contemptible instruments may become mighty through God to the destruction of the most powerful of his foes.

title: Judges 15:18
text: Great successes are often, in the course of providence, followed by great trials, that all who have been favored may feel their dependence on God and their constant need of his help.

title: Judges 15:19
text:
In the jaw; or, in Lehi.  Compare  Judges 15:9 .  That this latter is the right rendering appears from the fact that a permanent fountain was produced by this interposition of God, which continued to flow in the writer's day. 
 
  En-hakkore; fountain of him that called, that is, upon God in prayer. 
 
When men are sensible of their insufficiency, and look up with a humble, believing, and affectionate heart to God, he is able and willing to help them and cause them to raise a permanent memorial to his praise.

title: Judges 16:1
text:
Gaza; the capital of the southern district of the Philistines. 
 
Many men distinguished by special favors have fallen victims to the blandishments of vicious women, and from their wiles none, without the keeping of God, can be safe.

title: Judges 16:2
text: No one, when tempted to the commission of sin, can yield to the temptation without exposing himself to be destroyed.

title: Judges 16:3
text:
Before; in front of. 
 
The punishment of sin is often delayed for a season; but in due time, if men repent not, it will come upon them, and there will be no escape.

title: Judges 16:4
text:
Sorek; probably near the borders of Dan and the Philistines. 
 
Yielding to temptation increases its power.

title: Judges 16:5
text:
Eleven hundred pieces of silver; more than two thousand dollars. 
 
Tempters to sin often become tormentors; and those who yield to their enticements, may expect to partake of their plagues.

title: Judges 16:7
text: The farther men go in transgression, the greater the difficulties of escaping from it; and those who try to deceive others, tempt others to deceive them.

title: Judges 16:9
text:
In the chamber; in another apartment of the chamber. 
 
God is long-suffering, and often continues his favors to the guilty, not willing that they should perish, but that they should come to repentance.

title: Judges 16:10
text: Mocked; deceived.

title: Judges 16:13
text:
Seven locks; braids or plaits in which his hair may have been arranged. 
 
  Web; the cloth in the loom which Delilah was perhaps weaving.

title: Judges 16:14
text:
Pin of the beam; rather, pin of the braiding; that is, to which the braided locks with the web were fastened. 
 
Though lying may relieve a man for a moment, yet instead of getting him out of trouble, or in the end benefiting him, it will only plunge him into deeper sorrows.

title: Judges 16:16
text: Importunity has great influence both with man and with God, and much depends upon resolute, earnest, untiring perseverance.   Luke 11:8

title: Judges 16:17
text:
If I be shaven; in losing his hair, he would lose the badge of his Nazariteship and the strength connected with it. 
 
Those who persist in a course of sinning, will soon find themselves weak, helpless, and undone.

title: Judges 16:19
text: Her knees; as his pillow.

title: Judges 16:20
text: Men without the aid of God, are not aware of their helpless condition till they learn it by experience.

title: Judges 16:21
text:
Did grind; this was done by turning round a stone with the hands, and was, for a man, a degrading employment. 
 
Those senses which have been the inlets of iniquity often become the organs of punishment.

title: Judges 16:23
text: The fall of the professed friends of God greatly dishonors him, injures his cause, and gives the wicked occasion to reproach and triumph.

title: Judges 16:25
text:
Made them sport; was the subject of their sports. 
 
  The pillars; two central pillars near to each other, on which the building mainly rested.

title: Judges 16:27
text: The triumph of the wicked is short, and the height of their joys is the prelude of their ruin.   Psalms 73:18-20

title: Judges 16:28
text: Even the loss of eyesight, great as is the calamity, may be to a man the means of unspeakable good.  If it lead him to repentance of his sins and faith in Jesus Christ, though his grave be with the wicked, his resurrection will be with the just.

title: Judges 17:2
text: Covetousness often increases with age, so that the less a man has to hope for from the world, the more he cleaves to it.

title: Judges 17:3
text: What some people call dedication to Jehovah may be a violation of his law and an utter abomination in his sight.

title: Judges 17:5
text:
Teraphim; household images, or idol-gods. 
 
The wickedness of parents is often aided and imitated by their children, and thus those who should seek each other's salvation, promote each other's destruction.

title: Judges 17:6
text: The want of wise, efficient, and good civil government is a great calamity to a people; and that may seem right to ignorant, wicked men, which is a palpable and open violation of the law of God.

title: Judges 17:7
text:
Beth-lehem-judah; so called to distinguish it from Bethlehem in Zebulun. 
 
  Of the family; the city was in the tribe of Judah. 
 
Men may have an outward consecration to the service of God, and yet in heart and in practice be ready to unite with his enemies.

title: Judges 17:9
text: Men who rove about without any regular and stated employment are generally worthless, and ready, for money, to unite with others in open wickedness.

title: Judges 17:10
text: A father; a guardian, guide, and director in spiritual things.

title: Judges 17:12
text:
Consecrated the Levite; set him apart to the office of a priest. 
 
Many choose both gods and ministers of their own making, and depend for acceptance with Jehovah upon a religion which he abhors.

title: Judges 18:1
text:
Those days; the times referred to in the preceding chapter.  Judges 17:1-13  
 
  Had not fallen unto them; it had been allotted to them, but they had not gotten possession of all of it.   Judges 1:34 Joshua 19:40 Joshua 19:47

title: Judges 18:2
text:
Zorah, and--Eshtaol; towns or districts in the tribe of Dan.  Judges 13:2  
 
  Search the land; for a place to which a portion of the tribe might migrate. 
 
If men were as sensible of their spiritual wants as they are of their temporal, and as earnest and persevering in providing for them, they might all be made rich for eternity.   Proverbs 2:3-5

title: Judges 18:3
text:
Knew the voice of the young man; they were before acquainted with him, or knew from his speech who he was. 
 
  Makest; doest.

title: Judges 18:5
text: Wicked man often have some conviction of their dependence on God, and ask others to seek for them his blessing.

title: Judges 18:6
text: Before the Lord is your way; he regards it, and will prosper it.

title: Judges 18:7
text:
Laish; a town or district in the north of Palestine, at the foot of mount Lebanon and near the source of the Jordan; called also Leshem,  Joshua 19:47 . 
 
  No business with any man; no public connection or conversation with any people from whom they could expect protection and defence. 
 
Those who are without civil government are destitute of the means which God has appointed to restrain the wicked and encourage the good, and to protect the one from the aggressions of the other.

title: Judges 18:9
text: Power to take possession of a good land does not give men a right to it, nor is their success any evidence that God approves of their conduct.  He may in wrath suffer them to rob others, and that robbery may prepare the way for their own ruin.

title: Judges 18:12
text:
In; near. 
 
  Mahaneh-dan; the camp of Dan; the same place as that mentioned in  Judges 13:25 .  This encampment of the Danites took place before Samson's birth. 
 
  Behind; on the west side.

title: Judges 18:14
text:
Consider; whether it is not best for you to rob Micah of his images. 
 
Consideration and cool deliberate calculation in iniquity increase its guilt, and manifest great hardness of heart.

title: Judges 18:17
text: Rebellion against God and injustice towards men go together, and no ties of relationship or experience of kindness will lead the wicked ever to make it their object to do to others as they would that others should do to them.

title: Judges 18:19
text: Lay thy hand upon thy mouth; say nothing.

title: Judges 18:20
text: The great object of false teachers is worldly good; the prospect of this, though by conniving at and sharing in flagrant wickedness, makes them glad.

title: Judges 18:21
text:
The carriage; the baggage, consisting of such movables as men emigrating with their families must take with them. 
 
  Before them; in the front part of their train, that thus they might be secure against an attack on the part of Micah and his friends.

title: Judges 18:24
text: Idols can afford their worshippers no help; and were not the human mind awfully blinded, and the heart besotted by sin, no one would expect it from them.

title: Judges 18:25
text: Robbery prepares men for murder, and those who feel and act as if might gave right, will commit any enormity.

title: Judges 18:28
text:
Zidon; a populous city on the Mediterranean. 
 
  Beth-rehob; a place west of Laish.

title: Judges 18:30
text:
Set up the graven image; thus idolatry was first publicly established in Israel. 
 
Satan, in his worship, is willing men should use robbery for burnt-offerings; but Jehovah in his worship abhors it.  Idolatry begun by few may spread to many, and ultimately prove the ruin of all.

title: Judges 19:1
text: When there is no regular, efficient civil government, such is human nature, that crimes of all descriptions will abound and the wicked triumph.

title: Judges 19:6
text: Hospitality and kindness to friends are highly commendable, but we should not urge them against their convenience and to the neglect of their duties.

title: Judges 19:7
text: We should never let kindness and importunity overcome our judgment.  If we do, by the evils which spring from it we may, when too late, be taught our folly.  Multitudes have suffered for want of the habit of saying to all undue solicitations, promptly, firmly, perseveringly, No.

title: Judges 19:8
text: Nothing should be delayed till afternoon that ought to be done in the morning.

title: Judges 19:12
text:
A stranger; the city was then inhabited to a considerable extent by Jebusites, one of the nations of Canaan that had not been driven out. 
 
  Gibeah; this was a few miles north of Jerusalem, and on the way towards mount Ephraim. 
 
It is a great comfort and blessing to travellers to find good lodging places, where they can rest in quietness, and not be disturbed by the wicked.

title: Judges 19:13
text: Ramah; a place near Gibeah.

title: Judges 19:15
text: To lodge; there were then no taverns, and travellers were dependent for lodging on private hospitality.

title: Judges 19:16
text: Diligence in business is conducive to excellence of character, and promotive of all those virtues which secure the welfare and comfort of both citizens and strangers.

title: Judges 19:18
text: The house of the Lord; this was in Shiloh, and probably not far from the place where the Levite dwelt.

title: Judges 19:19
text: No want; except for lodging.  He mentioned his provisions to show that he should not be burdensome to his entertainer.

title: Judges 19:20
text:
Peace be with thee; the usual salutation of kindness. 
 
Hospitality, especially to the needy, is a great blessing to the giver and to the receiver.  It is well-pleasing to God, and when exercised from love to him will receive a gracious and an abundant reward.  Romans 12:13 I Timothy 3:2 Titus 1:8 I Peter 4:9

title: Judges 19:22
text:
Sons of Belial; wicked, abandoned men. 
 
The greater the light which men resist, the more wicked they will be; and apostate professors of religion, who become openly vicious, are among the worst of mankind.

title: Judges 19:25
text: Habitual wickedness makes men inexpressibly cruel, and none are so dead to pity and compassion as those who are given up to its power.  It is the spirit of hell, and those who pursue it are ripening for that place of torment.   Psalms 26:9

title: Judges 19:28
text: None answered; she was dead.

title: Judges 20:1
text:
Dan; in the northern extremity of the land. 
 
  Beer-sheba; in the southern extremity. 
 
  Gilead; on the east side of Jordan. 
 
  Mizpeh; a place south-west of Gibeah, and near the border of Judah and Benjamin. 
 
The sins of others, especially when great and aggravated, may be condemned; but without divine grace men will not abhor and forsake their own.

title: Judges 20:4
text: Men should carefully inquire into the facts, and obtain full proof of guilt, before they undertake to punish.

title: Judges 20:8
text: When men, in reliance on their own wisdom and strength, determine what they will do without asking direction of God or seeking his blessing, they should not think it strange if he does not give them success.  Deuteronomy 1:40-44

title: Judges 20:11
text: Knit; united.

title: Judges 20:12
text: Men who protect criminals and screen them from punishment, become partakers of their guilt, and often of their woes.

title: Judges 20:17
text: The race is not always to the swift, nor the battle to the strong.  Men are dependent on God, and numbers merely can never insure success.

title: Judges 20:18
text: Which of us shall go up first; they did not ask, as they should have done, whether they should go up.  This, in reliance on their own wisdom and strength, they had resolved to do, and they only asked who should go first.  The Lord told them, but did not by this insure their success.

title: Judges 20:23
text: Men may externally seek the Lord without forsaking their sins, and in righteous judgment he may suffer them to take a course which shall end in their ruin.

title: Judges 20:25
text: Destroyed--of the children of Israel--eighteen thousand; the Israelites had themselves been guilty of various crimes, and God saw fit thus to punish them before he used them as instruments of punishing Benjamin.

title: Judges 20:28
text:
Phinehas--stood before it in those days; this shows that these transactions took place not long after the death of Joshua or the elders that outlived him.   Judges 17:1  
 
  Or shall I cease? this shows that they were now in some measure humbled, ready to commit themselves to the guidance and disposal of God, and thus were better prepared for success. 
 
  I will deliver them; not without their use of means, but by such means. 
 
A disposition to be governed in all things, not by our own will, but by the will of God, is a good preparation for sure, ultimate, and complete success.

title: Judges 20:29
text: The promise of divine aid, rightly understood, leads men not to neglect means, but diligently and perseveringly to use them.

title: Judges 20:33
text: Baal-tamar; a place near Gibeah.

title: Judges 20:35
text: However numerous or efficacious the means which men use, their success comes from God, and in the Bible is ascribed to him as really as if no means had been employed.

title: Judges 20:45
text: Rock of Rimmon; supposed to be a place north-east of Gibeah.

title: Judges 20:46
text: The wicked in this world are often the means of punishing themselves and one another; and this, in the future world, may continue to be the case for ever.

title: Judges 20:47
text: In the rock; in its fastnesses.

title: Judges 21:1
text: Engagements made in the heat of passion often end in bitter repentance.

title: Judges 21:5
text: Civil wars, and those waged among brethren, are often most cruel, and lead on from one degree of enormity to another, till multitudes of both parties are overwhelmed in common woe.

title: Judges 21:8
text: Jabesh-gilead; a city in the half-tribe of Manasseh, on the east of Jordan.

title: Judges 21:10
text: Men may be very scrupulous about moral obligation in some things, and most regardless of it in others.

title: Judges 21:12
text: In the land of Canaan; on the west side of Jordan.

title: Judges 21:14
text: Conscience unenlightened and blinded by sin, is a very unsafe guide. What it forbids men to do directly, it often suffers them to do indirectly, and under circumstances which greatly increase their guilt.

title: Judges 21:18
text: Men may be so blinded by sin as to think that the giving of one wife, with her own consent and that of her parents, to one man is a crime; and that being accessory by robbery and violence to the giving, without their consent or that of their parents, of two hundred wives to two hundred men, is a worthy deed.  Surely, he that trusteth in his own heart is a fool.   Proverbs 28:26

title: Judges 21:22
text: Ye did not give unto them; by this they imply that they do not violate the oath spoken of in  Judges 21:1 Judges 21:7 Judges 21:18 , as the women were not taken by their consent.

title: Judges 21:23
text: Persons may sometimes be married very improperly, and without the consent of friends; yet after their marriage has occurred, and cannot be revoked, it is usually wise for friends cheerfully to acquiesce, and strive to make the connection as useful as possible.

title: Ruth 1:1
text:
The land; Palestine. 
 
  Moab; a country south-east of Palestine. 
 
Men are dependent on God for the comforts of this life, as well as the life to come; and without his blessing, notwithstanding all human efforts, the earth would never yield a harvest.

title: Ruth 1:2
text:
Ephrathites; Bethlehem was called Ephratah, and its inhabitants Ephrathites. 
 
To remove, from a regard to worldly circumstances merely, out of a land of religious light and privileges to a land of darkness and idolatry, is a course full of danger, and likely to terminate in distress.

title: Ruth 1:5
text: A state of widowhood is one of peculiar trials, which calls for, and should receive, peculiar sympathy and aid.

title: Ruth 1:6
text: All our blessings are the gift of God; they should be sought from him, and in the reception of them his goodness should be daily acknowledged.  Matthew 6:11

title: Ruth 1:9
text: The marriage of daughters with husbands who will give them a peaceful, pleasant, and useful home, is desired by wise and pious parents, not only for the good of their daughters, but of all who may feel their influence.

title: Ruth 1:14
text: Pious relatives may conduct with such wisdom and kindness as, with the blessing of God, to endear themselves to those who have no religion; and this they should desire, for the purpose of doing them good.

title: Ruth 1:15
text: Her gods; the idols which her countrymen worshipped.

title: Ruth 1:16
text:
Thy God my God; in this she expressed her determination to embrace and adhere to the Jewish religion. 
 
Fixed and strong resolution is necessary in order truly to serve God, and those who love him will, when called to it, give up all for his sake.

title: Ruth 1:20
text:
Naomi; meaning pleasant. 
 
  Mara; bitter. 
 
True piety will lead men to see and acknowledge the hand of God in their mercies and in their trials; to be thankful for the one and submissive under the other, and to endeavor in both to honor him.

title: Ruth 1:22
text: Beginning of barley-harvest; in April.

title: Ruth 2:1
text: Kinsman; relative.

title: Ruth 2:2
text:
Glean ears; pick up what was scattered and left in the field by the reapers. 
 
  Grace; favor. 
 
True piety will lead those who have it to be industrious, and to engage in any honest, useful employment to which they may in the providence of God be called.

title: Ruth 2:3
text:
A part of the field; the cultivated fields were not then ordinarily divided by fences, but by a stone or landmark. 
 
With a fatherly kindness God watches over and directs the concerns of the poorest, most obscure, and defenceless of his people, and directs them in such a manner as to promote their highest good.

title: Ruth 2:4
text: Love to God inspires goodwill to men, and promotes kind affection and true politeness in all conditions and relations of life.

title: Ruth 2:7
text: In the house; probably the tent pitched in the field where the reapers were at work, and under which Boaz saw her sitting; for she does not seem to have gone home to her mother in Bethlehem until evening.

title: Ruth 2:8
text:
Hearest thou not; hearken. 
 
  My daughter; an expression of kindness. 
 
Kindness to the destitute, especially to the stranger, the widow, the fatherless, and those who have no earthly helper, is peculiarly pleasing to God and endearing to men.

title: Ruth 2:10
text: She fell on her face; a common mode in those regions of expressing reverence and gratitude.

title: Ruth 2:11
text: Affectionate regard to parents and other relatives, and sacrifices for their benefit from love to God and his cause, are always remembered by him, and often even in this life receive a great reward.

title: Ruth 2:13
text:
Like unto one of thy handmaidens; as a foreigner she did not venture to put herself in the same rank with them. 
 
The humble, who esteem others better than themselves, are often exalted by God's providence above the proud and self-conceited.  Thus the modest Ruth became the wife of a "mighty man of wealth," and the ancestor of David and of Him who is greater than David.  All this earthly favor was but the earnest and pledge of that heavenly exaltation which is reserved for the meek and lowly in spirit.

title: Ruth 2:14
text: Vinegar; a kind of sour wine or sauce used in those days.

title: Ruth 2:15
text: A generous mind will avoid reproaches and every thing calculated to wound the feelings of the poor, and will delight to aid them in their efforts, by industry and economy, to provide for themselves and those dependent upon them.

title: Ruth 2:17
text: An ephah; nearly a bushel.

title: Ruth 2:19
text: In answer to the prayers of the pious poor for blessings on those who supply their wants, the rich often receive treasures better and more abundant than all which they bestow.

title: Ruth 2:20
text: One of our next kinsmen; one who according to the law had a right to redeem.   Leviticus 25:25

title: Ruth 2:22
text: When in a course which we find by experience to be safe and useful, and in which the Lord blesses us, it is ordinarily wise to persevere and not be disposed to change.  This the aged and experienced feel more deeply than the inexperienced and young.

title: Ruth 2:23
text: Wheat-harvest; in May.

title: Ruth 3:1
text:
Seek rest; by procuring a husband and a home for her. 
 
Wise and pious parents will desire that their children should, if the Lord open the way for it, be well settled in married life, as most conducive to their usefulness and comfort, and that of those around them.

title: Ruth 3:5
text: The directions of parents should be followed by children, even when they have arrived to mature years, so far as they accord with the revealed will of God.   Proverbs 1:8 Proverbs 23:22

title: Ruth 3:9
text: Spread--thy skirt; this was a request to him to redeem her husband's property and marry her, according to the directions in  Deuteronomy 25:5-10 .

title: Ruth 3:11
text: A readiness promptly to comply with the known will of God, and to promote the highest good of men, especially of the poor and needy, is peculiarly pleasing in his sight, and prepares us for the reception of his choicest blessings.

title: Ruth 3:13
text: Perform--the part of a kinsman; redeem the property and marry her.

title: Ruth 3:14
text:
Let it not be known; lest false reports should be raised. 
 
Many things may be proper in one country or generation which would not be proper in another; and while our great object should be in all things to do right, we should also, as far as consistent, avoid all appearance of doing wrong, all occasions of misapprehension, and of having our good evil spoken of.   Romans 14:16 I Thessalonians 5:22

title: Ruth 3:15
text: Veil; Ruth was in full dress,  Ruth 3:3 , of which a veil of large size constituted a part.

title: Ruth 4:1
text:
The gate; to which men resorted to transact business. 
 
Punctuality in the transaction of business, and a habit of having every thing done at the right time and in the right way, are highly conducive to prosperity, usefulness, and enjoyment.

title: Ruth 4:2
text:
He took ten men; to witness the transactions.   Ruth 4:9-11  
 
In the sale and conveyance of property, great care should be taken that the case be fairly stated and correctly understood by all concerned, that it be duly witnessed, and so conducted in all respects as to cut off all occasion of future misunderstanding and contention.

title: Ruth 4:5
text: To raise up the name of the dead; he must marry Ruth, as well as redeem or buy the land.

title: Ruth 4:6
text:
Cannot redeem it; that is, upon the condition just added by Boaz, which would impose upon him the burden of maintaining Ruth and Naomi, in addition to his own family. 
 
It is not wise for a man to purchase more property than he can pay for. Nor, if he has one wife, is it right for him to take another.  If he does, he violates the original law of marriage, and will find the way of transgressors to be hard.

title: Ruth 4:7
text: A testimony; that the man who gave the shoe transferred his right to the one who received it.

title: Ruth 4:10
text: Raise up the name of the dead; the eldest son would inherit the estate, and thus the name and inheritance of the family would be preserved.

title: Ruth 4:11
text:
Build the house; had a numerous posterity. 
 
  Ephratah-Bethlehem; different names of the place in which they lived. 
 
Marriage is an ordinance of God, which should be entered into in his fear, be solemnized before witnesses, and its duties so discharged that it may be a blessing to all concerned.

title: Ruth 4:12
text: Pharez; from whom Boaz and the Bethlehemites descended.

title: Ruth 4:14
text:
A kinsman; one who should perpetuate the name and inheritance of her family. 
 
The birth of a child is a just cause of rejoicing, and all interested should unite in supplication to God that it may live, be sanctified, and made a blessing to itself and its friends, to the church of God and the world.

title: Ruth 4:17
text:
Obed; meaning a servant, or one who would be serviceable.  From him descended David and Christ. 
 
Those who honor God he will honor, and make them blessings to all generations, even to the end of time and onward to eternity.  Blessed supremely, for ever blessed, are all who trust in obey him.

title: I Samuel 1:1
text:
Of Ramathaim-zophim; not the Ramah of Benjamin situated near Gibeah, a few miles north of Jerusalem.   I Samuel 1:19 I Samuel 7:17 I Samuel 25:1   Its position is uncertain.  Some suppose it to have been the place now called Soba, a short distance west of Jerusalem. 
 
  Mount Ephraim; this was probably a mountainous ridge that had its rise in Ephraim, and was continued south through Benjamin under the same name; for Ramathaim-zophim seems to have been south of the tribe of Ephraim. 
 
  An Ephrathite; Samuel was of Levitical descent, and belonged to the family of the Kohathites.  See the genealogy,  I Chronicles 6:33-35 , where the name Shemuel is, in the original, the same as that here called Samuel; Eliel is equivalent to Elihu, and Toah is only another form of Tohu.  His father Elkanah is called an Ephrathite either because he resided in mount Ephraim, just as the Ephraimites themselves are sometimes called Ephrathites,  Judges 12:5 I Kings 11:26 ; or, as some think, from his having lived in Bethlehem Ephratah.

title: I Samuel 1:2
text: When a man so far departs from the original law of marriage as to have two wives, he may expect to have peculiar trials.

title: I Samuel 1:3
text:
The Lord of hosts; this is the first mention in the Bible of Jehovah under this title.  See  I Samuel 1:11 .  It means, God of armies, or of the multitudes of heaven, and of the universe. 
 
  In Shiloh; where the tabernacle then was.  It lay in the tribe of Ephraim, among the hills a little east of the road leading northward from Jerusalem to Shechem. 
 
  Eli; he was then high-priest.

title: I Samuel 1:4
text: Portions; of the offering on which they were to feast.  Leviticus 7:15

title: I Samuel 1:5
text: A worthy portion; larger and better.

title: I Samuel 1:6
text:
Her adversary; supposed to be Peninnah.   I Samuel 1:7  
 
Designed and needless provocations increase the wickedness of the giver and the unhappiness of the receiver.

title: I Samuel 1:8
text: A just sense of our unworthiness as sinners, and of the numerous mercies which God bestows upon us, would cure us of discontent.

title: I Samuel 1:9
text: The temple; the tabernacle; the temple was not then built.

title: I Samuel 1:10
text: The best way to obtain relief from trouble is to go to God in humble, affectionate, believing prayer, spread out before him our wants, and beseech him for Christ's sake to bestow the blessings we need.

title: I Samuel 1:11
text:
Give him unto the Lord; to be employed all his life in the special service of Jehovah. 
 
  No razor came upon his head; he should be a Nazarite.  Numbers 6:2-5

title: I Samuel 1:16
text:
Daughter of Belial; an abandoned wicked woman. 
 
  Spoken; prayed to the Lord.

title: I Samuel 1:17
text: Fidelity in giving reproof, meekness in receiving it, and readiness to correct mistakes, and also to receive correction, are traits of character in the worshippers of Jehovah which prepare them for the mutual reception of his blessings.

title: I Samuel 1:18
text:
Grace; favor. 
 
  No more sad; she cheerfully committed her case to the Lord, and expected that he would answer her prayers. 
 
Prayer often brings sweet peace to the soul, before the particular blessings prayed for are received.

title: I Samuel 1:20
text:
Samuel; meaning, asked of God.  It appears from  I Chronicles 6:33-35 , that he was a descendant of Korah.  Thus out of the family of one whom God so sorely punished with sudden death, he yet in his great mercy raised up in after-times the prophet Samuel and the sweet singer Heman. The descendants of the ungodly, warned by the fate, and turning from the sins of their fathers, may through the grace of God become signally holy, honored, and useful. 
 
Blessings obtained of God in answer to prayer should be promptly and gratefully acknowledged, and measures be taken to keep his goodness in perpetual remembrance.   Psalms 116:1-2

title: I Samuel 1:23
text: A wise woman will, if consistent, nurse and train her own children. Even if it keep her for a time from public worship, and occasion many privations and cares, yet, in the health, character, and conduct of her well-trained children, she may expect, with the blessing of God, whose wise and good arrangement she has in this respect followed, a gracious and abundant reward.

title: I Samuel 1:24
text: One ephah; about thirty quarts.

title: I Samuel 1:28
text: No blessings are more dear, and none give greater comfort, than those which are gratefully received from, and heartily devoted to the Lord.

title: I Samuel 2:1
text:
My horn is exalted; the horn was an emblem of power: the Lord would cause her to triumph over all her foes. 
 
Whenever we receive new mercies, let who will be the instrument, we should feel that they come from God, and give him the praise.

title: I Samuel 2:2
text:
None besides thee; no other living and true God. 
 
  Rock; support, refuge, source of good.

title: I Samuel 2:3
text:
Actions are weighed; God perfectly understands their nature, character, and deserts. 
 
A conviction of the constant, all pervading presence of God tends to keep us from sin, excite us to duty, and make us humble, grateful, and better fitted for every good work.

title: I Samuel 2:4
text:
The mighty; who trust in their own strength. 
 
  They that stumbled; the feeble who trust in God.

title: I Samuel 2:5
text:
Ceased; ceased to be hungry, from the abundance that God gave them. 
 
  Borne seven; had many children.

title: I Samuel 2:6
text: Changes in the condition of individuals, families, and nations, though brought about by human instrumentality, are ordered by the Lord, and his agency in them should always be acknowledged.

title: I Samuel 2:8
text: The pillars of the earth are the Lord's; he made and sustains it, and he overrules and disposes of all its concerns.

title: I Samuel 2:9
text:
Keep the feet of his saints; preserve them. 
 
  By strength; of any created arm. 
 
However great the opposition of the wicked, the righteous shall finally overcome, and the temporary successes of the wicked will end in their final and everlasting defeat.

title: I Samuel 2:10
text: His king--his anointed; this is the first time the word Messiah, or the Anointed, is mentioned in the Bible.  It is applied to David and to Christ.

title: I Samuel 2:11
text:
Ramah; the same as Ramathaim-sophim.   I Samuel 1:1  
 
  Minister unto the Lord; perform such services about the sanctuary as were suited to his age. 
 
God is greatly pleased when little children devote themselves to his service; and the smallest child who loves him has more true spiritual knowledge than the greatest and most learned man who neglects his service.

title: I Samuel 2:12
text:
Sons of Eli; Hophni and Phinehas.   I Samuel 2:34  
 
  Sons of Belial; exceedingly wicked. 
 
  Knew not the Lord; on account of the wickedness of the priests. 
 
Men may be called priests, or ministers of religion, may conduct the forms of public worship, and have the best opportunities of knowing God, and yet hate him and be guilty of the most enormous wickedness.

title: I Samuel 2:13
text: Seething; boiling.

title: I Samuel 2:14
text: The priest took; this was robbing the offerer.

title: I Samuel 2:15
text: Sodden; boiled.

title: I Samuel 2:16
text: I will take it; this was an additional robbery.

title: I Samuel 2:17
text:
Men abhorred the offering of the Lord; on account of the wickedness of the priests. 
 
A covetous, self-indulgent, and licentious ministry is one of the greatest curses to the souls of men.  It leads multitudes to despise the ordinances of religion and sink into the darkness and pollution of infidelity.

title: I Samuel 2:18
text: A linen ephod; a garment like that which was worn by the priests.

title: I Samuel 2:20
text:
The loan;  I Samuel 1:1 1Sa 1.28. 
 
A freewill offering to the Lord, even of that which is his, he receives with delight, and bestows upon the offerer an abundant reward.

title: I Samuel 2:22
text: When those who have the right and the power to put licentious men out of the ministry, neglect to do it, they become partakers in their sins, and will share their woes.

title: I Samuel 2:24
text: Ye make the Lord's people to transgress; by tempting them to sin.

title: I Samuel 2:25
text:
The judge shall judge him; if it were an offence of a man against his fellow-man, he might be punished according to the law; or by offering the appointed sacrifice, he might through faith in Christ be forgiven.  But this was a sin not only against men, but against God; it profaned the sacrifice which typified the sacrifice of Christ, and there remained no more sacrifice for sin, but a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation.  Such was probably the meaning of Eli, but he did not convey it with clearness and power to the minds of his profilgate sons.  Nor did he, as he should have done, act it out, by not only reproving them, but expelling them from their office and visiting them with condign punishment, as a warning to all of the guilt and danger of such wickedness.  He was a judge as well as a father, and should have been a terror to those evil-doers.  But he regarded his sons in this matter more than he did the honor of God. 
 
  Because; on account of their sins.

title: I Samuel 2:26
text:
In favor--with the Lord; God may have given him renewing grace in his infant years, in answer to the prayers of his mother. 
 
Parents who receive their children as the gift of God, and train them up in the way they should go, may hope that, through the renewing and sanctifying influences of the Holy Spirit, they will early devote themselves to the service of Christ, and continue in it to the end of life.   Proverbs 22:6 Ephesians 6:4

title: I Samuel 2:27
text:
Appear unto the house of thy father; Eli descended from Aaron.  Exodus 4:14 Exodus 4:27 Exodus 28:1-4 Leviticus 7:7-35  
 
Great favors shown to any one lay him under great obligations to be faithful in the discharge of his appropriate duties, and will aggravate his guilt if he neglect them.

title: I Samuel 2:29
text:
Kick; dishonor, by profaning them or suffering them to be profaned. 
 
It is a great sin for parents to regard their children more than they do God, and the continued indulgence of this sin will bring upon them fearful punishment.

title: I Samuel 2:30
text:
Walk before me;  Exodus 28:43 Exodus 29:9  
  For ever; to the end of the Jewish dispensation. 
 
  Lightly esteemed; rejected and punished.

title: I Samuel 2:31
text:
Cut off thine arm; cause his power and authority to cease. 
 
The sins of parents may deeply affect not only their children, but their distant posterity, even to the end of time and onward to eternity.

title: I Samuel 2:32
text: An enemy in my habitation; or, the affliction of the tabernacle, on account of the ark being taken by the Philistines, and other calamities.

title: I Samuel 2:34
text:
A sign; an evidence that all which he had foretold would be accomplished.   I Samuel 4:11  
 
When God makes declarations with regard to the future, he furnishes such evidence of the certainty of their accomplishment as ought to produce universal conviction.

title: I Samuel 2:35
text:
A faithful priest; Zadok, a descendant not of Eli, but of Eleazar.  I Kings 2:27 I Kings 2:35 I Chronicles 29:22  
 
  Build him a sure house; continue his posterity in the priesthood. 
 
  Mine anointed; the kings of David's line who would be anointed by him to their office, and from whom Christ would come. 
 
  For ever; as long as the kings of Israel should continue. 
 
The providence of God is a commentary on his word, and the more we see of the operations of the one, the more we shall see of the truth of the other.

title: I Samuel 2:36
text:
In thy house; of Eli's descendants. 
 
  Shall say; on account of their great poverty and degradation.

title: I Samuel 3:1
text:
Precious; rare, uncommon. 
 
  No open vision; literally, "vision was not spread abroad," that is, revelations from God were not common. 
 
Those who are blessed with a fulness of divine instruction and with all the means of grace, but very faintly realize the sad condition of such as are without them, wandering in darkness and the shadow of death.

title: I Samuel 3:2
text: Eyesight is a great blessing, which should be carefully preserved and wisely employed; that in case of its loss, the mind, in rich stores of knowledge, may have materials for useful and happy contemplation.

title: I Samuel 3:5
text: Cheerful readiness in children to comply with the wishes of parents and teachers, in an indication of great excellence of character, and of eminent usefulness in future life.

title: I Samuel 3:7
text:
Did not yet know the Lord; did not know him in the way of receiving revelations from him. 
 
God by his Spirit, in his word and his providence, sometimes repeatedly speaks to men before they are aware of it, especially if they are young and have not been accustomed to distinguish his voice from that of others.

title: I Samuel 3:10
text: When men, and even children, manifest a readiness to be instructed by God, he will communicate to them a knowledge of his will; and though it may be trying, yet in doing it they will be accepted of him and receive a great reward.

title: I Samuel 3:13
text: Parents, to please God and escape his indignation, must not only pray with and for their children, and counsel and advise them, but must also govern them; and if they are disposed to be openly vicious, must inflict such punishment as will effectually restrain them.  Nor must fear or favor hinder them from exercising the authority and power which God has given them for this purpose.

title: I Samuel 3:14
text: Not be purged; not so done away as to prevent the threatened punishment.

title: I Samuel 3:17
text:
Do so to thee; punish thee. 
 
Parents should encourage their children freely and fully to communicate with them on all things in which they are interested, especially on the subject of religion and whatever pertains to the performance of duty.

title: I Samuel 3:18
text: When the will of God is made known, true piety in vigorous exercise will lead the soul to acquiesce in it, feeling that what God says must be true, and what he does must be right and good.

title: I Samuel 3:19
text:
Let none of his words fall; let none of his predictions fail of their accomplishment. 
 
When men follow the directions of God so far as they know them, he will communicate to them an increasing knowledge of his will, and by experience they will acquire the habit of readily understanding and promptly obeying it.

title: I Samuel 3:20
text: From Dan even to Beer-sheba; from one end of the land to the other.

title: I Samuel 4:1
text:
The word of Samuel; that which God revealed to him. 
 
  Eben-ezer--Aphek; Mizpeh, where Samuel judged Israel, is supposed to have been the modern Neby Samwil, (Prophet Samuel,) a few miles north-north-west from Jerusalem. Eben-ezer, here named by way of anticipation, was in its vicinity.   I Samuel 7:12   There were several places that bore the name of Aphek.  That named here can hardly have been the Aphek near Jezreel, where the Philistines encamped before the overthrow of Saul,  I Samuel 29:1 , as that is far distant from Eben- ezer.  It seems rather to have been situated in the tribe of Judah, perhaps south-west of Eben-ezer on the road to Ashdod.  1Sa 5.1 
 
The declarations of God in his word are often shown to be true by his providence, and those who had disbelieved them are thus made to see their truth.

title: I Samuel 4:3
text:
Let us fetch the ark; the emblem of the divine presence.  They hoped to receive from the emblem what could only come from God; as many now hope, from the image or figure of the cross, to receive what can come only from Him who bled upon it. 
 
Men often expect from the mere forms of religion what can come only from its power: from senseless wood or stone they expect what can come only from the one living and true God.

title: I Samuel 4:4
text: Between the cherubim; the Shekinah, or visible glory of God, was manifested over the mercy-seat between the cherubim, and that was regarded as his special dwelling-place.

title: I Samuel 4:5
text: Ignorant and false zeal in immoral and wicked teachers is apt to be noisy and vain-glorious, to be fond of show, and to abound in appeals to the senses and passions of men.

title: I Samuel 4:7
text: All men who are in any measure enlightened have a conviction of a power which is above them, and which, on account of their sins, they have reason to fear.

title: I Samuel 4:8
text: Gods; God.  Though this word in the original is in the plural number, yet when applied to Jehovah, it should be, as it usually is, translated in the singular.

title: I Samuel 4:9
text: Quit yourselves; do your duty.

title: I Samuel 4:10
text: Under wicked religious teachers the people also become exceedingly wicked, and thus ripen for divine judgments; and when ripe, others who are wicked are often suffered to bring those judgments upon them.

title: I Samuel 4:12
text: His clothes rent; in token of great mourning.

title: I Samuel 4:13
text: The place where God dwells is precious to good men, and they fear the loss of his presence more than that of any worldly good.

title: I Samuel 4:18
text:
He fell; Eli. 
 
The dishonor of God, and his frown upon the people, are more distressing to good men than the death even of their nearest earthly friends.

title: I Samuel 4:21
text:
Ichabod; no glory. 
 
The chief glory of a nation is the presence and favor of God, for the loss of which no earthly good can be an adequate compensation.

title: I Samuel 5:1
text:
Ashdod; one of the cities of the Philistines. 
 
As a punishment to his people, God often suffers the wicked for a time to triumph over them, and to take from them many precious blessings.

title: I Samuel 5:2
text: Dagon; from dag, signifying a fish.  It was the name of an idol, the upper part of which was in the form of a man, and the lower part in that of a fish.

title: I Samuel 5:4
text:
Only the stump; in the original, the dagon, that is, the fishy part of the idol. 
 
All the efforts of the wicked to perpetuate their triumphs, and ultimately to prevail over the people of God, will be unavailing.

title: I Samuel 5:5
text: Tread on the threshold; from superstitious reverence towards it, as being the place where Dagon's body has lain.

title: I Samuel 5:7
text: God will finally convince all that they cnanot continue to oppose him and prosper, and that those things which they have idolized, and from which they expected help, have proved their ruin.

title: I Samuel 5:8
text:
Lords; rulers. 
 
  Gath; another city of the Philistines.

title: I Samuel 5:9
text: Emerods; hemorroids, or a species of the piles.

title: I Samuel 5:10
text:
Edkon; the northernmost city of the Philistines. 
 
All expedients of men to save themselves from the wrath of God, without returning in penitence and faith to him, are vain.

title: I Samuel 5:11
text: Very heavy; God smote them with sore judgments.

title: I Samuel 5:12
text: Diseases are God's servants; they go and come at his bidding, and all things in heaven, earth, and hell, are subject to his control.

title: I Samuel 6:1
text: So long as men continue in wickedness, it is vain to expect permanent deliverance from trouble.

title: I Samuel 6:2
text: Priests--diviners; their religious guides.

title: I Samuel 6:4
text: Sinners who are ignorant of, or who reject the way of acceptance which God has provided through Jesus Christ, devise various methods of their own, and are often willing to make great sacrifices and be at much expense to appease his wrath and purchase his favor.

title: I Samuel 6:5
text: Mice; these, it is supposed, destroyed their crops.

title: I Samuel 6:7
text: No yoke--bring their calves home; they judged that if, in such circumstances, the kine proceeded straight on the road to the Israelitish city Beth-shemesh, it would be a proof that they were immediately guided by Jehovah himself, and that his presence had been the cause of their calamities.

title: I Samuel 6:8
text: Coffer; a small chest or box for money and precious treasures.

title: I Samuel 6:9
text:
Beth-shemesh; a city of priests in the tribe of Judah and on the border of the Philistines. 
 
Men had rather feel that their sufferings come by chance, than see in them the hand of God, and feel that they are manifestations of his displeasure against their sins.

title: I Samuel 6:12
text: God has perfect control over the animal as well as the rational creation, can use the instincts of nature or counteract them as he pleases, and will eventually convince all that nothing comes by chance throughout his dominion.

title: I Samuel 6:13
text: Their wheat-harvest; in May.

title: I Samuel 6:18
text:
Both of fenced cities, and of country villages; the meaning of these words seems to be, that while the five golden mice answered in number to the five chief cities of the Philistines, a contribution was levied for them upon all the towns, whether fenced cities or open villages. 
 
  Unto the great stone of Abel; which marked the boundary of Philistia, on the road taken by the kine.  It is the same stone mentioned in 1Sa 6.15. 
 
  Abel means mourning, the stone receiving this name from the circumstance recorded in 1Sa 6.19. 
 
An unhallowed desire to see what God has hidden, to pry into what he has not revealed, and do what he forbids, is a sin, the indulgence of which has involved multitudes in ruin.

title: I Samuel 6:19
text:
Because they had looked into the ark; by divine appointment the ark was kept in the Holy of Holies, concealed from the eyes of all but the high-priest on the great day of atonement.  In the journeyings of the Israelites in the wilderness, it was carefully covered from view.  Numbers 4:5-6   None but the high-priest and his sons might see it, or any of the holy things the sanctuary contained.  The act of the men of Beth-shemesh therefore was one of profane curiosity, contrary to the divine command, and to that reverence which God required for the holy things of the tabernacle. 
 
  Fifty thousand and threescore and ten; literally, threescore and ten men, fifty a thousand; supposed by some to mean fifty out of a thousand, or seventy out of fourteen hundred inhabitants. 
 
  A great slaughter; for such a place.

title: I Samuel 6:21
text: Kirjath-jearim; north-east of Beth-shemesh, and on the border between Judah and Benjamin.

title: I Samuel 7:1
text: The ordinances of God will benefit all who rightly observe them, but none who continue to neglect them.

title: I Samuel 7:2
text: It was twenty years; after the ark was brought to Kirjath-jearim, before the Israelites humbled themselves and turned to the Lord as related in the following verses.

title: I Samuel 7:3
text: By the right use of means which God has provided, men are bound to prepare their hearts for his service.

title: I Samuel 7:4
text: Baalim and Ashtaroth; images of Baal and Astarte.

title: I Samuel 7:5
text: Penitent confession of sin, and humble prayer for divine mercy, are essential to forgiveness, and are a sure preparation for the reception of divine favors.

title: I Samuel 7:6
text: Poured it out before the Lord; by this symbolical act, in connection with fasting and prayer, they seem to have denoted the entire prostration of their souls before God in humble penitence.

title: I Samuel 7:8
text: All who have right views of God and of themselves, will place a high value on the prayers of his people, and will earnestly desire them.  Esther 4:16 Job 42:8-9 James 5:16

title: I Samuel 7:10
text: Humble, believing, earnest, persevering prayer has great influence with God, and is instrumental of unspeakable good to men.

title: I Samuel 7:12
text: Eben-ezer; meaning, the stone of help, or the help-stone.

title: I Samuel 7:15
text: Rulers who are men of prayer, and who transact their civil duties in the fear and love of God, are great blessings to the people.

title: I Samuel 7:16
text: Bethel was north, and Mizpeh (in the original Mizpah) north-west from Jerusalem.

title: I Samuel 7:17
text: Rameh; in Benjamin, generally supposed to be the same as Ramathaim-zophim.

title: I Samuel 8:3
text:
Lucre; gain. 
 
  Bribes; gifts to induce one wrongly to favor those who offer them. 
 
When men appoint their own rulers, if they do not have such, and such only, as are wise and good, it is their own fault; but when the government is hereditary, and descends from parents to children, whether good or bad, wise or foolish, it is often unjust and cruel, for wise and good parents may be followed by foolish and wicked children.

title: I Samuel 8:5
text: When men in trouble follow their own judgment merely, as to the way of getting out of it, they often take a course which tends only to increase it; and if they will not be dissuaded from such a course, God in righteous judgment sometimes suffers them to pursue it, and thus dreadfully to punish themselves.   Jeremiah 2:19

title: I Samuel 8:6
text:
Displeased Samuel; appeared to him to be wrong. 
 
  Samuel prayed; to be rightly directed with regard to the matter in question. 
 
When in new and difficult circumstances men go to God for direction, choosing rather to be governed by his will than their own, he will guide them, and in the proper use of their own faculties will lead them to right decisions.

title: I Samuel 8:7
text: Hearken unto the voice of the people--they have not rejected thee, but--me; for the accomplishment of his own wise and holy purposes, God saw good to grant their request; but it proceeded from a spirit of unblief and worldly confidence.  In looking to an earthly king, after the manner of their heathen neighbors, instead of Jehovah, for deliverance, they rejected him as their king, and brought upon themselves many great evils, from which simple faith in God and obedience to his words would have saved them.

title: I Samuel 8:9
text:
Hearken; give them a king, if, after showing how he will treat them, thy continue to insist upon it.   I Samuel 8:19-22  
 
  The manner of the king; how he would treat them.   I Samuel 8:11  
 
God delights to communicate to men all needed information, so that if they will follow his directions, they may be saved from suffering the fruits of their folly.

title: I Samuel 8:11
text: Run before; as attendants and waiters.   II Samuel 15:1

title: I Samuel 8:12
text: To ear; to plough.   Genesis 45:7

title: I Samuel 8:13
text: Confectionaries; persons who prepared perfumes and spices.

title: I Samuel 8:18
text: When men with their eyes open go on in wickedness, regarding their feelings more than the testimony of Jehovah, and thus bring themselves into trouble, God leaves them to endure it till they are convinced of their sin and turn to him, or sink into utter ruin.

title: I Samuel 8:19
text:
The voice of Samuel; in dissuading them from having a king. 
 
  Nay; we will not hearken to thee. 
 
When men by word or deed say to God, Not thy will, but mine be done, let them prepare for trouble.  If in that way they should succeed and be finally blessed, it would show that their will was wiser and better than his, as Satan tempts them to believe.  Hence God, in vindication of his own character, disappoints them.

title: I Samuel 8:20
text: Men who are enchanted with the trappings of royalty, and carried away by a thirst for military glory, are not safe guides for themselves nor their fellow men.

title: I Samuel 9:2
text:
A choice young man; these words relate chiefly to his personal appearance. 
 
A sound mind and a well-formed, healthy, and vigorous body are rich gifts of God, which lay those who possess them under peculiar obligations of distinguished usefulness in his service.

title: I Samuel 9:3
text: All earthly possessions are liable to be lost; and this should lead us to seek those treasures which will be secure, and which when obtained will be enjoyed for ever.

title: I Samuel 9:4
text: Mount Ephraim; see note to  I Samuel 1:1 .

title: I Samuel 9:5
text: As property is of little value compared with life, it is foolish, as well as wicked, for the sake of obtaining the one to sacrifice the other.

title: I Samuel 9:6
text:
In this city; it has been commonly assumed that this was Ramah, the home of Samuel.  But Saul, on his return home, passed by Rachel's sepulchre, which was south of Jerusalem near Beth-lehem.  This circumstance has led some to suppose that the city where Saul and his servant found Samuel was not Ramah, but some place near Beth-lehem, whither he had gone in the discharge of his public duties. 
 
If men were as anxious to be saved from sin as they are to find lost property, they would seek all needful information, and when they learned the way would let nothing hinder them from walking in it.  Proverbs 2:4-5

title: I Samuel 9:7
text: A present; such as it was then, and in the East is now, customary to offer.

title: I Samuel 9:8
text: A shekel; about fifty cents.

title: I Samuel 9:12
text:
Before you; in the city to which thy were going. 
 
  The high place; the eminence on which they offered sacrifices.

title: I Samuel 9:13
text:
They eat; that portion of the offering which was allowed them in the Levitical law. 
 
Those who eat, drink, and enjoy the good things of life without thanking God or imploring his blessing, act in this respect like atheists, and the language of their practice is, No God.  Psalms 14:1 Psalms 53:1

title: I Samuel 9:15
text: The Lord makes known to those who do his will many things of which others are ignorant, and which no one without obeying him will ever know.

title: I Samuel 9:20
text: While men in their actions seek one object, God often by them accomplishes another; and no one, when he performs any act, can tell what great results may be connected with it.

title: I Samuel 9:22
text: Those who are selected by God as rulers should, for their office' sake, receive all due honors, and when the will of God with regard to them is known, all should acquiesce in it.

title: I Samuel 9:24
text: Left; rather, reserved, in anticipation of Saul's coming.

title: I Samuel 9:25
text: The top of the house; a retired place, to which they often went for conversation.

title: I Samuel 9:27
text: Ministers should make known to rulers as well as others the will of God, and none are ever so exalted as not to be under sacred obligations in all things to obey it.

title: I Samuel 10:1
text: Poured it upon his head; in token of his being set apart and furnished by God to be king of Israel.

title: I Samuel 10:2
text:
Rachel's sepulchre;    See note,  I Samuel 11:6 . 
 
If men wait upon God and follow his directions, he will show them what he would have them do, and furnish them for the duties to which he calls them.

title: I Samuel 10:3
text:
Tabor; or oak of Tabor: not mount Tabor, but a place apparently in the tribe of Benjamin. 
 
  Men going up to God; to worship God.

title: I Samuel 10:5
text:
The hill of God; an eminence on which he was worshipped, and on which was a school of the prophets. 
 
  They shall prophesy; praise God, under divine inspiration, with the voice and instruments of music.

title: I Samuel 10:6
text:
Prophesy with them; compare  Exodus 15:21 I Chronicles 25:3 . 
 
  Turned into another man; so changed by the influence of God's Spirit as to be fitted to become king.

title: I Samuel 10:7
text:
As occasion serve; as he should judge best; or as circumstances might require. 
 
If men are under the guidance of God and seek his glory, they will be able to judge, in view of all circumstances, what should be done to render themselves most useful.

title: I Samuel 10:9
text:
Another heart; one that fitted him to govern the people. 
 
All the qualifications of men for the formation and accomplishment of great and useful plans come from God, and lay them under increased obligations of devotion to his service; but enlarged views and great talents may be given, and men may join externally in the worship of God, without the renewing and sanctifying influences of his Spirit.

title: I Samuel 10:11
text: Is Saul also among the prophets? they were surprised that, without having been instructed, he should be able thus to join with them.

title: I Samuel 10:12
text: Their father; the father of the prophets.  This was God, who could endow whomsoever he pleased with the gift of prophecy.  It ought not then to surprise them that Saul was among the prophets.

title: I Samuel 10:19
text:
Rejected your God; by insisting on a change in the government which he had established. 
 
The reception from God of an object which is sought is no certain evidence of his approbation.  He may give it in wrath.   I Samuel 12:12-13 I Samuel 12:19  We should therefore rely upon his wisdom rather than our own, saying, Not my will, but thine be done.

title: I Samuel 10:20
text: Benjamin was taken; they cast lots, and the lot fell upon the tribe of Benjamin.

title: I Samuel 10:22
text:
Should yet come thither; or, had yet come thither. 
 
  Stuff; the baggage and other furniture of the assembled people.

title: I Samuel 10:23
text: Higher than any of the people; personal size and strength were much valued by the ancients in their kings.  God was pleased, in the first instance, to give the people a king after their own ideas, before he gave them one after his own heart.

title: I Samuel 10:25
text:
The manner of the kingdom; the regulations which God had prescribed for its government.   Deuteronomy 17:14-20  
 
Kings, and men in authority, as well as in all other conditions of life, are bound to be acquainted with and to be governed by the revealed will of God.

title: I Samuel 10:26
text: Had touched; inclined by his Spirit to follow Saul and support his authority.

title: I Samuel 10:27
text: The best way to treat difficulties often is, for a time at least, to say and do nothing about them.

title: I Samuel 11:1
text:
Jabesh-gilead; a city in the tribe of Manesseh, on the east side of Jordan. 
 
If it is wise in men to make great sacrifices and submit to many hardships to save their lives, how much more wise is it to sacrifice and suffer whatever may be needful to save their souls.   Matthew 5:29-30

title: I Samuel 11:2
text: Great cruelty and bitter oposition to the people and cause of God generally go together.

title: I Samuel 11:4
text:
Gibeah; in Benjamin, where Saul lived. 
 
It is right that one portion of the human family should deeply sympathize with the sufferings of another, and do whatever may be consistent with truth and duty to afford them relief.

title: I Samuel 11:6
text: The Spirit of God; awakened Saul's indignation and inspired him with wisdom, courage, and all needful qualities to collect an army and lead them forth to victory.

title: I Samuel 11:7
text: The fear of the Lord; that he would in his providence bring dreadful judgments upon them, if they should not go forth to protect their brethren.

title: I Samuel 11:8
text: Bezek; a place between Sechem and Jabesh-gilead.

title: I Samuel 11:9
text: If gladness and joy are occasioned by deliverance from temporal calamities, much more should they be by deliverance from those which are eternal.

title: I Samuel 11:11
