text: The morning-watch; between two o'clock and sunrise.

title: I Samuel 11:12
text: Who is he;  I Samuel 10:1

title: I Samuel 11:13
text: True courage and real greatness are manifested in forgiving personal injuries, not in avenging them.

title: I Samuel 11:14
text: Renew the kingdom; publicly proclaim Saul as king.

title: I Samuel 12:2
text: Those who serve God from their childhood are often made distinguished benefactors to mankind.

title: I Samuel 12:3
text: His anointed; Saul.   I Samuel 10:1

title: I Samuel 12:4
text:
Taken aught; any thing wrongfully. 
 
Men who have long been in public life, and have been governed by the fear and love of God, may expect when they retire to leave a conviction of their fidelity in the hearts of others, which shall tend greatly to promote his glory and the good of their fellow men.

title: I Samuel 12:6
text: Aged men, after retiring from more laborious and active duties, may still be useful by communicating to the young a knowledge of facts in the history of their fathers, and of the instructions which those facts afford.

title: I Samuel 12:10
text: A just review of the past will impress the conviction that sin leads to misery, and that there is no escaping it, except in repentance and hearty devotion to the service of God.

title: I Samuel 12:11
text:
Jerubbaal; Gideon.   Judges 6:14 Judges 6:32  
 
  Bedan; perhaps either Barak or Abdon.

title: I Samuel 12:12
text: That Nahash--came; the attack of Nahash upon Jabesh-Gilead took place after Saul had been anointed king; but he had previously threatened the Israelites, and the fear of him was with them a chief motive for asking of Samuel a king to go before them and fight their battles.

title: I Samuel 12:15
text: However great the blessings which God bestows upon a people, they cannot long preserve them unless they hearken to his voice and walk in his ways.

title: I Samuel 12:18
text: The Lord sent thunder and rain; an uncommon thing, as it ordinarily never rained in Palestine during the season of wheat-harvest.

title: I Samuel 12:19
text: The true friends of God can greatly benefit their fellow men; and often the wicked in their distress feel this, and apply to them for help.

title: I Samuel 12:23
text: However ungratefully pious men may have been treated, they will labor to do good even to those who have done them evil; while they maintain that there can be no real blessedness but in hearty obedience to the commands of God.

title: I Samuel 13:2
text:
Michmash; this place lay on the north side of a precipitous valley, a few miles north of Jerusalem; while Geba, which must not be confounded with Gibeah of Benjamin, lay over against it on the south side of the same valley. 
 
  Mount Bethel; a short distance north-west from Michmash. 
 
  Gibeah of Benjamin; not far from Geba on the south-west.

title: I Samuel 13:3
text: Smote the garrison--in Geba; thus he obtained control of the south side of the valley north of which Michmash lay.

title: I Samuel 13:6
text: Those who rely on their own wisdom, trusting to man not to God, and expect to prosper, will be disappointed, and troubles will come upon them, from which, without returning to him, they cannot escape.

title: I Samuel 13:7
text: Went over Jordan; to escape from the oppression of the Philistines.

title: I Samuel 13:9
text: The expedients which men adopt to deliver themselves from calamities, often only increase them.

title: I Samuel 13:13
text:
Thou hast done foolishly; in offering sacrifices which he had no right to offer, and in not waiting for Samuel, as God had commanded. 
 
No one can tell the evils which may result from a single act of known disobedience to God.

title: I Samuel 13:14
text: A man after his own heart; David.

title: I Samuel 13:17
text:
Camp of the Philistines; who had their head-quarters at Michmash. 
 
  Ophrah; north-east from Michmash.

title: I Samuel 13:18
text:
The way to Beth-horon; toward the west. 
 
  Toward the wilderness; on the east.

title: I Samuel 13:19
text:
There was no smith; the Philistines had removed them to prevent the Israelites from being furnished with implements of war. 
 
For their sins, a people are often brought into oppressive and degrading bondage, when, had they obeyed God, they might have enjoyed liberty, peace, and prosperity.

title: I Samuel 13:23
text: Went out to the passage of Michmash; to its commencement on the north side of the steep and difficult way that led across the valley from Michmash to Geba.  Saul and Jonathan were on the south side of the same valley.

title: I Samuel 14:1
text: On the other side; of the valley which lay between the Israelites and the Philistines.

title: I Samuel 14:5
text: Over against Gibeath; the original reads Geba, which should not be interchanged with Gibeah.  This latter place lay about three miles west of south from Geba.

title: I Samuel 14:6
text: When men in the fear and love of God engage in duties to which he calls them, they may safely trust in him, and expect, in following his directions, to meet with success.

title: I Samuel 14:10
text: A sign; that God called them to go up to the Philistines, and would give them success.

title: I Samuel 14:12
text:
Will show you a thing; will show you something; namely, how soon we can destroy you. 
 
Right views of dependence on God will lead men to use means to obtain his blessing, and when it is obtained, to acknowledge his goodness and give him the glory.

title: I Samuel 14:16
text: The multitude; of the Philistines.

title: I Samuel 14:18
text: Bring hither the ark of God; for the purpose of inquiring of God, through his priest, what should be done.  The inquiry was made by the Urim and Thummim, in the high-priest's breast-plate.  Exodus 28:30   Numbers 27:21   Why Saul wished for the presence of the ark is not certainly known.  Perhaps it was that God, who dwelt between the cherubim, might thus be visibly present at the transaction.

title: I Samuel 14:19
text: Withdraw thy hand; he need not proceed any furhter in his inquiry as to what Israel should do, for the duty of pursuing the Philistines now seemed plain to him.

title: I Samuel 14:20
text:
Against his fellow; the Philistines destroyed one another. 
 
When God sets himself against a people, he can cause them to fall, not only before their enemies, but by the hands of one another.

title: I Samuel 14:24
text:
Cursed; devoted to destruction. 
 
There is neither wisdom nor piety in forbidding men to partake of those bounties of providence the proper use of which is conducive to their comfort, and to the best discharge of their appropriate duties.

title: I Samuel 14:27
text: His eyes were enlightened; he was invigorated and refreshed.

title: I Samuel 14:31
text: Aijalon; in the tribe of Dan, towards the land of the Philistines.

title: I Samuel 14:32
text:
Did eat them with the blood; in a manner forbidden by their law. 
 
Forbidding men to do what God allows, increases their temptations to do what he forbids, and thus to bring trouble not only on themselves, but upon all with whom they are connected.

title: I Samuel 14:35
text: Education, the goadings of conscience, the hope of gain, and many other motives may lead men to attend to some of the externals of religion, who never make it their great object in all things to obey God, and who have no real love to his character or ways.

title: I Samuel 14:36
text: Draw near--unto God; inquire of him whether they should go after the Philistines or not.

title: I Samuel 14:38
text: This sin; the sin which prevented the answer to his inquiry.

title: I Samuel 14:39
text: Those who are least sensible of their own sins are often most ready to denounce the sins of others, and while they openly disobey God's commands, to kill those who disobey theirs.

title: I Samuel 14:44
text:
God do so; inflict greater evil upon me, if I do not put thee to death according to my oath.   I Samuel 14:24  
 
Reckless zeal, profane swearing and great cruelty, may all be united, and under cover of regard for truth and duty, stifle even natural affection and lead to the commission of the most abominable crimes.

title: I Samuel 14:45
text: The most solemn engagements to commit sin can never be binding on the conscience, and should never in any case be fulfilled.  The guilt in such cases is not in breaking the engagement, but in making it; and the fulfilment of it would only increase the sin.

title: I Samuel 14:47
text: Zobah; a part of Syria north-east of Canaan.

title: I Samuel 14:48
text:
Amalekites; south and south-east of Canaan. 
 
Civil government, though administered by wicked men, may be the means of protecting God's people, and procuring for them blessings which lay them under new obligations to honor him, and to do good, as they have opportunity, to their fellow men.

title: I Samuel 15:1
text: The reception of special favors lays men under special obligations to hearken attentively to the directions of God, and in all things to follow them.

title: I Samuel 15:2
text:
That which Amalek did;   
 
Though God may delay for a time to punish the wicked, yet he does not forget their sins, and unless they repent, he will in due time punish them according to their deserts.

title: I Samuel 15:4
text: Telaim; supposed to be a place in the southern part of Judah.

title: I Samuel 15:6
text:
Kenites; supposed to have been descendants of Jethro. 
 
  Ye showed kindness;  Exodus 40:38 Numbers 10:29-32:1 
 
Intimate associations with the wicked are dangerous, and we must separate ourselves from their sins, or we shall share in their punishment.

title: I Samuel 15:7
text:
From Havilah; in the east border of their country. 
 
  To Shur; in the west border.

title: I Samuel 15:8
text: All the people; all who fell into his hands.

title: I Samuel 15:9
text: God requires that some men should be put to death; and in sparing them we may as really rebel against him and expose ourselves to his wrath, a sin taking the life of those whom he requires to be preserved.

title: I Samuel 15:11
text: It repenteth me; he would change his conduct towards Saul on account of his sins, and would reject him from being king.  I Samuel 15:23-28

title: I Samuel 15:12
text:
To Carmel; a city in the south part of Judah. 
 
  A place; a monument of his victory.

title: I Samuel 15:13
text: Men often imagine that they have obeyed God and are entitled to his favor, when their obedience has been only external, and has extended only to a part of his commands.   I Samuel 15:20

title: I Samuel 15:14
text: Facts often show the falsehood of men's professions, and that however high they may stand in their own estimation, they are rebels in the sight of God.

title: I Samuel 15:16
text: The Lord's messengers must point out and condemn the sins of rulers as well as of people; and let nothing hinder them from declaring with plainness and fidelity the whole revealed will of God.

title: I Samuel 15:21
text: Wicked men when convicted of sin often try hard to throw the blame of it on others.

title: I Samuel 15:22
text: No external attention, even to things which God has commanded, can be accepted as a substitute for an obedient heart.  He is a Spirit, and to be accepted, men must obey him in spirit and in truth.

title: I Samuel 15:23
text: As the sin of witchcraft; in its guilt.

title: I Samuel 15:25
text: Multitudes are more anxious to stand well with their fellow men than with God, and often look for pardon to them rather than to him.

title: I Samuel 15:27
text: He laid hold upon the skirt of his mantle; Saul laid hold upon the skirt of Samuel's mantle, as if forcibly to detain him.

title: I Samuel 15:28
text: To a neighbor; David.

title: I Samuel 15:29
text:
The Strength; Jehovah, who had given Israel the victory. 
 
  Nor repent; he would not reverse the sentence he had pronounced against Saul.

title: I Samuel 15:32
text:
Delicately; or, with pleasure. 
 
  Bitterness--is past; he thought that as Saul had spared his life, he should not now be slain. 
 
When wicked menmost confidently imagine that they have escaped all danger, they may be the nearest to ruin.  There is and can be no security except in the friendship and protection of Jehovah.

title: I Samuel 16:1
text:
The Beth-lehemite; so called from his residing in Bethlehem. 
 
No sorrows should ever lead us to murmur at the dealings of God, or to neglect the duties to which he calls us.

title: I Samuel 16:2
text: When God requires men to engage in perilous services, they need not fear; if they trust in him and follow his directions, he will protect them and give them all desirable success.

title: I Samuel 16:4
text: Trembled at his coming; perhaps fearing that he had come to rebuke them for some neglect of duty.

title: I Samuel 16:5
text: Sanctify yourselves;  Exodus 19:10-15

title: I Samuel 16:7
text: As God looks upon the heart, and judges of men according to their real character, the great object of all should be, not outward appearance or external accomplishments merely, but internal purity and the exercise of such feelings as are pleasing to God.

title: I Samuel 16:11
text:
Sit down; to feast on the sacrifice. 
 
Those who are faithful in the duties of private life, will be most likely to be so in the duties of public life.

title: I Samuel 16:13
text: The Spirit of the Lord came upon David; to fit him to become king of Israel.

title: I Samuel 16:14
text:
Departed from Saul; thus he lost the qualifications which God had before given him for the successful discharge of public business. 
 
  An evil spirit from the Lord troubled him; the meaning seems to be that God gave him up the the power of an evil spirit, which from time to time assailed him, filling him with melancholy suspicion and ungovernable anger.

title: I Samuel 16:16
text: Thou shalt be well; they hoped that music would cheer up his spirits, and remove his difficulties.

title: I Samuel 16:17
text: Human expedients may for a time lessen one's sorrow; yet there is no permanent relief from the sad effects of sin but in heartily forsaking it, and believing in Jesus Christ, who died, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God.

title: I Samuel 17:1
text: Shochoh; a place in Judah between fifteen and eighteen miles south-west from Jerusalem, having a valley north of it, which is believed to be the ancient valley of Elah.  Azekah and Ephes-dammim were near to Shochoh.

title: I Samuel 17:2
text: By the valley of Elah; on the north side of it.

title: I Samuel 17:4
text: Whose height was six cubits and a span; a cubit was about eighteen inches, and a span about nine inches.

title: I Samuel 17:5
text:
Coat of mail; in the original, a coat of mail of scales; that is, made of thin plates of metal overlapping each other like the scales of a fish. 
 
  Five thousand shekels; nearly two hundred pounds.

title: I Samuel 17:6
text: Target; a smaller shield suspended between his shoulders, to be used when occasion might require.  The larger shield was carried before him by his armor-bearer.  Some, however, prefer to understand a javelin hung by a strap behind his back.

title: I Samuel 17:7
text: Six hundred shekels; about twenty-five pounds.

title: I Samuel 17:10
text: When distinguished strength and courage make men proud, adn lead them to trust in themselves and despise others, they often become the occasion of their ruin.

title: I Samuel 17:12
text: That Ephrathite of Beth-lehem-judah; so called from Ephratah, one of the names of Bethlehem.   I Samuel 16:1 Micah 5:2

title: I Samuel 17:17
text: Men in executing their projects often have no idea of the ends which God by them will accomplish.

title: I Samuel 17:22
text: Carriage; the articles which he had brought with him.  Carriage, in the old English use of the word, signifies baggage, vessels, etc., that one carries with him in journeying.

title: I Samuel 17:25
text:
Free; free from taxes and public burdens. 
 
Men are induced to perform much labor, and make many sacrifices, by the hope of reward; and God graciously points us to the joy set before us, as a motive to deny ourselves, take up the cross, and follow Christ.  Romans 8:24

title: I Samuel 17:28
text: Men naturally envy those who do better and are more honored than themselves, and no ties of relationship are any certain security against the effects of this evil and malignant passion.   James 4:5

title: I Samuel 17:32
text: Confidence in God is a source of the highest and noblest courage, the most self-sacrificing devotion to duty, and the most exalted virtue.

title: I Samuel 17:34
text: Past experience of the readiness and power of God to help, encourages men to trust in him, and to expect from him in future all which they need.

title: I Samuel 17:38
text: The devices and efforts of men to aid us often prove a hinderance instead of a help, and we must renounce dependence on them and depend on God in our efforts, in order to meet with success.

title: I Samuel 17:39
text:
Assayed; attempted. 
 
  Not proved them; not been accustomed to them, and could not readily use them.

title: I Samuel 17:40
text: True dependence on God leads men not to neglect appropriate means, but in the right way to use them.  Thus, while they work, God works by them in securing the result, and preparing them to give him the glory.

title: I Samuel 17:43
text: Pride goeth before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.  Proverbs 16:18

title: I Samuel 17:45
text: In the name of the Lord; by his direction, with confidence in him, and for the purpose of promoting his cause.

title: I Samuel 17:46
text: One great design of Jehovah in all his dealings, is to make known his character, and show to the universe that there is no one but himself who governs and controls in the kingdoms of nature, providence, and grace.

title: I Samuel 17:51
text: The strongest as well as the weakest are dependent upon God, and that expectation which rests on creatures is liable at any time to be disappointed.

title: I Samuel 17:55
text: Services performed for men may by them be forgotten, and those who render them pass out of mind; but services done for God he always remembers, and will graciously reward.

title: I Samuel 18:1
text: Real excellence of character forms the surest basis for ardent and durable friendship, and those who rightly cultivate it on earth may hope to enjoy it for ever in heaven.

title: I Samuel 18:5
text: The presence and favor of God are the grand source of all true wisdom, and the surest guarantee of durable success.

title: I Samuel 18:6
text: Tabrets; or timbrels; a sort of small drum.

title: I Samuel 18:8
text: An envious disposition tends to torment him who indulges it, and all who feel its influence.

title: I Samuel 18:9
text: Saul eyed David; he watched him with jealous feelings.

title: I Samuel 18:10
text:
Prophesied; under the influence of the evil spirit, the king imitated the manner of speaking that belonged to the true prophets when they were under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit. 
 
  A javelin; a light spear pointed with metal.

title: I Samuel 18:11
text: There is no wickedness so great but the human heart, unrestrained by divine grace, may commit it.

title: I Samuel 18:15
text: Rulers often regard their own glory more than the public good, and seek to destroy those whom the people delight to honor.   Luke 19:47-48

title: I Samuel 18:17
text: What men will not do directly, they often attempt to do indirectly, and thus try to cast the responsibility of their evil actions on others.

title: I Samuel 18:18
text: What is my life; what is my condition of life?  or, as we say, What are my circumstances?  He imitates that they are too humble to allow him to think of such an alliance.  Compare  I Samuel 28:23 .

title: I Samuel 18:25
text: Dowry; among the Hebrews, and generally, in the East, a compensation or present made by the bridegroom to the father of the bride.

title: I Samuel 18:26
text: The days; previous to the time appointed for his marriage.

title: I Samuel 18:29
text: The more one is favored in the course of divine Providence, the more will envious men hate him.

title: I Samuel 18:30
text: Went forth; to fight with Israel.

title: I Samuel 19:1
text: Envy indulged often leads to murder, and many are in heart guilty of this sin wo are prevented from outwardly ocmmitting it.   I John 3:15

title: I Samuel 19:3
text: In the field; where Jonathan expected his father would walk.

title: I Samuel 19:4
text: Real love will seek the good of the object beloved, and if need be, perform labors, make sacrifices, and meet dangers to promote it.

title: I Samuel 19:6
text: Sound reason and kind persuasion may for a time overcome passion; but without a change of heart, when depravity is restrained in one direction it will break out in another.

title: I Samuel 19:10
text: When one is given up to the power of evil, not only engagements but solemn oaths will be disregarded, and malignant passions will overcome all restraint.

title: I Samuel 19:17
text: Those who hate others, and treat them as enemies, are apt to feel that others hate them and are their enemies.

title: I Samuel 19:18
text: Naioth; a place in Benjamin, near to Ramah.

title: I Samuel 19:20
text: The hearts of all are in the hands of the Lord, and he can turn them whithersoever he will.  No devices will succeed against those whom he designs to bless, and no evils will come upon them which he will not overrule for their good.

title: I Samuel 19:24
text:
His clothes; his outer garments. 
 
  Naked; without his upper garments.

title: I Samuel 20:1
text: This is a state of trial, and even obedience to God will not keep a person from sufferings; yet it will cause them to be overruled for his good and the good of others.

title: I Samuel 20:5
text: The new moon; the beginning of the month, when it was customary for relatives to unite in a sacrifice and a feast.

title: I Samuel 20:10
text: The certainty that David would be king did not render it unnecessary for him to use means to preserve his life; nor does the promise of God, to keep his children to the end, render unnecessary their own diligent prayers and efforts to persevere in faith and holiness.  It is through the use of appropriate means, and not without them, that the end will be accomplished.

title: I Samuel 20:12
text: Sounded; learned his state of mind.

title: I Samuel 20:14
text: The kindness--that I die not; it was common, when one began to reign, for him to put to death those who were supposed to have a claim to the throne.

title: I Samuel 20:15
text:
My house; his posterity. 
 
The conduct of parents may deeply affect not only their children, but their distant posterity, and each one should so act as shall attend to secure blessings to all who come after him, to the end of time.

title: I Samuel 20:16
text: Require it; take vengeance on either party, should they break this covenant.

title: I Samuel 20:18
text: Thy seat; at the family feast.

title: I Samuel 20:19
text: The stone Ezel; this was apparently a way-stone.

title: I Samuel 20:22
text: Hath sent thee away; in order to preserve his life.

title: I Samuel 20:23
text: An habitual conviction that the Lord is witness of all we do, that we shall stand before him in judgment, and be treated for eternity according to our works, tends to make us circumspect, upright, and faithful.

title: I Samuel 20:26
text: He is not clean; Saul thought that David was ceremonially unclean, and had kept away on that account.

title: I Samuel 20:27
text: An appearance of kindness may cover a murderous heart, and no crime is so abominable that a supremely selfish heart, under strong temptation, may not commit it.

title: I Samuel 20:31
text: Men in saying, I will, or, He shall, often speak as if events depended solely on themselves, whereas they depend on God; and men ought ever to feel, that if the Lord will, they shall live and do this or that.  James 4:15

title: I Samuel 20:39
text: Men often promote more benevolent objects, and accomplish greater good, than they are aware of; and all who faithfully do their duty, however humble their condition, when they see the results of their labors, will admire the grace of God, and be filled with gratitude and joy.

title: I Samuel 20:40
text: Artillery; weapons.

title: I Samuel 21:1
text:
Nob; a city of Benjamin. 
 
  Ahimelech; one of the descendants of Eli. 
 
  Was afraid; that there was a difficulty between David and Saul, and that it might be dangerous to entertain him. 
 
  No man with thee; no one of his customary retinue.  He was not absolutely alone, but appeared at Nob as a private person. 
 
Elevated situations are often places of peculiar trials, and from the height of worldly prosperity men may suddenly fall into deep distresses; we should therefore not put our trust in men, nor even in princes, but in the living God, who hath said to all who trust in him, I will never leave nor forsake thee.

title: I Samuel 21:2
text: When men are guilty of falsehood for the sake of obtaining a present good, they know not what evils they may occasion to themselves and others.   I Samuel 22:9-22

title: I Samuel 21:4
text: Hallowed bread;  Exodus 25:30

title: I Samuel 21:5
text:
In a manner common; every Sabbath, the bread which had stood on the table during the week was taken away to be eaten by the priests, and new bread was put in its place.  The old bread which had been taken from the table, was that of which David and his men partook.  Matthew 12:3 Mark 2:25-26  
 
  Though it were sanctified; since other bread is this day sanctified, or put in its place.   I Samuel 21:6

title: I Samuel 21:7
text:
Detained; for the purpose, it is supposed, of performing some religious service. 
 
Men may externally attend on the worship of God, and yet in their hearts be opposed to him, and when tempted, may even destroy those with whom, in the forms of devotion, they have united.

title: I Samuel 21:10
text:
Achish; this was his proper name as an individual, while Abimelech, that is, king's father, was the common hereditary title.  Compare the title of Psalms 34:1-22  and  Genesis 20:2 Genesis 26:1 . 
 
It is sometimes more safe to be among the heathen, than among those who have enjoyed the light of revelation and have abused it--who in words profess friendship to Jehovah, but in works deny him.

title: I Samuel 21:12
text: Sore afraid; lest Achish should think that he had come for some evil purpose, and should treat him as an enemy.

title: I Samuel 22:1
text: Adullam; in the tribe of Judah.

title: I Samuel 22:3
text:
Mizpeh; in Moab, on the east of Jordan. 
 
The distresses of children occasion great anxiety to parents, and right-minded children will strive to alleviate their sorrows, and as far as Providence may permit, to provide for their wants.

title: I Samuel 22:5
text:
Hareth; in the land of Judah. 
 
While we exercise our own best judgment, we should feel our need of divine guidance, seek wisdom from above, and be ready to go wherever God calls.

title: I Samuel 22:6
text: In Ramah; or, in a high place.

title: I Samuel 22:7
text: Men are apt to judge others by themselves, and when they are supremely selfish to think that others are so too.

title: I Samuel 22:9
text:
I saw the son of Jesse;  I Samuel 21:1 
 
To exalt themselves, and gain the favor of those above them, many will occasion the ruin of others, and even imbrue their hands in the blood of the innocent.

title: I Samuel 22:11
text: His father's house; the descendants of Eli.

title: I Samuel 22:13
text: Hast inquired of God for him; that is, as Saul alleges, with a view to aid him in his plan to possess himself of the kingdom.

title: I Samuel 22:17
text: Tyrants who resolve to take the life of their fellow men will not be hindered by want of reasons, or be backward to contend that the public good requires it.

title: I Samuel 22:18
text:
Fourscore and five; thus was fulfilled the Lord's declaration to Eli,  I Samuel 2:31-36 I Samuel 3:12-14 . 
 
Rulers who require men to commit sin, will generally find some who are wicked enough to obey them.

title: I Samuel 22:22
text: To have been even the innocent occasion of the death of others is exceedingly distressing to an ingenuous mind, and much more distressing is it when it has been occasioned by their kindness to us or by our sins.

title: I Samuel 23:1
text: Keilah; south-west from Jerusalem.

title: I Samuel 23:2
text: A conviction of our dependence on God, and a disposition to seek his direction, are a good preparation for receiving his favor and securing success.

title: I Samuel 23:6
text: An ephod in his hand; this is supposed to have been the high-priest's ephod, containing the breastplate with Urim and Thummim. Upon the death of Ahimelech this was saved by Abiathar in his flight, and David consulted God by it.

title: I Samuel 23:7
text: Men are apt to interpret the providences of God, and a disposition to seek his direction, are a good preparaton for receiving his favor and securing success.

title: I Samuel 23:12
text: It is not uncommon for men to return evil for good, and requite their benefactors with base ingratitude.

title: I Samuel 23:14
text: Wilderness of Ziph; a rough, hilly region in the tribe of Judah south-east of Hebron.

title: I Samuel 23:16
text:
Strengthened his hand in God; encouraged him to hope in God, and expect deliverance from him. 
 
Pious friendship delights in giving comfort in distress, by raising expectations from, and inspiring hope in Jehovah.

title: I Samuel 23:19
text: Jeshimon; meaning wilderness, or desert.

title: I Samuel 23:21
text: Men sometimes invoke the blessing of the Lord in the pursuit of objects which he abhors.

title: I Samuel 23:24
text: Maon; a place south of Ziph.

title: I Samuel 23:27
text: The Lord has a variety of ways in which he can protect his people, and he sometimes makes use of one enemy to deliver them from another.

title: I Samuel 23:28
text: Sela-hammah-lekoth; meaning, according to some interpreters, the rock of divisions; according to others, the rock of escape.

title: I Samuel 23:29
text: En-gedi; north-east of Maon, and on the border of the Dead sea; called also, Hazezon-tamar.   Genesis 14:7 II Chronicles 20:2

title: I Samuel 24:2
text:
Rocks of the wild goats; the wild, uncultivated regions inhabited by those animals. 
 
Where the heart is not duly humbled and turned from the love of sin, men will continue in some form to practise it.  When disappointed in one way they will pursue it in another, and nothing but the grace of God will lead them wholly to forsake it.

title: I Samuel 24:3
text: A cave; caves in that country are often large enough to contain hundreds of men.

title: I Samuel 24:4
text: We should be very careful not to interpret the opportunity and inclination for iniquity as a license from God to commit it.

title: I Samuel 24:5
text: David's heart smote him; fearing he had done wrong in cutting off Saul's skirt, and had not treated him whom God had made king with proper respect.

title: I Samuel 24:6
text: Conscientious regard to propriety in the treatment of those whom God has raised to be rulers, will ever characterize his enlightened and consistent friends.  Yet this will not lead them to justify their errors, nor hinder them from condemning their vices.

title: I Samuel 24:7
text: To be accepted of God, we must not only abstain from evil ourselves, but must use our influence to prevent it in others.

title: I Samuel 24:9
text: It is highly honorable to religion, when the conduct of its friends shows that the slanders of their enemies are false.

title: I Samuel 24:13
text:
Wickedness--from the wicked; if David had been wicked, and sought Saul's life, he would have killed him.  But as he did not, it showed that he was not thus wicked. 
 
The conduct of men is the best evidence of their character, and they should ever so act as to show supreme regard to God and good will to men.

title: I Samuel 24:14
text: After a dead dog; one insignificant and worthless.

title: I Samuel 24:16
text: Wicked men often see that they are wicked, that the righteous are more excellent and more happy than they, and that their end will be more glorious.

title: I Samuel 24:21
text: Not destroy my name; by cutting off his posterity.

title: I Samuel 25:1
text:
At Ramah; the place where he was born, and had lived. 
 
  Paran; near the southern border of Judah. 
 
The removal by death of the wise and good is a just cause of lamentation to the living, and should lead to fervent prayer that God would raise up others to fill their places, and carry forward his work.

title: I Samuel 25:2
text: Carmel; a few miles south of Hebron.  It should be distinguished from mount Carmel on the Mediterranean.

title: I Samuel 25:6
text: Kind feelings manifested in kind words and actins, even towards the evil and unthankful, are means of great good to those who indulge them, and tend to the good of all who feel their influence.

title: I Samuel 25:8
text: Whatsoever cometh to thy hand; what he had and could conveniently spare.

title: I Samuel 25:10
text: Unkindness and reproaches torment those who indulge in them, and often tempt others to commit sin.

title: I Samuel 25:14
text: Servants are often wiser and better than their masters, are more grateful for kindness, and more disposed to treat it as it deserves.

title: I Samuel 25:16
text: A wall unto us; they protected us.

title: I Samuel 25:18
text: A prudent wife is from the Lord, and may be the means in his hands of unspeakable good to her husband.

title: I Samuel 25:22
text:
So and more also do God; this was a kind of oath which David took that he would destroy every man belonging to Nabal. 
 
Men who have nobly withstood great and sore temptations, may meanly give way to those which are small, and profanely resolve to commit such enormous crimes as would cover them with deserved and perpetual disgrace.

title: I Samuel 25:24
text:
This iniquity; the blame belonging to her husband for so basely treating David and his men. 
 
  Audience; hearing

title: I Samuel 25:25
text: Nabal; meaning folly.

title: I Samuel 25:26
text:
Hath withholden thee; by sending Abigail to persuade him not to do as he had intended. 
 
All the wisdom needful in conducting a difficult concern, and all the success of human efforts in accomplishing it, come from God, and to him the wise and the good will give the glory.

title: I Samuel 25:27
text: This blessing; the present she had brought.

title: I Samuel 25:28
text: Make my lord a sure house; establish and prosper him in his kingdom.

title: I Samuel 25:29
text:
A man; Saul. 
 
  Soul; life. 
 
  Bound in the bundle; surely be preserved. 
 
  Sling out; destroy or reject them.

title: I Samuel 25:30
text: When one is raised by God to a station of great power and influence, it is a source of much pleasure to be able to look back and see that he has not swerved from the path of truth and duty in order to obtain it.

title: I Samuel 25:32
text: However great the blessings which come through the instrumentality of creatures, we should not overlook the Creator, or fail to acknowledge his gracious agency in the affairs of men; nor while we acknowledge him as the source of all good, should we fail to be grateful to the voluntary and benevolent instruments through which his goodness is bestowed.

title: I Samuel 25:34
text: None but God knows how many evils may be averted from a foolish and wicked husband by a pious, prudent, and energetic wife.

title: I Samuel 25:36
text: A person when drunk is ordinarily not in a condition to be benefited by conversation, and it is not usually wise, while he is in that state, to attempt to converse with him.

title: I Samuel 25:37
text: His heart died; he was overcome and became senseless.

title: I Samuel 25:38
text: Many a drunkard, after lying for a time as dead, has been smitten by the Lord, and in less than ten days has gone to the drunkard's grave; and no one who falls into the drunkard's sleep can avoid the danger of awaking in the drunkard's eternity.

title: I Samuel 25:43
text: Men who see and acknowledge the duty and the blessedness of obeying God, and in some things actually do it; in other things, when tempted, are sometimes left openly to rebel against him, and thus pierce themselves and others through with many sorrows.

title: I Samuel 26:2
text: Whatever promises of reformation men may make, unless they are led to hate sin they will continue in some form to commit it; and after temporary and partial reformation, if they go back, they often become worse than before.

title: I Samuel 26:5
text: No one, when closing his eyes to sleep, can tell to what dangers he may be exposed before he awakes.  Each one should therefore examine and see whether he is prepared for whatever may befall him, and commit himself and all his interests to Jehovah, who alone can make him dwell in safety.

title: I Samuel 26:9
text: It is never necessary to do wrong in order to obtain any needful good, and confidence in God will lead a man, in the path of duty, to wait till He shall give him what he desires.

title: I Samuel 26:15
text: Confidence in men for protection and support is always liable to be disappointed, and none are or can be safe except those who put their trust in God.

title: I Samuel 26:19
text:
Let him accept an offering; if David had sinned, and on that account was persecuted, he would present the proper offering, and thus seek forgiveness and a termination of his distresses. 
 
  Go, serve other gods; by driving him out among the heathen, they had tempted and exposed him to idolatry.

title: I Samuel 26:20
text:
A flea--a partridge; a thing of small value, difficult to catch, and of little use when caught. 
 
Worldly men often pursue what it is very difficult to obtain, and what, if they should obtain it, would in the end do them little good.

title: I Samuel 26:21
text: For a man supremely to regard himself and seek his own glory, is foolish as well as wicked.  It exposes him to great vexation, and will end in total disappointment.

title: I Samuel 26:24
text: Those who seek to glorify God, and to promote the highest good of men, will in the end receive from him all which they can reasonably desire.

title: I Samuel 27:1
text: Persons who at one time exercise strong confidence in God, may at another be guilty of great unbelief, and instead of seeking his guidance, may trust to their own wisdom, and bring upon themselves and others many sorrows.

title: I Samuel 27:2
text:
Unto Achish; this act of David, in seeking to ally himself to a heathen ruler after he had received so many signal deliverances from God, seems to have been the fruit not of faith but of unbelief; and it was the occasion of his being led into one wrong deed after another. 
 
  Gath; the easternmost city of the Philistines, near the border of Judah.

title: I Samuel 27:5
text:
Grace; favor. 
 
The people of God are sometimes more persecuted by his professed friends, than by the heathen; and have fled to the one, to escape the violence of the other.

title: I Samuel 27:6
text: Ziklag; a town allotted first to Judah, which afterwards fell to Simeon, and was now occupied by the Philistines.

title: I Samuel 27:8
text:
Geshurites--Gezrites--Amalekites; people south of Judea. 
 
  Shur; a region between Palestine and Egypt.

title: I Samuel 27:10
text:
Jerahmeelites; descendants of Jerahmeel, who was of the tribe of Judah.   I Chronicles 2:9   They lived in the southern part of Judah. 
 
  Kenites; a people near the Jerahmeelites.  The deception practised by David on Achish is not mentioned to be commended.  It proceeded not from faith in God, but from a worldly spirit that seeks deliverance by worldly policy. 
 
Intimate connections with the wicked are sources of great temptation, and those who needlessly expose themselves cannot rationally expect to escape unharmed.

title: I Samuel 27:12
text: Therefore; supposing from David's equivocal answer that he had fought the Israelites.

title: I Samuel 28:2
text:
What thy servant can do; Achish understood David to mean, what he would do in favor of the Philistines; though he did not say that, but gave, as in  I Samuel 27:10 , an equivocal reply. 
 
  Keeper of my head; captain of his body-guard. 
 
When men equivocate to get out of one difficulty, they often plunge into a greater, and unless the grace of God do better for them than they do for themselves, they will sink into utter ruin.

title: I Samuel 28:3
text: Those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards; persons who pretended to have conversations with evil spirits, and by their aid to foretell future events.

title: I Samuel 28:4
text:
Shunem; in the tribe of Issachar. 
 
  Gilboa; a mountain near Shunem, and at the south-east side of the valley of Jezreel. 
 
When godly magistrates and ministers of religion are removed the people become peculiarly exposed, and if on account of their sins God have departed from them, their enemies may be expected to triumph.

title: I Samuel 28:6
text: By Urim; as worn by the high-priest.   Exodus 28:30 Numbers 27:21

title: I Samuel 28:7
text:
A woman that hath a familiar spirit; in the original, "a woman mistress of a familiar spirit;" that is, one who claimed to have such a spirit at her command--her familiar, as it were, that would come at her call--and to be able to obtain from it the knowledge of secret things.  This seems to have been a false pretence, kept up by jugglery and cheating; but even if we were to suppose such conversation with familiar spirits to be a reality, its wickedness would be none the less, for it would be nothing else than resorting to created spirits for that knowledge which God keeps in his own power.  All such conversation with the spirits of the dead, or spirits of any other order, God has strictly forbidden.  It withdraws men's love and confidence from himself and his word and Spirit, and its reward will be such as Saul received on mount Gilboa.   I Chronicles 10:13  
 
  En-dor; east of Shunem. 
 
Those who have resisted great light, and long continued in open disobedience to known commands of God, often commit sins which they once had earnestly opposed, and go from one degree of iniquity to another, till they become their own destroyers.

title: I Samuel 28:10
text:
Saul sware to her; in doing this, he swore that he would not obey God.   Exodus 22:18  
 
Men who wish to commit crimes themselves are often ready to connive at them in others, and if need be, to bind themselves by awful imprecations to secure them from punishment.

title: I Samuel 28:11
text: Bring me up Samuel; witches pretended to be able to do this, though it was a false pretence.

title: I Samuel 28:12
text:
When the woman saw Samuel; if he really appeared, it was not she, or an evil spirit, that brought him up, but it was God, who sent him to denounce the death of Saul. 
 
  Thou art Saul; what there was connected with the appearance of Samuel's form, that revealed to the woman the fact that it was Saul who was consulting her, is not stated, and conjuctures upon it would be vain.

title: I Samuel 28:13
text: I saw gods ascending; or a god,  I Samuel 28:14 .  She seems herself to have been surprised and affrighted at what she saw.

title: I Samuel 28:15
text:
Why hast thou disquieted me; from my rest in the world of spirits; that is, Why hast thou been the occasion of it? 
 
If men continue in sin, God will at length depart from them, and they will then find no effectual help from heaven, earth, or hell.

title: I Samuel 28:17
text: To him; that is, done for himself.

title: I Samuel 28:18
text: Thou obeyedst not;  I Samuel 15:9 I Samuel 15:23-26:1

title: I Samuel 28:19
text:
With me; with the dead. 
 
Though none suffer except for their own sins, nor more than they deserve, yet ungodly parents may be the means of great distress to their children, and ungodly rulers of great calamities to their people.

title: I Samuel 28:22
text: Men may as well expect to have health and strength without eating, drinking, or sleeping, as to be blessed here or hereafter without obeying God.  They may say, He is good, and his is almighty.  This is true, but it will not save them from death, temporal nor eternal.

title: I Samuel 29:1
text: Aphek; in Issachar, not far from Gilboa.

title: I Samuel 29:2
text:
By hundreds, and by thousands; that is, having the men under their charge arranged in divisions of hundreds and thousands. 
 
  Passed on in the rearward with Achish; by dissimulation and false-hood David had ingratiated himself into the friendship and confidence of Achish, and been made keeper of his life.  The consequence was that he now found himself in a very embarrassing situation.  He must accompany Achish to the war against Israel, and there either betray the man who had honored him with his highest confidence, or fight it against his own country-men.  From this dilemma it pleased God to deliver him through the distrust of the lords of the Philistines; a deliverance, however, on which he had no right to calculate. 
 
The fact that men have so often been assembled by hundreds and thousands for the sake of destroying one another, shows the awful depravity of the human heart, and the necessity of its being changed by the Holy Spirit before men will love one another as they love themselves, or do to others as they would that others should do to them.

title: I Samuel 29:4
text:
His place; Ziklag. 
 
  His master; Saul. 
 
  With the heads of these men; by killing the Philistines.

title: I Samuel 29:6
text: When men have brought themselves into difficulty, the Lord often graciously delivers them, and by means which they never thought of, and for purposes wholly unexpected; and when afterwards they see the ends which he had in view, they behold new manifestations of his wisdom, kindness, and grace.

title: I Samuel 29:8
text: That I may not go fight; he seems to have said this for the purpose of maintaining his reputation for loyalty towards Achish.  Thus one act of dissimulation led to another.

title: I Samuel 30:1
text:
The south; the south part of Judea, where Ziklag was situated. 
 
We can never be certain when we leave our friends, that we shall again meet them in this world.  We should therefore commit them and ourselves heartily to the care of God, and endeavor so to act that if we meet them not again on earth, we may be prepared to meet them in heaven.

title: I Samuel 30:4
text: No one beforehand can tell how great may be his calamities, how soon or suddenly they may come upon him, or how deeply they may afflict him.

title: I Samuel 30:6
text:
Spake of stoning him; for leaving their wives and children exposed and defenceless. 
 
  Encouraged himself in the Lord; by remembering what God had already done for him, and what He had promised to do. 
 
It is not wise under troubles to vent reproaches on others, or to give up in despair; we should rather confess and forsake our sins, seek help from God, and endeavor to learn and do his will.

title: I Samuel 30:9
text: The brook Besor; a small stream which empties into the Mediterranean south of Gaza.

title: I Samuel 30:10
text: All cannot endure the same fatigue, or perform the same amount of labor; but if from love to God and men we do what we can, he will see that we are not left destitute, but partake with others in the rich blessings of his grace.

title: I Samuel 30:12
text:
His spirit came again; he was revived and strengthened. 
 
Servants who are destitute of property are liable when sick greatly to suffer, and sometimes even to die from want, and those who with right feelings assist them will not fail of an abundant reward.

title: I Samuel 30:14
text:
Cherethites; Philistines.   I Samuel 30:16  
 
  The south of Caleb; this was probably "the south land" given by Caleb to Othniel and his daughter Achsah, upon their marriage.  Joshua 15:19

title: I Samuel 30:16
text: Great prosperity tempts to sensual indulgence, and is often the means and forerunner of speedy and utter ruin.

title: I Samuel 30:22
text: Selfishness is hard-hearted and cruel, ungrateful and wicked.  It would keep all it can get, and leave others, equally deserving, to destitution and death.

title: I Samuel 30:26
text: A benevolent mind takes pleasure in giving; its happiness is increased by imparting to others, and thus enabling them to become partakers of its joys.

title: I Samuel 30:27
text:
vv 27-31. 
 
The places here mentioned were those visited by David in the south of Judea.

title: I Samuel 31:2
text: Good men are, in the natural order of things, more or less involved in the calamities which wicked rulers bring upon themselves, and the state intrusted to their care.

title: I Samuel 31:4
text: The wicked are more afraid of men than they are of God, and seek the praise of men more than the praise of God.

title: I Samuel 31:6
text: Though the righteous and the wicked may here live and die together, yet in eternity they will be separated and be in states as diverse as heaven is from hell.

title: I Samuel 31:9
text: It matters little where the body is, or how it is treated after death, if the soul is freed from sin and happy with God in heaven; for the body in that case will soon rise in the likeness of Christ's glorified body, and with the soul shine for ever like the sun in the kingdom of God.

title: I Samuel 31:10
text:
Beth-shan; on the west of Jordan, and north-east of mount Gilboa. 
 
The final reward of resorting to unlawful means for deliverance from trouble and the maintenance of earthly power and honor, will be shame and ruin.

title: I Samuel 31:11
text: Jabesh-Gilead; in the tribe of Manasseh, east of Jordan.

title: I Samuel 31:12
text: The character of truly noble men appears most clearly in times of deep distress.

title: II Samuel 1:1
text: When David was returned;

title: II Samuel 1:2
text: Many will pay court to those who are to have power, hoping in this way to obtain their favor and gain promotion.

title: II Samuel 1:10
text: The courses wicked men take for their own advancement, often prove the occasion of their ruin.

title: II Samuel 1:11
text: Rent them; in token of anguish.

title: II Samuel 1:12
text: A good man will not desire the death even of his bitterest enemy, though it would open the way to his own elevation, influence, and honor.

title: II Samuel 1:14
text: The Lord's anointed; him whom God had anointed to be king.

title: II Samuel 1:17
text: It is proper to lament the death of those with whom we have been connected; and while we bow with submission to the afflicting hand of God, we should acknowledge with gratitude his goodness in the natural endowments as well as the spiritual blessings which he bestowed on them.

title: II Samuel 1:18
text:
The bow; some suppose this to be the title of the poem which follows.  2Sa 1.29-27 
 
  The book of Jasher;  Joshua 10:1

title: II Samuel 1:19
text: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places; that is, Saul and Jonathan, here called the beauty or glory of Israel.

title: II Samuel 1:21
text: As though he had not been anointed with oil; he has perished in dishonor, as though he had been a common man, and not the Lord's anointed.

title: II Samuel 1:23
text:
Lovely and pleasant; that is, in their relation to each other. Though Jonathan was the firm friend of David, yet he remained faithful to his father; and Saul, except in some moments of jealousy, honored Jonathan with his entire confidence.   I Samuel 20:2   It is worthy of remark how David mentions what was good in Saul, omitting his faults. 
 
vv 23-24 In speaking of the dead it is proper to omit all notice of their faults, except when the cause of truth requires that they be mentioned.

title: II Samuel 1:24
text: Clothed you in scarlet--put on ornaments of gold; the reference is probably to the spoil taken from the enemies of Israel, with which he enriched the Israelitish women.

title: II Samuel 1:26
text: The most intimate and endearing friendships must soon be broken; but if founded in true piety, they will be revived again never to be interrupted, but to become more and more intimate and endearing for ever.

title: II Samuel 2:1
text:
Hebron; the chief city of Judah before David chose Jerusalem as his residence.  It lay in the central part of the territory of Judah, in a mountainous region; was an ancient and honorable city; and was every way suitable to be his residence while he reigned over Judah alone. 
 
Men who in all their ways acknowledge God, seek direction from him, and are disposed to follow his guidance, will see the path of duty, and in walking in it will find great reward.

title: II Samuel 2:3
text:
Cities of Hebron; towns near Hebron and dependent upon it. 
 
Those who have befriended and assisted us in adversity, should be gratefully remembered and duly honored by us in prosperity.

title: II Samuel 2:4
text:
Anointed David king; by the first anointing under Samuel's hand he had been designated by God as the future king; by the present anointing he was solemnly inducted into office. 
 
  Buried Saul;

title: II Samuel 2:5
text: Gratitude and kindness to benefactors are not only right, but the surest means of securing gratitude and kindness in return, and thus promoting the good of all concerned.

title: II Samuel 2:8
text:
Mahanaim; a city on the east of Jordan, in the tribe of Gad. 
 
Men who aspire to power, and grasp at the possession of it without asking counsel of God or inquiring whether it is right, though they may for a time succeed, will in the end find it to be a source of vexation, bitterness, and sorrow.

title: II Samuel 2:9
text: The Ashurites; supposed to have been a region east of the Jordan. It must not be confounded with the tribe of Asher.

title: II Samuel 2:12
text: Gibeon; north-west of Jerusalem, in the tribe of Benjamin.

title: II Samuel 2:14
text:
Play before us; the meaning of this proposal was, that a chosen number from each army should make a trial of their strength in fighting. 
 
Warriors often treat the butchering of men as a matter of sport, and thus show themselves to be children of him who was a murderer from the beginning, and who as a roaring lion walketh about seeking whom he may devour.   John 8:44 I Peter 5:8

title: II Samuel 2:16
text: Helkath-hazzurim; meaning, according to some, the field of the strong men; according to others, the field of the swords.

title: II Samuel 2:18
text: Zeruiah; a sister of David.   I Chronicles 2:16

title: II Samuel 2:21
text:
Take thee his armor; he means to say, that if Asahel is determined to fight, he should choose some one over whom he could prevail. 
 
Ambition to be distinguished as a warrior has often proved a man's ruin, and from the height of expectation and effort he has fallen suddenly into an untimely grave.

title: II Samuel 2:26
text:
Bitterness in the latter end; the unrelenting persecution of your brethren will exasperate them and drive them to extremities, and thus bring great calamities on you as well as on them. 
 
Want of success in war often disposes men to peace, and leads them to speak very differently about the evils of war from what they did when it began; and though they have been the cause of their own troubles, they often try to throw the blame of them on others.

title: II Samuel 2:27
text:
Unless thou hadst spoken; that is, according to some, challenged the young men to combat,  II Samuel 2:14 .  Hadst thou in the morning of to-day shown a disposition for peace, my followers would have retired from thee in peace.  Others suppose him to mean, Unless thou hadst now spoken, the pursuit would not have ended till the morning of to-morrow. 
 
  Gone up; to the higher region of Hebron.

title: II Samuel 2:29
text: Bithron; a hilly country between the Jordan and Mahanaim.

title: II Samuel 3:1
text: Though the accomplishment of divine promises may for a time be delayed, yet all things will conspire to their ultimate fulfillment.

title: II Samuel 3:2
text: Men who depart form the original constitution of God with regard to marriage, will find the way of transgressors hard, and may expect, through life, to reap the sad fruits of their folly.

title: II Samuel 3:3
text: Geshur; a country on the east of Jordan near mount Hermon.

title: II Samuel 3:8
text: Men often revolt form the charge, and even from the suspicion of crime, who have no hesitation in committing it.

title: II Samuel 3:12
text: Selfish and ambitious men when disappointed in one quarter will turn to another; and in prosecuting their objects will sell themselves to the highest bidder.

title: II Samuel 3:13
text: Michal;  I Samuel 25:1

title: II Samuel 3:16
text: Bahurim; in the tribe of Benjamin, not far from Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 3:18
text: Such is the wickedness of men, that they will often act in opposition to what they know to be the revealed will of God.

title: II Samuel 3:20
text: When those who have been our enemies profess to become our friends, we may treat them as such, yet we cannot and ought not to repose full confidence in them till their professions are verified by their conduct.

title: II Samuel 3:25
text: Men may appear very anxious to accomplish one object, when they are looking principally at another; and may denounce others for deception, while they are seeking to practise it themselves.

title: II Samuel 3:26
text: The well of Sirah; supposed to have been near Hebron, to which city Abner was brought back by the emissaries of Joab.

title: II Samuel 3:34
text: So fellest thou; by the hand of an assassin.

title: II Samuel 3:39
text:
Weak--to hard; David was not able then to punish the murderers, on account of their great influence with the army. 
 
None are so high in authority and power that they can commit murder with impunity.  Though they should not be punished by men, the vengeance of God in due time will overtake them, and they will sink under his indignation.   I Kings 2:5-6 I Kings 2:32-34

title: II Samuel 4:1
text: A common method by which God overthrows nations and parties that oppose themselves to his righteous couse, is to take from them the wise and strong men to whom they trusted as leaders.

title: II Samuel 4:2
text: Beeroth; a city near Gibeon.

title: II Samuel 4:4
text:
The tidings came; of the death of Saul and Jonathan. 
 
Many are the dangers of life and limb to which little children are exposed, and the kindness of God in their preservation and comfort is constant and great.

title: II Samuel 4:6
text:
As though they would have fetched wheat; more literally, fetching wheat.  To conceal their guilty purpose they fetched wheat, as though this was their business. 
 
Rulers who depend for support only on soldiers, can never be safe; many who for a time fight against them and even take their life.

title: II Samuel 4:7
text: The plain; the Jordan valley, which lay between Mahanaim and Hebron.

title: II Samuel 4:8
text: Men often glory in iniquity, and speak of treason, bloodshed, and murder as if they were pleasing to God, and entitled the perpetrators to the gratitude of their fellow men.

title: II Samuel 4:9
text: Men who trust in God will not commit sin to accomplish his or their purposes; nor will they reward it or connive at it in others.

title: II Samuel 4:10
text: One told me;  II Samuel 1:2-6:1

title: II Samuel 4:11
text: A righteous person; innocent as to his murderers, one who had done them no wrong.

title: II Samuel 4:12
text: All who expect in the end to be gainers by the commission of sin, will meet with sure and woeful disappointment.

title: II Samuel 5:1
text:
Then came all the tribes; David had before reigned over only the tribe of Judah.   II Samuel 5:5  
 
Those who wait upon God in humble supplication and hearty obedience, will in due time, and in the best way, receive all which they need or can reasonably desire.

title: II Samuel 5:2
text: Feed my people; this is the first time a ruler is spoken of in the Bible under the emblem of a shepherd.

title: II Samuel 5:3
text: A clear definition and correct understanding of the mutual relations and duties of rulers and people tend to promote the stability of civil government and to increase its usefulness.

title: II Samuel 5:6
text:
Jerusalem; a portion of this city had continued to be inhabited by the Jebusites. 
 
  Except thou take--the blind and the lame; rather thus: Thou shalt not come in hither; but the blind and the lame shall take thee away; that is, though we had only the blind and lame, they could repel thee. 
 
Dependence on creatures is followed by sore disappointment; while dependence on God secures his blessing and leads to glorious success.

title: II Samuel 5:8
text: The lame and the blind; the Jebusites themselves, with allusion to their boast,  II Samuel 5:6 .

title: II Samuel 5:9
text: Millo; supposed to have been a apart of the fortress on mount Zion.

title: II Samuel 5:11
text: Tyre; a city of the Phenicians on the Mediterranean, near the northern border of Palestine.

title: II Samuel 5:12
text: Rulers are appointed and intrusted with authority for the good of the people, and are bound in all thier acts to seek this end.

title: II Samuel 5:13
text: Great prosperity increases the power of temptation, and often leads to great transgressions.

title: II Samuel 5:17
text:
The hold; a fortress, or fortified place. 
 
Such is the wickedness of men, that the increasing power and prosperity of one nation awakens the jealousy and provokes the hostility of another, and leads them to seek their own elevation by the depression or ruin of their neighbors.

title: II Samuel 5:18
text: Rephaim; a valley on the south-west of Jerusalem.

title: II Samuel 5:20
text:
Baal-perazim; meaning the plain of breaches; it was in the valley of Rephaim. 
 
One nation can gain no advantage over another, except such as God sees fit to grant, or for wise reasons to permit; and whenever he gives prosperity, he lays men under new obligations to obey him.

title: II Samuel 5:25
text: From Geba untl thou come to Gazer; in  I Chronicles 14:16  we read, "from Gibeon even to Gazer."  Geba was a short distance north of Jerusalem, and Gibeon a short distance north-west.  Gazer was on the western border of Ephraim.   Joshua 16:3

title: II Samuel 6:2
text:
Baale; another name for Kirjath-jearim. 
 
Rulers and people should without any unnecessary delay establish the worship of God, and regularly attend, according to his will, upon all the ordinances ofhis appointment.

title: II Samuel 6:3
text:
Upon a new cart; following in this the example of the Philistines; while the divine ordinance was that the ark should be reverently borne by the Levites, for which purpose it was provided with rings and bars.  Numbers 4:5-15  
 
  In Gibeah; rather, on the hill.

title: II Samuel 6:6
text:
Put forth his hand; this was contrary to the command of God.  Numbers 4:15-20  
 
Irreverence and rashness in our approaches to God and all disregard to his commands in our attendance on his worship, are offensive in his sight and expose men to his displeasure.

title: II Samuel 6:8
text: Perez-uzzah; meaning, the breach of Uzzah.

title: II Samuel 6:10
text:
The Gittite; so called, it is supposed, from Gath-rimmon, the place of his birth of abode. 
 
The displeasure of God against those who profane his worship, should not lead any to neglect it, for that will also displease him; while in properly attending upon it, they will secure his favor and receive a great reward.

title: II Samuel 6:13
text: They that bare the ark; it was now borne by the Levites, according to the divine direction.

title: II Samuel 6:14
text: Danced before the Lord; as a manifestation of joy in God and gratitude for his mercies.

title: II Samuel 6:16
text:
Despised him; she thought he was degrading himself. 
 
Ardent love to God and engagedness in his worship, are thought by many to be suitable only for the weak and ignorant; but they are in reality exalting and ennobling, and confer the highest and most durable honor upon persons of all descriptions.

title: II Samuel 6:18
text: Acts of piety should never be dissociated from those of charity and mercy; nor should the public duties of religion be disconnected from those of the family and the closet; but regular attendance on the one should be a preparation for the conscientious and habitual performance of the other.

title: II Samuel 6:20
text: Uncovered himself; he had laid aside his royal robes for the ephod of the priests,  II Samuel 6:14 .

title: II Samuel 6:21
text:
It was before the Lord; for the purpose of honoring him. 
 
  Will I play; or, I did play. 
 
Those who know by experience the pleasure and benefit of fervently worshipping God in spirit and in truth, will not be deterred from it by the sneers and scoffs of friends or foes; but will resolve in his strength, whatever others may do, to be more and more devoted, for time and eternity, to his service.

title: II Samuel 7:1
text: When men employ their seasons of rest and retirement in reviewing the goodness of God, and in devising plans for the promotion of his glory, much benefit may be expected to result to them, to their children, and to all who may feel their influence.

title: II Samuel 7:2
text: Within curtains; in the tabernacle.   II Samuel 6:17

title: II Samuel 7:7
text: The tribes; their rulers.

title: II Samuel 7:8
text: A faithful review of the goodness of God to us is suited to fill us with humility and self-abasement, and also with adoring gratitude and praise.

title: II Samuel 7:11
text: Make thee a house; give him posterity to succeed him on the throne of Israel.

title: II Samuel 7:12
text:
I will set up thy seed after thee; the immediate reference is to Solomon, but in such a way that it includes also the whole royal line, at the head of which, after David, Solomon stood; and which terminated in Christ, the son of David according to the flesh, to whom God gave the throne of his father David.   Luke 1:32-33   The complete fulfilment, therefore, of this prophecy can only be in Christ's everlasting kingdom. 
 
God, in giving parents reason to hope that when they die their children will imitate their good example, and execute the schemes of benevolence which they devise, greatly encourages them to call upon him, and to devote themselves with increasing fidelity to his glory and the good of their fellow men.   Genesis 18:18-19 II Timothy 1:4-6

title: II Samuel 7:14
text:
I will be his father, and he shall be my son; not the father of Solomon alone, considered as an individual, but of the whole royal line from Solomon to Christ; and the father of Christ in a preeminent sense. 
 
  With the rod of men; gently and for his good, as a kind father corrects his child.

title: II Samuel 7:16
text: Thy throne shall be established; it should not be taken away, as it was from Saul; but should continue in David's family till the coming of Christ, who, as King of his people, will reign for ever.

title: II Samuel 7:18
text:
Sat before the Lord; before the ark of the tabernacle. 
 
When the goodness of God leads men in humble and devout thanksgiving to himself, it shows that they are ripening for increasing manifestations and experience of his goodness for ever.

title: II Samuel 7:21
text: For thy word's sake, and according to thine own heart; David ascribes all God's gifts to him and his family, not to any goodness of his own, but to God's free promise, made according to the counsel of His own will.

title: II Samuel 7:24
text: To have Jehovah for their God, and to be governed by his laws, is the best defence and highest glory, not only of individuals and families, but of states and nations.

title: II Samuel 8:1
text: Metheg-ammah; meaning, the bridle of the metropolis; that is, Gath and her towns.   I Chronicles 18:1

title: II Samuel 8:2
text:
Casting them down to the ground; more literally, making them to lie down upon the ground.  The meaning seems to be, that he compelled the captives to lie down upon the ground in regular order, and then measured off two portions of them to be slain, and one to be preserved. 
 
Some are called to meet death, while others who appeared to be equally exposed are preserved alive.  But whoever may be the instruments, and in whatever way life is preserved, those who enjoy it are indebted for it to God, and are bound to devote it to him.

title: II Samuel 8:3
text: Zobah; a part of Syria north-east of Palestine.

title: II Samuel 8:4
text: Houghed; cut their hamstrings.

title: II Samuel 8:6
text: However exposed men may be to danger in doing the will of God, by putting their trust in him they may be safe.  He will protect them till their work on earth is accomplished, and then receive them to the rewards of grace in heaven.

title: II Samuel 8:9
text: Hamath; a city with its territory on the Orontes north of Damascus, and bordering on Zobah.

title: II Samuel 8:13
text: The valley of salt; south of the Dead sea, where David's general slew eighteen thousand Syrians, or Edomites united with the Syrians against him.   II Kings 14:7 I Chronicles 18:12   See the title to  Psalms 60:1 .

title: II Samuel 8:15
text: However successful in war any ruler may be, his chief glory consists in doing justly, loving mercy, walking humbly with God, and advancing, as far as may be in his power, the highest good of mankind.

title: II Samuel 8:16
text: Recorder; an officer appointed to record the events of the king's reign; an official historian.

title: II Samuel 8:17
text: Scribe; king's secretary.

title: II Samuel 8:18
text: The Cherethites and the Pelethites; supposed to have been David's body-guards.

title: II Samuel 9:1
text: True piety will be grateful, not only to God the author of all good, but to those who imitate him, and through whom his goodness is displayed; and it will manifest itself not only towards them, but when practicable towards others who are connected with them.

title: II Samuel 9:3
text: The kindness of God; kindness exercised in the fear of God, in accordance with his oath to Jonathan.   I Samuel 20:14-17

title: II Samuel 9:4
text: Lo-debar; east of Jordan, in the land of Gilead.

title: II Samuel 9:7
text:
Thy father; his grandfather. 
 
The good character and conduct of parents, and their kindness, especially to the distressed, are often followed by great blessings on their children.

title: II Samuel 9:8
text:
A dead dog; an expression of great unworthiness of such distinguished favors. 
 
A conviction of unworthiness, and true gratitude for favors, tend greatly to increase the liberality and usefulness of the giver, and also the happiness and benefit of the receiver.

title: II Samuel 9:10
text: May have food to eat; though Mephibosheth himself sat at the king's table, he needed a suitable provision for his household.

title: II Samuel 9:13
text:
Was lame;  II Samuel 4:1 
 
Bodily infirmities, though a present calamity to thise who suffer them, may be overruled for their highest good.

title: II Samuel 10:2
text: His father showed kindness unto me; this is supposed to have occurred while David was persecuted by Saul.

title: II Samuel 10:3
text: Selfish men, who intend when they can to deceive others, are ever ready to suspect that others intend to deceive them; and those who hearken to such counsellors, will be likely to be led by them into mischief.

title: II Samuel 10:4
text: Shaved off the one half of their beards; to the inhabitants of the East, the mutilating of the beard is considered a great disgrace.

title: II Samuel 10:5
text:
Jericho; one of the first towns to which they came, after crossing the Jordan on their return. 
 
Those who in the discharge of duty are dishonorably and basely treated, should not be cast down by the indignities of the wicked, and should receive from their friends special kindness.

title: II Samuel 10:6
text:
Beth-rehob; on the northern borders of Palestine, in the valleys of Lebanon. 
 
  Zoba; a part of Syria north-east of Palestine. 
 
  Ish-tob; rather, "the men of Tob."  The land of Tob was beyond Jordan,  Judges 11:3 . 
 
  King Maacah; or, the king of Maacah,  II Samuel 10:8 .  Maacah is supposed to have been at the foot of Hermon, near Geshur.   Deuteronomy 3:14  
 
Those who are most ready to give needless and wanton offence, are most backward to make amends for it, and often proceed from one offence to another till they are ruined.

title: II Samuel 10:8
text: The entering in of the gate; the gate of Medeba, a city in the tribe of Reuben, near the border of the Ammonites, and in their possession.   I Chronicles 19:7

title: II Samuel 10:9
text:
Before and behind; the Syrians on one side and the Ammonites on the other. 
 
  The Syrians; all the people named in  II Samuel 10:6 , as hired by the Ammonites. 
 
The fact that men are dependent on God, and that he gives success to whomsoever he will, does not supersede the necessity of their using the most appropriate means; for by such means God usually works, in accomplishing the end.

title: II Samuel 10:12
text: A conviction and acknowledgement of dependence on God for success in the use of means, is one of the surest ways of obtaining it.

title: II Samuel 10:16
text:
Hadarezer; the king of Zoba. 
 
  The river; Euphrates. 
 
All the efforts of men to thwart the counsels of God, and to succeed in opposition to him, will be in vain, and in the end will recoil on themselves.   Psalms 2:1-9

title: II Samuel 11:1
text:
The time when kings go forth; in the spring. 
 
  Rabbah; the capital of the Ammonites. 
 
Great prosperity, while it increases the power of temptation, lessens the firmness of resistance, and is often followed by the commission of the greatest crimes.

title: II Samuel 11:2
text: An evening-tide; the latter part of the afternoon.

title: II Samuel 11:4
text: Neither mercies nor trials, privileges nor obligations, reputation nor usefulness, will keep back the human heart, when left to itself, from the commission of the grossest and most enormous wickedness.

title: II Samuel 11:6
text:
The Hittite; one who descended from the Hittites, but had united with the Israelites. 
 
The commission of one sin increases the temptation to commit another and another, and, without the grace of God, the soul will go on adding sin to sin for ever.

title: II Samuel 11:8
text:
Wash thy feet; this was the custom after travelling, as they wore sandals, or soles tied to their feet; it was a great refreshment. 
 
All attempts to hide iniquity, and to prevent the final disclosure of it, are vain.  They may for a time screen it from the view of men, but God will at length bring it all to light.   Matthew 10:26

title: II Samuel 11:9
text: The servants of his lord; probably the soldiers who formed David's body-guard.

title: II Samuel 11:11
text: I will not do this thing; he resolved to be as self-denying as were the soldiers in the field.

title: II Samuel 11:14
text: The soul under the blinding, polluting, and hardening power of sin, can plot the ruin of a most devoted and self-denying friend, and no generous emotion keep it back from the guilt of shedding, with cool deliberation, a benefactor's blood.

title: II Samuel 11:21
text: Jerubbesheth; Jerubbal, Gideon.   Judges 6:32 Judges 8:35 Judges 9:53

title: II Samuel 11:25
text:
This thing; the loss of his men. 
 
Death-like moral insensibility is one of the fruits of allowed and continued iniquity; the soul under its influence can contemplate with indifference, and attempt to smooth over and even rejoice in the foulest transgression.  Let him that thinketh he standeth, take heed lest he fall.  He who trusteth in his own heart is a fool.  Proverbs 28:26 I Corinthians 10:12

title: II Samuel 12:1
text:
Nathan; a prophet of the Lord.   II Samuel 7:2  
 
Men may try ever so much to hide their iniquity, but all who commit it may be sure that in due time their sin will find them out.

title: II Samuel 12:2
text: Much knowledge of men and much skill are requisite in order most effectually to administer reproof, especially to rulers and men of high rank; and few methods are more suited to this, than wisely selected and graphic illustrations.

title: II Samuel 12:5
text: Those most indulgent to their own sins, are often most severe against the supposed sins of others.

title: II Samuel 12:6
text:
Fourfold;  Exodus 22:1 
 
Pity for those in distress is a duty so obvious, lovely, and universal, that those who have been most hardened and cruel themselves, when they see in others only a shadow of their own baseness, are ready indignantly to condemn it.

title: II Samuel 12:7
text: To rulers, as well as all other classes of people, the ministers of God, when called to it, should make a plain, personal, and faithful application of his truth.  Neither fear nor favor should hinder them from pointing out the wickedness of the most exalted sinner, and declaring, Thou art the man.

title: II Samuel 12:9
text:
Thou hast killed; a man is said to do, and is held responsible for doing, what he causes to be done. 
 
Great mercies bestowed on any one exceedingly aggravate the guilt of his transgressions, and render him deserving of an aggravated punishment.

title: II Samuel 12:10
text:
The sword shall never depart; there would be war and various distresses in his family to the end of his life.   II Samuel 11:11  
 
  Thou hast despised me; by regarding his own sinful gratification more than the will of God.

title: II Samuel 12:11
text:
I will take thy wives;  II Samuel 16:21-22:1 
 
God often causes men to read their sins in their punishment, and what they did in secret is punished before the world.

title: II Samuel 12:12
text: I will do this thing; it would take place in the course of God's providence, through the wickedness of Absalom, in violation of God's law, and to the great distress of David.

title: II Samuel 12:13
text:
Put away thy sin; so forgiven it, in view of his penitence, as expressed in  Psalms 51:1-19 , that he should not die according to the law,  Leviticus 20:10 . 
 
One of the first things in doing good to sinners, is to make them sensible of their sins, and lead them to condemn themselves, and feel that God would be just should he punish them as they deserve.

title: II Samuel 12:14
text: Though the truly penitent, however great their transgressions, will, for Christ's sake and through faith in him, be forgiven, yet many distressing effects of their sins they may experience to the end of life.

title: II Samuel 12:16
text: Lay all night upon the earth; in token of his sorrow for sin, his deep humiliatin, and his earnest desire that the child, if consistent with the will of God, might live.

title: II Samuel 12:20
text:
Washed and anointed--changed his apparel, and--worshipped; in token of his hearty submission to the manifested will of God. 
 
The true penitent, however he may desire and pray that his distresses may be removed or lessened, will heartily submit to those that God lays upon him; feeling that God doeth all things well, and saying, Not as I will, but as thou wilt.  Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him.  Matthew 26:39 Job 13:15

title: II Samuel 12:24
text: Solomon; meaning, peaceable.

title: II Samuel 12:25
text: Jedidiah; meaning, beloved of the Lord.

title: II Samuel 12:26
text: Fought against Rabbah; Joab was besieging Rabah when David committed the sin in respect to Uriah.  The sacred writer, having mentioned this great crime, proceeds with the account of its consequences as far as the birth of Solomon, before he returns to the history of the siege of Rabbah.  The capture of that city and the punishment of its people occurred in the interval, certainly before the birth of Solomon, and perhaps before the repentance of David.

title: II Samuel 12:27
