text: The practice of iniquity shows that the heart is turned away from God, and subjects the soul to his just indignation.  No previous favors, and no fulness or variety of earthly blessings, can then preserve it from trouble and sorrow.

title: I Kings 11:11
text: Thy servant; Jeroboam.

title: I Kings 11:13
text: One tribe; Judah, including also Benjamin.

title: I Kings 11:15
text: Every male; all that he could capture.

title: I Kings 11:18
text: Paran; south of Palestine, between Edom and Egypt.

title: I Kings 11:25
text: The wickedness of rulers tends greatly to corrupt their people, and often brings on them numerous long and dreadful calamities.

title: I Kings 11:26
text: Zereda; in the tribe of Ephraim.

title: I Kings 11:29
text: Shilonite; a native or inhabitant of Shiloh.

title: I Kings 11:31
text: When rulers and people become corrupt, public peace and prosperity will decline, and divisions, revolutions, and bloodshed may be expected to follow.

title: I Kings 11:34
text: God is merciful and gracious, not willing that men should perish, but that they should come to repentance; and punishments are sometimes delayed, and children suffered to live in the enjoyment of manifold blessings, out of regard to the piety and faithfulness of parents.

title: I Kings 11:38
text:
Build thee a sure house; cause his posterity to reign after him. 
 
The promises of God are connected with obedience.  If men walk in his ways, blessings will be granted, and may go down increasing to their children.  But if they rebel against him, they forfeit his favor, and may deprive not only themselves, but their posterity, of his mercies.

title: I Kings 11:41
text: The book; a record which was kept of the transactions of his reign.

title: I Kings 12:1
text: Shechem; in the tribe of Ephraim.   I Kings 12:25

title: I Kings 12:4
text: Governments should exist for the good of the people, and this should be sought in all their acts.

title: I Kings 12:7
text:
Be a servant; comply with their wishes. 
 
No enlightened and patriotic people can permanently be governed by mere force or fear.  Every wise ruler will therefore endeavor to conciliate his people, and secure their confidence and love.  This, old men who have long observed the course of events and are well acquianted with human nature, feel much more deeply than young men.

title: I Kings 12:10
text: Young men, especially those who have grown up in luxury and dissipation, without restraint, and under the influence of bad examples, are apt to be proud, self-confident, and overbearing; not only fond of power, but of making a display of it, and accomplishing their objects not by truth, reason, and moral influence, but by force.

title: I Kings 12:15
text:
The cause was from the Lord; he so ordered events in his providence as to fulfil his declarations.   I Kings 12:24  
 
When God leaves a man, especially a ruler, to follow pernicious counsels and his own wicked inclinations, it is evident that he is preparing to punish him, and those who are partakers in his sins.

title: I Kings 12:18
text: The tribute; the revenue of the kingdom.

title: I Kings 12:20
text: In the appointment of rulers, the agency of men and the agency of God are both concerned; and while the heart of man deviseth his way, the counsel of the Lord shall stand.

title: I Kings 12:25
text: Penuel; east of Jordan, on the river Jabbok.

title: I Kings 12:27
text:
If this people go up to do sacrifice; according to the Mosaic law all the males throughout Israel were required to go up to Jerusalem three times a year to the national feasts.  Jeroboam feared the influence of these annual visits upon the people, and determined to prevent them by corrupting the public worship of God.  Thus he set the supposed interests of his own family above the authority of God and the religious welfare of the people. 
 
  They shall kill me; this was in direct contradiction to what God had said, showing that he did not believe him.   I Kings 11:38 . 
 
Unbelief of God's declarations is a most fruitful source of trouble; and the wicked courses which men take to avoid apprehended evils, are often the means of bringing those evils upon them.

title: I Kings 12:29
text:
Beth-el;in the south part of his kingdom. 
 
  Dan; in the north part.

title: I Kings 12:30
text: Wicked rulers often wish to govern the church as well as the state, and to have no ministers of religion except such as will regard them more than God.

title: I Kings 12:31
text: A house of high places; a temple for the idolatrous worship at Dan, which the sacred writer first describes.

title: I Kings 12:32
text:
The eighth month; called Bul, and answering to a part of October and November. 
 
  Like unto the feast; the feast of tabernacles, celebrated in Jerusalem a month earlier.   Leviticus 23:39-44  
 
  So did he in Beth-el; as he had done in Dan.  The writer now proceeds to describe the idolatrous institutions at Beth-el.

title: I Kings 13:1
text:
By the word of the Lord; at his command. 
 
Shrewd worldly politicians know that men must have some religion, and they encourage that which they think will increase and perpetuate their power.  But in substituting one of their own devising for that which God requires, they incur his wrath and accelerate their own ruin.

title: I Kings 13:2
text:
Offer the priests of the high places; kill them, and burn their bones on the altar.   II Kings 23:20  
 
  Men's bones shall be burnt upon thee; the bones of men long since dead.   II Kings 23:16

title: I Kings 13:3
text:
A sign; a miracle, to show that God had sent him.   I Kings 13:5  
 
When God sends a message to men, he gives such evidence that it comes from him as ought to convince, and if rightly treated, will convince them; and if it does not, it is their own fault.

title: I Kings 13:6
text: God can easily and quickly bring the most bitter persecutors of his people into such a condition that they will earnestly desire and implore their help.

title: I Kings 13:8
text: The messengers of God should show that they regard him more than all earthly good, and no temptations should induce them to swerve from following his directions.

title: I Kings 13:15
text: God's people are sometimes tempted to disobey him, but they are never forced to do it; and if they do it, they displease him, and subject themselves to his rebuke.

title: I Kings 13:19
text:
He went back; instead of following the command of God: he had received his directions from God, and had no right to deviate from them until God himself had countermanded them.  That God had done so, he had no sufficient evidence. 
 
When God has clearly made known his will, we are not to follow the opposing counsels of men, however plausible they may seem.

title: I Kings 13:24
text: As no one knows the time or manner of his death, all should so live as to be prepared at any time to meet it, and hear the joyful sentence, Well done, good and faithful servant; enter thou into the joy of thy Lord.

title: I Kings 13:30
text: When those we have injured are dead, the recollection of our influence over them often gives us poignant sorrow.

title: I Kings 13:32
text: Samaria; a part of Canaan which lay between Judea and Galilee.

title: I Kings 13:33
text: We are often reminded that no mercies or judgments, promises or threatenings, without the grace of God, will lead men to forsake their sins and turn to him; and that whatever be his dealings, they will continue in transgression till they perish.

title: I Kings 14:1
text: Parents are often punished in the sickness of their children, and should be led by it to repentance of their sins, and hearty consecration of themselves to the service and glory of God.

title: I Kings 14:2
text: Men who profess to believe that God is acquainted with all things, often act as if they hoped to deceive him; but all such efforts are vain, and will end in disappointment and sorrow.

title: I Kings 14:3
text:
Cracknels; a kind of cakes. 
 
Men are frequently more anxious to know the secret purposes of God, than to know his will for the sake of doing it.

title: I Kings 14:5
text: Though age and infirmities may lessen or destroy the human senses, God can, and if men are disposed to obey him, he will, reveal to them all they need to know in order to understand and do their duty.

title: I Kings 14:7
text: A man's guilt is aggravated in proportion to the blessings he has abused; and in the same proportion, unless he repent, will be his punishment.

title: I Kings 14:8
text:
Followed me with all his heart; not that he did not commit great transgressions, but he repented of them, and was sincerely devoted to the service of God. 
 
In reading the Bible, we are often called to witness that many things which take place in the course of providence and are accomplished by human instrumentality, are spoken of as done by God.  I Kings 14:14-15 Jeremiah 51:39

title: I Kings 14:9
text: Cast me behind thy back; treated him as unworthy of regard.

title: I Kings 14:10
text: By obedience to God, parents may be the means of bringing on their children great blessings, and by disobedience, great evils.  I Kings 11:38

title: I Kings 14:13
text: Come to the grave; be buried with respect.

title: I Kings 14:14
text: Even now; what he predicted was certain and near.

title: I Kings 14:15
text:
As a reed is shaken; they would be subject to perpetual commotions. 
 
  Beyond the river; the river Euphrates.   II Kings 15:29

title: I Kings 14:17
text: Tirzah; where Jeroboam lived, supposed to have been near Sechem.

title: I Kings 14:21
text: To put his name there; as the place where he would be publicly inquired of and worshipped.

title: I Kings 14:22
text: The course of human nature left to itself is downward from bad to worse, and the most highly exalted by privileges and blessings, when not restrained by divine grace, will become the most wretched and debased by their crimes.

title: I Kings 15:2
text: Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom; in  II Chronicles 13:2 , the mother of Abijam (Abijah) is said to be Michaiah, the daughter of Uriel.  This may perhaps be explained on the supposition that Michaiah is another name borne by Maachah; and that she was the grandaughter of Abishalom, and the daughter of Uriel.

title: I Kings 15:3
text: Perfect; sincerely devoted to God.

title: I Kings 15:4
text: A lamp; continue to him the kingdom.

title: I Kings 15:5
text: Turned not aside from any thing; not in such a wicked and notorious manner in any thing else; and for that he heartily condemned himself, and most sincerely repented.   Psalms 51:1-19

title: I Kings 15:8
text: Sometimes very pious parents are followed by very wicked children, and very wicked parents by very pious children.

title: I Kings 15:10
text: His mother's name; that is, as we must necessarily understand, his grandmother's name,  I Kings 15:2 .

title: I Kings 15:13
text:
Made an idol in a grove; rather, an idol to Asherah, that is, Ashtoreth. 
 
  Kidron; a torrent-bed on the east side of Jerusalem, between the city and the mount of Olives; the same as Cedron,  John 18:1 . 
 
No affection or regard for earthly relatives or friends, however exalted, should lead us to encourage or connive at their sins, or hinder us from using all proper means to prevent their injurious influence.

title: I Kings 15:14
text: The high places were not removed; of both Asa and Jehoshaphat his son it is said that they took away the high places,  II Chronicles 14:3 II Chronicles 17:6  and yet it is said of both, that during their reign the high places were not taken away.  See, also  I Kings 22:43 II Chronicles 15:17 II Chronicles 20:33 .  Some have supposed that in one case the reference is to high places where idols were worshipped, and in the other to high places for the worship of Jehovah.  But perhaps the more probable meaning is, that while these two kings did what lay in their power to remove the high places, they could not wholly extirpate them.

title: I Kings 15:17
text: Built Ramah; commenced the work of fortifying it.  Ramah was in the tribe of Benjamin, a short distance north of Jerusalem.  Baasha's object in doing this was to command the road to and from Jerusalem on the north.

title: I Kings 15:18
text:
Damascus; the capital of Syria. 
 
When men, instead of trusting in God and doing his will, apply to the wicked for help and devote to them what should be devoted to him, though they may sometimes gain temporary relief, yet it will in the end be very likely to increase their trouble.

title: I Kings 15:20
text: Ijon--Dan--Abel-beth-maachah--Chinneroth; places in the north part of Israel, next to Syria.

title: I Kings 15:23
text: However long any may live, and however much in the providence and by the grace of God they may be favored, they are constantly liable to disease and death.  Nothing should hinder them from being habitually ready to close life, and enter upon the retributions of eternity.  Ecclesiastes 8:6-13 Ecclesiastes 12:1

title: I Kings 15:27
text: Gibbethon; in the tribe of Dan, but occupied by the Philistines.

title: I Kings 15:29
text:
The saying of the Lord;  I Kings 14:1 
 
One set of wicked men, in the prosecution of their wicked objects, may without intending it bring on other wicked men punishments which God has denounced.   Isaiah 44:28 Isaiah 45:1-5 Daniel 5:30-31

title: I Kings 16:2
text: By whatever means and in whatever way any are exalted to power, authority, or influence, there is an important sense in which their elevation is of the Lord; and all their increase of power increases their obligations to honor him and do good, and if they do not, increases their guilt and their exposure to speedy and awful ruin.

title: I Kings 16:3
text: Imitation of predecessors in wickedness prepares the way for similarity in punishment.

title: I Kings 16:7
text:
Killed him; not Jeroboam himself, but his posterity.  I Kings 15:27-29   Though God had foretold,  I Kings 14:14 , that Baasha would do this, and it was before hand certain that he would, yet he was just as wicked and guilty in doing it as if it had not been foretold, or had not been certain. 
 
Wicked men may by their wickedness fulfil the declarations of God and be executioners of his wrath on his enemies, without lessening their guilt or their exposure to his just indignation.

title: I Kings 16:9
text: Those who use as a beverage intoxicating liquor, are ont only in danger of forming an intemperate appetite, but of becoming intoxicated, and while in that state being summoned to the bar of God.

title: I Kings 16:13
text:
Vanities; here used, as often elsewhere, of the false gods which the people substituted for Jehovah the only living and true God.  The idols themselves and the confidence which the people reposed in them were alike vain and profitless.  "The stock is a doctrine of vanities."  Jeremiah 10:8  
 
Those who not only sin themselves, but who, by fear, favor, or any temptation, induce others to sin, become peculiarly offensive to God and obnoxious to his wrath.

title: I Kings 16:18
text: A man's pride and cowardice may be so great as to lead him to kill himself; or in a duel, or some other equally foolish and wicked way, expose himself to be killed by others.

title: I Kings 16:22
text: For the wickedness of a people many are the rulers thereof.  When revolution quickly succeeds revolution, and rulers in rapid succession, by violence and murder, succeed rulers, without any fixed, stable, just, and efficient government, God has a controversy with the people, and is through their revolutions and rulers punishing them for their sins.  And without repentance and reformation there will be no permanent relief from their troubles.

title: I Kings 16:24
text:
The hill Samaria; a beautiful hill lying a few miles north-west of Shechem, and compassed all round by a deep broad valley.  It was very suitable for the capital of the Israelitish kingdom, being a strong as well as a central position. 
 
  Called the name--Samaria; in the Hebrew, Shomeron, from Shemer.

title: I Kings 16:30
text: The children of the wicked, when raised to power, and left to act out their wickedness, often do worse than their fathers; choosing the openly vicious for their companions, they become abandoned in wickedness, and plunge into remediless destruction.

title: I Kings 16:31
text: Baal; the chief idol of the Zidonians.

title: I Kings 16:34
text:
Beth-elite; one who lived in Beth-el, where Jeroboam had put one of his golden calves.   I Kings 12:29  
 
  The word of the Lord; spoken more than four hundred years before.  Joshua 6:26

title: I Kings 17:1
text:
According to my word; as he should foretell and pray for it. 
 
Instead of at once destroying the wicked as they deserve, God often waits long upon them, visits them with judgments and with mercies, and does all that infinite wisdom and goodness can consistently do to lead them to repent, and thus to escape the destruction which continued wickedness and impenitence will bring upon them.

title: I Kings 17:6
text: Neither the fowls of the air nor the beasts of the field ever rebel against the will of their Creator, nor do they refuse to do what he bids them.

title: I Kings 17:9
text:
Zarephath; a city on the Mediterranean, between Tyre and Zidon; in the New Testament, Sarepta.   Luke 4:26  
 
When one means of supply fails those who trust in God, he will provide for them another, and in obeying him they never will want any thing necessary to their highest good.

title: I Kings 17:11
text: God often requires of his people what nothing but strong faith and active benevolence will lead them to do.

title: I Kings 17:12
text: Two; meaning a few.

title: I Kings 17:15
text: Confidence in the promises of God, manifested by acting under a conviction of their truth, will not be disappointed, but will be followed by timely and abundant supplies.

title: I Kings 17:17
text: No exercise of faith in God, love to his friends, or readiness to honor him in doing them good, will secure us from liability to great and sore trials.  It is only through much tribulation that any are prepared to enter the kingdom of God.   Acts 14:22 Romans 5:3 II Corinthians 1:3-11 II Corinthians 7:4-10   I Thessalonians 3:3-13 Hebrews 11:35-40 Hebrews 12:1-13 Revelation of John 7:14-17

title: I Kings 17:18
text:
Slay my son; she supposed her afflictions might have been as a punishment for her sins, and brought upon her by God through the instrumentality of the prophet. 
 
All our sufferings are caused by our sins, and should lead us more and more to loathe and forsake them, trusting in Christ for pardon, and for all which we need to do the will of God, and meet his gracious acceptance.

title: I Kings 17:24
text:
In thy mouth is truth; she knew that what the prophet had declared was true, and would be accomplished. 
 
To those who obey God, he so manifests himself as to convince them that all his declarations will be surely and fully accomplished.

title: I Kings 18:3
text: The fidelity and usefulness of truly religious persons sometimes lead very wicked men to employ them in preference to all others; and good men should ever strive so to act as to show that godliness is profitable unto all things, and that it renders those who possess it conscientiously diligent and faithful in the discharge of all the duties of life.

title: I Kings 18:4
text: Under the government of wicked rulers the Lord's ministers are often persecuted, imprisoned, and dependent on charity for support, while Satan's ministers go at large, and riot in luxury and abundance.

title: I Kings 18:9
text: Even the people of God are sometimes afraid to do what he commands them, lest they should suffer; but if they are truly devoted to him, and desirous of doing their duty, he will make it plain and enable them by his grace to perform it.

title: I Kings 18:10
text: No nation or kingdom; in that vicinity, or connected with Israel.

title: I Kings 18:17
text: Persecutors are apt to represent those who condemn them for their wickedness as disturbers of the public peace and troublers of the people, and to contend that their liberty is inconsistent with the public good, and that they should be banished or put to death.

title: I Kings 18:18
text:
Baalim; images of Baal. 
 
The troubles which come upon rulers and people are a punishment from God on account of their sins.  Not those who condemn these sins, but those who commit them, are the real troublers of the country.

title: I Kings 18:19
text:
Mount Carmel; a mountain near the Mediterranean, and south of the bay of Acre. 
 
  Of the groves; or, of Asherah, the same as Ashtoreth.

title: I Kings 18:21
text:
Halt ye; act as if doubtful whether Jehovah or Baal were the true God. 
 
As Jehovah has in various ways shown conclusively that he is the only living and true God, reason, interest, and duty require that all to whom he is revealed should, without hesitation or reserve, love, worship, and obey him.

title: I Kings 18:22
text:
I only; he was the only prophet of Jehovah who was present, or appeared before the people. 
 
Which is the right way is not to be determined by the numbers, wealth, and power of those who follow it.  God's friends may be few, poor, feeble, and despised, while Satan's may be many, rich, powerful, and respected.  It is better, in such cases, to be of the few than of the many.   Psalms 138:6 Proverbs 3:34 Proverbs 16:19 Proverbs 28:6

title: I Kings 18:24
text: Let him be God; let him be acknowledged and adored as God.

title: I Kings 18:26
text: Leaped; as was the custom with idolaters.

title: I Kings 18:27
text:
He is a god; spoken in irony, intimating the absurdity of idol-worship. 
 
The worship of images, and of all false, imaginary deities, is mean, base, and foolish.

title: I Kings 18:28
text: The worship of false gods is cruel to the worshippers, and often leads to the infliciton of great bodily penances and sufferings.  Such sufferings please the tormentors, but do the tormented no good; and are an abomination to Jehovah, whose ways are ways of pleasantness, and whose paths are paths of peace.

title: I Kings 18:29
text: The time of the offering; about three o'clock in the afternoon, or between that and sunset.

title: I Kings 18:32
text: Two measures; a measure was about ten quarts.

title: I Kings 18:33
text: True religion has nothing to fear from experiment, and from candid, thorough, and searching investigation.  It loves the light, and seeks to diffuse it among all classes of people, so that they may be able to judge of it themselves, and act intelligently with regard to it.

title: I Kings 18:37
text:
Turned their heart; to worship Jehovah as the true God. 
 
Prayer, simple, earnest, and sincere, not in a foreign tongue which is not understood, but in that which the hearers themselves speak, is a powerful means of grace, and one by which God often convinces men of the truth and leads them to embrace it.

title: I Kings 18:40
text:
The brook Kishon; which emptied into the bay of Acre near the foot of mount Carmel. 
 
  Slew them; according to the command of God.   Deuteronomy 13:5 Deuteronomy 18:20   Jeremiah 48:10

title: I Kings 18:42
text: Went up; from the brook Kishon to a place where refreshments were provided for him.

title: I Kings 18:43
text: Not only sincerity and earnestness, but perseverance in supplication and obedience to God, are essential to the highest success.  However small the number or trying the condition of the friends of Jehovah, let them trust in him, seek of him what they need, and follow his directions, and they shall in due time gloriously triumph over all their foes.

title: I Kings 18:44
text: Get thee down; from the mountain where he was, and return to his palace at Jezreel.

title: I Kings 18:46
text:
The hand of the Lord was on Elijah; imparting to him supernatural strength. 
 
  Girded up his loins; put a girdle or belt around his outer garments, as was the custom when about to travel. 
 
  Ran before Ahab; after the manner of royal attendants, that he might thus publicly honor him as the king of Israel.

title: I Kings 19:2
text:
So let the gods do to me; let them kill me, if I do not kill thee. 
 
No miracles or means of grace will of themselves lead persecutors and haters of God to cease from their efforts to overcome and destroy his people.

title: I Kings 19:3
text: However bold, courageous, and successful the people of God may have been under his influence, unless that is of God may have been under his influence, unless that is their duty, and in despair even wish to die.

title: I Kings 19:4
text: Into the wilderness; which lay south of Canaan, and in which Israel had wandered forty years.

title: I Kings 19:5
text: God knoweth the frame of his people and remembereth that they are dust. He compassionates their infirmities and sympathizes in their sorrows, and when they duly feel their weakness and wants, appears for their relief.

title: I Kings 19:8
text:
Forty days and forty nights; being miraculously supported. 
 
  Horeb; where God appeared to Israel and gave them the law.  Deuteronomy 1:6

title: I Kings 19:9
text: Men are made not merely to be acted upon but to act, and should never voluntarily go where they have nothing to do, or can do nothing.

title: I Kings 19:10
text:
Jealous for the Lord; desirous of honoring him by leading the people to obey him. 
 
  I only; no other prophet openly appeared to stem the torrent of iniquity. 
 
Men are never more likely to boast of their past labors, than when they are neglecting their present duty; nor ever more likely to complain, find fault with others, and sink into despair.

title: I Kings 19:11
text:
vv 11-12. 
 
  The Lord was not in the wind--earthquake--fire; indicating that he would not reform Israel by terrific outward displays of his power, but by the quiet persevering labors of his servants, under the invisible and silent influences of his Spirit.

title: I Kings 19:12
text: It is not always that which is most visible and tangible, or which makes the most noise, that is most efficacious in doing good.

title: I Kings 19:15
text: If the people of God, when fearful, discouraged, and desponding, would get out of trouble, they must go to work; what their hands find to do, they must do for the purpose of honoring God and doing good, committing themselves and all their interests to his guidance and disposal.

title: I Kings 19:16
text: Abel-meholah; a town in the plain of Jordan, between Beth-shean and Shechem.

title: I Kings 19:17
text: Hazael--Jehu--and--Elisha; they would all be instrumental in the punishment of idolatrous Israel.

title: I Kings 19:18
text:
Seven thousand; who were still worshippers of Jehovah. 
 
Some good men are at times tempted to think that there are none who labor in the right way to sustain the cause of God but themselves, and that when they are gone it must sink.  But he will show that it is not as dependent on them as they thought it was.

title: I Kings 19:19
text: Cast his mantle upon him; indicating that he should follow him.

title: I Kings 19:20
text:
Go back again; probably said to try the firmness of his purpose. 
 
God can at any time so touch the hearts of men that they will voluntarily and cheerfully leave all for him and his cause.  But in doing this, he will not lessen their natural affection, or lead them to neglect any of the proper kindnesses and courtesies of life.  I Peter 3:8

title: I Kings 19:21
text:
Took a yoke of oxen; to provide for himself and friends a feast before he left them. 
 
  Ministered unto him; waited on and assisted him.

title: I Kings 20:1
text: Kings; rulers of cities and the adjoining districts of country.

title: I Kings 20:4
text:
I am thine; meaning, that he would be tributary to the king of Syria. 
 
Wickedness persevered in not only prevents men from receiving any saving benefit from divine judgments and mercies, but renders them mean, cowardly, base, and contemptible.

title: I Kings 20:6
text: Success in wickedness often increases men's pride, arrogance, haughtiness, and rapacity, emboldens them in sin, and thus ripens them for ruin.

title: I Kings 20:10
text:
If the dust of Samaria shall suffice; meaning, that he would come with such a multitude of people that the sand of Samaria would not give to each a handful. 
 
For men to boast of what they have done, is vain and foolish; to boast of what they will do, presumptuous and wicked.  It is glorying in the creature, and rebelling against the Creator.

title: I Kings 20:11
text:
Girdeth on his harness; puts on his armor for battle, or begins a war. 
 
  Putteth it off; victoriously closes it.

title: I Kings 20:13
text: The object of God in suffering wicked rulers to assemble great multitudes for war and go forth to battle, is very different from their object in doing it.  The design to promote their own glory, and he designs to show his perfections and advance his cause.

title: I Kings 20:14
text:
The young men; those who waited upon the princes; their servants. 
 
  The princes of the provinces; these seem to have been the rulers who governed in the different districts of the kingdom.

title: I Kings 20:16
text: Under the influence of intoxicating liquor, men are self-confident and reckless, and they often speak and act as if all things were under their control, and are urged on by Satan and their own lusts from one crime to another till they perish.

title: I Kings 20:22
text: God knows and can reveal what men will so before they think of doing it, and yet leave them as free and accountable as if he had not revealed what they would do.

title: I Kings 20:23
text: Gods of the hills; therefore they were stronger than we; the idea was, that different gods ruled over different places, and that they must fight the Israelites in places where their gods did not govern.

title: I Kings 20:26
text: Aphek; in the tribe of Issachar.  It seems to have been in the valley of Jezreel.

title: I Kings 20:28
text: God hears all that wicked men say, sees all that they do or intend to do, and can adapt his providence to meet their cases, and make them the occasion of advancing his glory and the welfare of his people.  None therefore who put their trust in him, and follow his directions, need to fear.   Psalms 2:2-4

title: I Kings 20:31
text: Go out to the king of Israel; as prisoners of war, liable, according to the then prevalent custom, to be put to death.

title: I Kings 20:32
text:
On their heads; about their necks. 
 
  My brother; as king.

title: I Kings 20:35
text:
In the word of the Lord; by his command. 
 
No feelings or considerations should ever hinder men from obeying God, and when they save from death those whom God requires to be slain, they incur his displeasure, and expose themselves to be destroyed.

title: I Kings 20:40
text: Thyself hast decided; that according to his own statement, which was designed to represent the case of Ahab, he had forfeited his life. Ahab decided that he should be put to death, and thus virtually condemned himself for letting Ben-hadad go when he had him in his power.

title: I Kings 20:42
text:
Appointed to utter destruction; required that he should be destroyed. 
 
  Thy life--for his life; Ahab would himself be destroyed. 1Ki 22.31-37

title: I Kings 21:1
text: The palace of Ahab king of Samaria; see note to  I Kings 21:18 .

title: I Kings 21:4
text: Covetousness is idolatry; and if the heart be under its power, and cannot obtain its wishes, it may at any time be rendered miserable. Even little things that cannot be obtained, but are inordinately desired, may make a man wretched.

title: I Kings 21:7
text: Despotic power in the hand of man or woman under the control of wickedness is a terrible curse, and liable at any time to be employed in the commission of the most outrageous and abominable injustice and cruelty.

title: I Kings 21:8
text:
Wrote letters; from Samaria. 
 
  Sealed them with his seal; this gave them the king's authority, and required all to obey on pain of his displeasure.

title: I Kings 21:9
text:
Proclaim a fast; to make an impression that Naboth had committed some great wickedness, which required him to be put to death. 
 
No plans are so wicked that men who are disposed may not find some wicked enough to aid in executing them; and no forms of injustice and cruelty are more execrable, and none will receive a deeper condemnation, than those which are perpetrated under the cover of religion and law.

title: I Kings 21:10
text:
Sons of Belial; wicked, abandoned men. 
 
  Stone him; stoning was the punishment which God commanded for blasphemy, the crime of which Naboth was falsely accused,  Leviticus 24:15-16 .

title: I Kings 21:16
text:
To go down; from Samaria to Jezreel. 
 
Men who have the power and the right to prevent crime, and yet suffer it for the sake of sharing its gains, are partakers in the guilt of those who commit it, and will share in their plagues.

title: I Kings 21:18
text: Which is in Samaria; whose customary residence is in Samaria. Samaria was the capital of Ahab's kingdom, and his proper residence,  I Kings 22:37-39 ; but he had also a palace at Jezreel, and sometimes resided there.   I Kings 21:1 II Chronicles 22:6

title: I Kings 21:20
text:
Sold thyself; abandoned himself to wickedness. 
 
Sinners are apt to be enemies to those who, by the command of God, denounce his wrath against them, and to feel as if such persons were their enemies.  But this is a great mistake.  They hate their sins, and lament the ruin these occasion.   Matthew 23:37

title: I Kings 21:21
text: Shut up and left; a proverbial expression originally denoting bond and free, but put here to represent all classes of persons.

title: I Kings 21:23
text: Ringleaders in transgression will be distinguished in their punishment; and though external humiliation may secure temporal favors, nothing short of real penitence and hearty forsaking of sin will save from its endless consequences.

title: I Kings 22:3
text: Ramoth; a city of Gad, east of Jordan.

title: I Kings 22:4
text:
I am as thou art; I will act in concert with thee in all things. Jehoshaphat had joined affinity with the king of Israel by taking for a wife to his son Jehoram, Athaliah the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel.  II Kings 8:18 II Chronicles 18:1   By this wrong step he brought upon himself, his family, and his kingdom very dreadful calamities.  In consequence of the alliance between him and Ahab, he felt obliged to offer his services on the present occasion, though evidently with much misgiving. 
 
Intimate connections with the wicked, and readiness to form coalitions with them, are exceedingly dangerous, and often lead to the most disastrous results.

title: I Kings 22:6
text:
Prophets; these were false prophets, probably connected with the worship of the golden calves, who had not been present at mount Carmel when Elijah slew the prophets of Baal and Ashtoreth. 
 
False teachers are numerous, and they endeavor to ingratiate themselves with those who employ them by consulting their wishes, pandering to their pleasures, and aiding in accomplishing their favorite designs.

title: I Kings 22:13
text: Many seem to think it unwise for ministers to confine themselves to truth and duty; and that it would be better to go with the multitude, and do what is popular, especially with the rich and powerful.

title: I Kings 22:15
text: Go, and prosper; this was spoken ironically, and in a manner that showed the king that Micaiah did not expect him to prosper.

title: I Kings 22:17
text: I saw; a representation of what would take place at the battle, upon Ahab's death.   I Kings 22:36

title: I Kings 22:18
text: True ministers will proclaim only the truth and will of God.  Of course they can promise no good to those who continue in sin, and on this account they are often hated.

title: I Kings 22:19
text: I saw; a representation of what was then going on for the deception and ruin of Ahab.

title: I Kings 22:23
text:
The Lord hath put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these thy prophets; an instance of the manner in which things that take place, in the providence and under the government of God, are ascribed to him; he suffered those false prophets to tell lies, and by their lies, as a punishment of Ahab for his sins, to deceive him to his destruction. 
 
As a punishment for their sins, God sometimes suffers wicked men to be deluded by false teachers and evil spirits, and under that delusion to be destroyed.   II Peter 2:1-3 II Peter 2:18-22

title: I Kings 22:25
text: Thou shalt see; know who speaks the truth, you or I.

title: I Kings 22:27
text: Bread of affliction; coarse and scanty fare.

title: I Kings 22:28
text: They who disbelieve the word of God, will learn the truth of his declarations by thier fulfilment.

title: I Kings 22:30
text:
Disguise myself; so array himself as not to be known to be king. 
 
No efforts of the wicked to escape the evils which God intends to bring upon them will be successful.

title: I Kings 22:34
text:
At a venture; shooting into the midst of the Israelites, without taking aim at any one. 
 
Every arrow which flies is under the direction and control of God, and --though often without the intention of men--always accomplishes his designs.

title: I Kings 22:38
text:
According unto the word of the Lord;  I Kings 21:19 II Kings 9:25-25:30 
 
Animals, in following the instincts and appetites which God has given them, may be instruments of his wrath against the wicked, and the means of fulfilling his declarations concerning them.

title: I Kings 22:39
text: The ivory house; a house adorned with ivory, or precious ornaments made of elephants' tusks.

title: I Kings 22:43
text: The ways of Asa; 1Ki 15.11-15.

title: I Kings 22:44
text: Made peace; by making affinity with him.  See note to 1Ki 22.4.

title: I Kings 22:48
text: Ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir; the ships were made at Ezion-geber on the eastern arm of the Red sea, which was the port for going to Ophir.  Some suppose they are called "ships of Tarshish" merely to indicate ships of a certain form or size, such as were used in voyages to Tarshish.  See notes to  I Kings 10:22 II Chronicles 20:36 .

title: II Kings 1:1
text: Moab rebelled; they had before, from the days of David, been tributary to the Israelites.   II Kings 3:4-5

title: II Kings 1:2
text:
Lattice; or balustrade; a light fence, or net-work. 
 
  Baal-zebub; and idol god. 
 
  Ekron; a city of the Philistines. 
 
The constant liability of men to sickness and death should lead all so to live, as to be at all times prepared for these events.  They will then have no occasion for anxiety, and no inclination to turn away from Jehovah in applying for help.

title: II Kings 1:3
text: Applying to false gods, is acting as if Jehovah were not the only living and true God; and is highly provoking to Him, who will not give his glory to another, nor his praise to graven images.

title: II Kings 1:8
text: A hairy man; in his person; probably also dressed in a garment made of hair.   Matthew 3:4

title: II Kings 1:9
text: It is sometimes necessary for good men, in order to honor God, to disobey the highest earthly authority; and even to be instrumental in the destruction of those who rebel against him.

title: II Kings 1:10
text: Let fire come down; this was designed to show that Jehovah was the only living and true God, and able to protect all who put their trust in him.

title: II Kings 1:13
text: The only way for wicked men finally to escape the judgments of God, is by humble submission to him, hearty acknowledgment of his authority, and fervent supplication for his mercy.

title: II Kings 1:15
text: When God commands, his people may visit in safety their greatest persecutors, and proclaim without fear his truth and will concerning them.

title: II Kings 2:1
text: At whatever time or in whatever way men are removed from this world, it is God who removes them and although his reasons may not be known by creatures, yet they are always the wisest and the best, and we should bow submissively and cheerfully to his holy will.

title: II Kings 2:2
text: It is a great privilege to be with wise and holy men who realize that they are near the close of life, and who are expecting soon to exchange earth for heaven.

title: II Kings 2:3
text: Sons of the prophets; young men instructed, it is supposed, by the prophets in seminaries for that purpose.

title: II Kings 2:8
text: No obstructions will meet a soul that is ripe for heaven, which true faith will not overcome.  It can, when called to do so, go through Jordan on dry ground, and rise to God in a chariot of fire.

title: II Kings 2:9
text:
A double portion; he wished a double portion of the influences of the Holy Spirit; not necessarily double the amount that had rested on Elijah, but rather double the amount granted to the prophets in general; that is, a very plenteous endowment, such as should qualify him to stand at the head of the school of the prophets. 
 
It is right to desire a double portion of the spirit which prepares good men for usefulness and for glory; and attending upon their instructions, uniting with them in devotion, and ministering to their wants, are fruitful means of obtaining such a blessing.

title: II Kings 2:12
text: The chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof; as much as to say, the chariot of fire and horses of fire have taken from Israel him who was their true chariot and horsemen; a better protection than any earthly chariots and horsemen can be.  Compare the application of the words to the dying Elisha.   II Kings 13:14

title: II Kings 2:14
text:
Where is the Lord God of Elijah? let him manifest his presence and power, as he had been wont to do unto Elijah. 
 
  They parted; by this God showed that he was with Elisha, as he had been wont to do unto Elisha, as he had been with Elijah, and that his request,  II Kings 2:9 , was granted. 
 
Though the wisest and best of men are removed from earth, God can make their successors wiser and better than they; so that the light, not only of his ministers and individual Christians, but of his church, shall be as the light of the morning, growing brighter and brighter to the perfect day.

title: II Kings 2:15
text: Bowed themselves; acknowledging him as their teacher in the place of Elijah.

title: II Kings 2:16
text: The wisdom of age and experience cannot by any methods of instruction be imparted to the young.  There is much, very much, which they need to know, that nothing but experience will effectually teach them.  Job 15:8-10 Job 32:7 s

title: II Kings 2:17
text: Was ashamed; any longer to refuse.

title: II Kings 2:19
text:
Naught; bad. 
 
There are many places and conditions which are externally very pleasant, and yet are internally barren and bitter.

title: II Kings 2:21
text: Divine kindness, power, and grace, can make a wilderness become like Eden, and a desert like the garden of God.

title: II Kings 2:23
text:
Little children; young persons. 
 
  Go up, thou bald head; an expression of the contempt of these young idolaters for the presence and office of the aged prophet. 
 
The wickedness of parents is often followed and sometimes exceeded by that of their children, and the curse of God on the children becomes the means of punishing the parents, till those who have been mutual and successful tempters become mutual and dreadful tormentors.

title: II Kings 2:24
text: Cursed them in the name of the Lord; this was intended to show God as the protector of his people and the punisher of idolatry.

title: II Kings 3:3
text:
Cleaved unto the sins of Jeroboam; though he put away the image of Baal, he still continued to worship the golden calves.  I Kings 12:28-29  
 
Men may refuse to commit, or may break off some sins, and yet continue to practise others; but without a heart to hate and forsake all known sins, they must perish.

title: II Kings 3:7
text: When men engage in projects without acknowledging God or seeking his direction, especially when they join the wicked in the prosecution of their plans, they may expect to be brought into trouble, and will have special reason for gratitude if they escape destruction.

title: II Kings 3:8
text: The wilderness of Edom; south of the Dead sea.

title: II Kings 3:11
text:
Poured water; in washing one's hands, it was then customary for an attendant to do this. 
 
In times of danger it is always safest to go to God, and ask counsel of him.

title: II Kings 3:14
text:
Not look toward thee; not deign to notice him, or regard his request, because of his idolarty. 
 
From regard to his people, the Lord often bestows great blessings not only on them, but on others with whom they are connected; and the wicked may thus receive favors, which they would otherwise never obtain.

title: II Kings 3:15
text: A minstrel; one who could play on a musical instrument in praising God; and thus aid in preparing the mind of the prophet to be directed by him.   I Samuel 10:5

title: II Kings 3:16
text: God requires men in their troubles, not only to seek his help, but to show by their actions that they believe him and are willing to follow his directions; and unless they do this, they cannot reasonably expect that he will grant them relief.

title: II Kings 3:18
text: A light thing; only a small part of what God will do.

title: II Kings 3:23
text: Things often appear to the wicked to be very different from what they really are; and as they do not feel their need of divine guidance, and do not seek it, they have no security against fatal deception.

title: II Kings 3:25
text:
Kir-haraseth; a stringly fortified place in the land of Moab; called also Kir-haresh.   Isaiah 16:7 Isaiah 16:11  
 
  The stones thereof; that is, the stones of which the wall was built.

title: II Kings 3:26
text: To break through; through the forces of the king of Edom, and so perhaps escape.

title: II Kings 3:27
text:
Offered him; as a sacrifice to his idols, hoping in that way to obtain their help. 
 
The devices of men to atone for their sins and obtain help from idols, are sanguinary and cruel.  The leave the heart wedded to its lusts, and are utterly vain.

title: II Kings 4:1
text: The power to take and hold men as bondmen in payment for debt, is a source of great distress, from which all proper means should be used to afford relief.

title: II Kings 4:7
text: Poverty does not release debtors from obligation to pay their creditors.  Whenever God gives them the means to pay their debts, they should do it with promptness and alacrity.

title: II Kings 4:8
text:
Shunem; a city in the tribe of Issachar. 
 
  A great woman; wealthy and influential.

title: II Kings 4:9
text: A disposition to relieve and assist the pious is pecularily pleasing to God, and a means of securing the special manifestations of his presence and favor.

title: II Kings 4:13
text: The truly pious are grateful for the favors they receive, and are disposed to make the best return in their power.

title: II Kings 4:18
text: Some of the highest joys and the deepest sorrows come to parents through the medium of their children.  But both are from God, and in both he should be acknowledged as doing all things well.

title: II Kings 4:26
text: True piety inspires a deep interest in the happiness of others, especially of benefactors; and leads us to delight in communicating enjoyment, as we have opportunity, to all, especially to the people of God.

title: II Kings 4:27
text: The Lord hath hid it from me, and hath not told me; the prophets did not know more than other men, except as the Lord taught them.

title: II Kings 4:38
text:
A dearth; scarcity of food. 
 
  Seethe; boil.

title: II Kings 4:39
text:
Knew--not; that they were hurtful. 
 
Though every creature of God is good for the purpose for which he made it, yet there are many things which he did not make for food or drink; and men cannot so use them without producing sickness and death, and, if they know these to be their effects, sinning against God.

title: II Kings 4:40
text: Death; that which was hurtful and might cause death.

title: II Kings 4:41
text: No harm; nothing that would injure them.

title: II Kings 4:42
text:
Baal-shalisha; in the tribe of Ephraim. 
 
Kindness to the good because they are good blesses not only those who bestow and those who receive it, but often multitudes of others; and while it breathes goodwill to men, it brings glory in the highest to God.

title: II Kings 4:43
text: Servitor; servant.

title: II Kings 5:1
text: No honors or successes can secure men from trouble; and for the blessings they obtain by their own efforts, or those of others, they are indebted to God.

title: II Kings 5:3
text:
The prophet; Elisha. 
 
Servants may be the means of great blessings to their masters; and the good influence even of a pious child may be felt through a nation, and to distant countries and times.

title: II Kings 5:4
text: His lord; Ben-hadad the king of Syria.

title: II Kings 5:5
text:
He; Naaman. 
 
  Pieces; that is, shekels.  A talent of silver contained three thousand shekels.  A shekel of silver has been estimated at from fifty to sixty cents.  A shekel of gold was many times greater.  See note to  I Kings 10:14 .

title: II Kings 5:6
text:
That thou mayest recover him; he expected the cure to be performed by Elisha, but supposed that the prophets of Israel, like those of the heathen nations, were under the direction of their monarch, and would act at his bidding. 
 
Despotic rulers often feel and act as if ministers of God in the discharge of their duties were to be subject to their control.

title: II Kings 5:10
text: Ministers who understand and do their duty, will not be elated nor overawed by the presence of the rich and great; but will make known to them with plainness and fidelity the will of God, whether they will hear or forbear.

title: II Kings 5:13
text: Servants are sometimes wiser and better than their masters, and give them advice which it would be well for them to follow.

title: II Kings 5:14
text: Simply following the diretions of God, however plain and easy, is more efficacious than the most skilful, laborious, and costly schemes of men.  These tend to feed and strengthen human pride; the other to exalt and glorify God.

title: II Kings 5:15
text: A blessing; a gift or present.

title: II Kings 5:16
text: Disinterested kindness, and doing good without expecting or wishing any earthly reward, is adapted to convey to men a correct impression of true religion.

title: II Kings 5:17
text: Two mules' burden of earth; with this it is supposed he intended to build an altar or mound, on which to offer sacrifices to Jehovah, considering the earth of Israel more sacred than that of his own country.

title: II Kings 5:18
text:
Rimmon; an idol god. 
 
  When I bow down myself; it has been supposed that he meant not as himself worshipping the idol, but only in attending on, and performing a civil duty to the king.

title: II Kings 5:20
text: The unprincipled, selfish, and covetous think it wise to take any course in which, without danger, they can get money.

title: II Kings 5:22
text: My master hath sent me; this was false.

title: II Kings 5:25
text:
Went no whither; another falsehood. 
 
Men who will sacrifice conscience for money, will tell lies in order to keep it; but the getting or keeping of money by lying, instead of being in the end a source of profit, will occasion most dreadful loss.

title: II Kings 5:26
text: Went not my heart; did I not perceive.

title: II Kings 5:27
text: For ever; as long as they should live.

title: II Kings 6:1
text:
The place; the building or apartment they occupied. 
 
  Strait; narrow, small.

title: II Kings 6:5
text: Borrowed articles should be used with care, and in due time returned, uninjured, to the owner.

title: II Kings 6:13
text: Dothan; a place a few miles north of Samaria,  Genesis 37:17 .

title: II Kings 6:14
text: Wicked men often hope to prevail against those who have God for their protector, but all such hopes are vain.

title: II Kings 6:16
text: They that be with us; God, and all the heavenly hosts.

title: II Kings 6:17
text: All who have right views will see that the servants of God, however great their apparent danger, are perfectly safe under his care.

title: II Kings 6:18
text: This people; the hosts of the king of Syria.

title: II Kings 6:22
text:
Wouldest thou smite those; he would not; and much less should he smite those who had been miraculously delivered into his power. 
 
Kindness towards enemies is good policy, as well as a Christian duty; however it may be received, will be the means of good to those who exercise it.

title: II Kings 6:25
text:
Pieces; shekels. 
 
  A cab; between one and two quarts. 
 
  Dove's dung; supposed by many to be a mean kind of pulse or pea, called by that name. 
 
None but God can fully understand the evils of war, or the guilt of those who are instrumental in needlessly inflicting them upon their fellow men.

title: II Kings 6:31
text:
If the head of Elisha--shall stand on him; he considered Elisha as the cause of the famine, or as guilty in not removing it.  Many suppose that the prophet had promised him deliverance from the Syrians, and that he was vexed at the delay, and ready to destroy Elisha as a deceiver.  See note to  II Kings 6:33 . 
 
Those who foretell the calamity of the wicked, are often treated as it they were the cause of it, and as if their removal would prevent the coming or continuance of threatened evils; but all expectations of relief in that way will be disappointed.

title: II Kings 6:33
text: What should I wait for the Lord; the exclamation of the king, who immediately followed his messenger to the door of Elisha; implying that God was his enemy, that the promised deliverance was no longer to be hoped for, and that confidence in Jehovah was a vain thing.

title: II Kings 7:1
text:
A measure; in the Hebrew, a seah, which contained about one-third of a bushel.  Considering the present severity of the famine,  II Kings 6:25 , this seemed to the unbelieving lord an incredible change. 
 
However great the calamities which any people suffer, the Lord can remove them; and interest as well as duty require all to wait upon him in the way of his appointment, till they obtain relief.

title: II Kings 7:2
text:
Would make windows in heaven; to rain down provisions.  This was an expression of unbelief, for which Elisha immediately announced that he should be excluded from a share in the coming plenty. 
 
Disbelief of the promises of God cuts men off from the blessings of their fulfilment.

title: II Kings 7:4
text: Though deliverance comes from God, it is ordinarily granted through the instrumentality of human efforts; and to obtain it, men must use the means which God has appointed for that purpose.

title: II Kings 7:6
text: Hear a noise; like that of chariots, horses, and a great army.

title: II Kings 7:9
text: When men are blessed with abundance, true wisdom, as well as real gratitude, and even self-interest, require that they should desire others to enjoy it with them.

title: II Kings 7:13
text: Behold, they are; or, they will be; the horses and horsemen will be exposed to no worse calamity in exploring the Syrian camp than that which awaits the beseiged in the city.  They can but die, and death awaits them if they sit still.

title: II Kings 7:16
text: However great the improbability, or to human appearance the impossibility, the word of the Lord will in due time be perfectly accomplished.

title: II Kings 7:17
text: The people trode upon him; in their haste to get food.

title: II Kings 7:18
text: The fulfilment of divine declarations is to some the means of salvation, and to others of destruction.

title: II Kings 8:1
text: When the Lord is about to chastise a people for their sins, he remembers his children and supplies their wants or sanctifies their privations to their highest good.

title: II Kings 8:2
text: The land of the Philistines; on the Mediterranean, south-west of Canaan.

title: II Kings 8:6
text: The goodness of God is often manifested towards his people, by inclining those in authority to do them justice and show them favor.

title: II Kings 8:7
text: Damascus; the capital of Syria.

title: II Kings 8:8
text:
Hazael; an officer of the king of Syria. 
 
Men who in health pay no regard to God or his people, in sickness or distress often apply to them for help.

title: II Kings 8:10
text:
Thou mayest--recover; his disease was not in itself mortal, and would not cause his death. 
 
  He shall surely die; because, as the event showed, Hazael would kill him.  Such is the common, and perhaps the preferable interpretation of this passage.  But the original Hebrew text may be read, Go, say unto him, Thou shalt surely not recover; for the Lord hath showed me that he shall surely die.  According to this reading, Hazael directly falsified the prophet's words.  According to the common interpretation, he suppressed the second part of them. 
 
Of many blessings which God would otherwise bestow, men are often deprived by the wickedness of their fellow men.

title: II Kings 8:11
text:
He settled his countenance; on Hazeal. 
 
  Until he was ashamed; till Hazael was put out of countenance. 
 
  Wept; foreseeing the cruelties Hazael would commit.

title: II Kings 8:13
text:
But what, is thy serant a dog;probably meaning, What is thy servant, who is but a dog?  that is, a man in a very humble position. 
 
  This great thing; a work which could be performed only by one invested with royal power. 
 
A change of circumstances often shows that men are much more wicked than they imagined, and that nothing but the grace of God keeps them from the commission of the most enormous crimes.

title: II Kings 8:14
text:
Thou shouldest surely recover; see note to  II Kings 8:10 . 
 
A slight change in the words of a communication may entirely alter its meaning, and convey to the hearers a false impression.

title: II Kings 8:15
text: He took; Hazael did this.

title: II Kings 8:18
text: A man's character and conduct are greatly influenced by his wife; and no one should marry a woman who will draw him away from the service of God.

title: II Kings 8:21
text: Smote the Edomites which compassed him about; this seems to have been not so much a decisive victory on the part of Jehoram, as an escape from destruction.  Hence it is added in the next verse that the revolt of the Edomites was permanent.

title: II Kings 8:22
text: Libnah; one of the cities of Judah.

title: II Kings 8:27
text: The evil example of parents and those in authority may extend its mischievous influence not only to their children, but also to their distant posterity; and long after they are dead be instrumental in ruining their fellow men.

title: II Kings 8:28
text: Ramoth-gilead; east of Jordan, in the tribe of Gad.

title: II Kings 8:29
text:
Jezreel; west of the Jordan, in the tribe of Gad. 
 
  Ahaziah--went down; from Ramoth-gilead, whither he had gone in alliance with Joram.  Thus, by the providence of God, the king of Judah, being one of Ahab's descendants, was brought to Jezreel, to meet his death there with Joram at the hand of Jehu.

title: II Kings 9:1
text: One of the children of the prophets; a young man who was under the instruction of Elisha and preparing to be a prophet of the Lord.

title: II Kings 9:8
text: God claims and exercises the right of giving authority to such as he chooses; and all who are intrusted with it are laid under peculiar obligations to employ it according to his will.

title: II Kings 9:10
text: The portion of Jezreel; the portion of land that had belonged to Naboth the Jezreelte,  II Kings 9:25 .

title: II Kings 9:11
text:
Ye know the man; that is, to what class of men he belongs. 
 
  His communication; his discourse.  As much as to say, When a prophet comes you expect him to discourse on religious duties.  This was an attempt to evade their question, and they so understood it.

title: II Kings 9:21
text: The declarations of God in his word are fulfilled in his providence; and though the fulfilment may be long delayed, in due time it will be perfectly accomplished.

title: II Kings 9:22
text:
Whoredoms; this word is used in the Old Testament to denote idolatry. 
 
  Her witchcrafts--many; expressive of the various superstitious and deceitful practices which Jezebel used to draw the people into idolatry.

title: II Kings 9:25
text: Laid this burden; denounced this judgment against him and his family.   I Kings 21:19 I Kings 21:29

title: II Kings 9:27
text:
Smite him also in the chariot; Ahazuah at first escaped to Samaria and concealed himself there. But being found, he was brought to Jehu, and by his command slain at the ascent of Gur, by Ibleam.  See  II Chronicles 22:9 . 
 
Those who associate with the wicked are in danger of partaking in their punishment.

title: II Kings 9:30
text: Painted her face, and tired her head; intending by her royal attire and demeanor to overawe Jehu.

title: II Kings 9:31
text: Had Simri peace; as much as to say, You may expect Zimri's fate. See  I Kings 21:19 .

title: II Kings 9:36
text:
In the portion of Jezreel; Elijah had said, By the wall of Jezreel,  I Kings 21:23 , which was literally fulfilled, since Ahab's palace stood by the wall at the entering of the gate,  II Kings 9:31 .  As Naboth's vineyard was "hard by the palace of Ahab," Jezebel's body may have been taken up and cast into it, as Joram's had been.  Or Jehu may have spoken of her as devoured by the dogs in the portion of Jezreel, because he regarded this as simply a part of the royal establishment. 
 
Men may have a conviction of the truth of divine declarations, and even see their fulfilment in the destruction of the wicked, and yet not forsake their sins, or flee from the wrath to come.

title: II Kings 10:6
text: The sins of parents are often the occasion of destruction to their children, and of various evils to all connected with them.

title: II Kings 10:9
text: Said to all the people, Ye be righteous; ye are in no way concerned in my master's death, and are therefore impartial judges, in a condition to understand the meaning of this transaction.  He then proceeds in the next verse to show that it is a pledge of the fulfilment of all Jehovah's threatenings against the house of Ahab.  I Kings 21:19-24

title: II Kings 10:15
text:
Is thy heart right; do you favor my cause? 
 
Wicked men, who externally obey the commands of God, are often proud of their obedience and disposed to proclaim it that they may receive the praises of men.

title: II Kings 10:17
text: The saying of the Lord;  I Kings 21:1

title: II Kings 10:19
text: The Lord often uses one wicked man in punishing others, and afterwards punishes him for his wickedness.

title: II Kings 10:27
text: A draught-house; a house for the reception of filthy ordure.

title: II Kings 10:30
text: External obedience to some of the known commands of God, is often rewarded with external mercies; but that obedience only which springs from the heart, and has respect to the whole will of God, has the promise of eternal life.

title: II Kings 11:1
text:
Destroyed all the seed royal; so that she might reign without a rival. 
 
Love of power tends to destroy natural affection, and leads not only to the violation of the rights of humanity, but to the commission of the most abominable crimes.

title: II Kings 11:4
text:
Jehoiada; the high-priest. 
 
  Fetched the rulers over hundreds; he had previously assembled the Levites and chiefs of the fathers of Israel out of all parts of the kingdom, that he might have a force sufficient to withstand Athaliah.  II Chronicles 23:2  
 
Subjects are not always bound to obey their rulers, but may be called in extraordinary cases to set them aside, and place others in their stead; and if need be, to bring about a revolution for this purpose.

title: II Kings 11:5
text: Enter in on the Sabbath; take your weekly turn in ministering at the temple.

title: II Kings 11:7
text: Go forth on the Sabbath; are released after your week's service at the temple.

title: II Kings 11:8
text:
Ye shall compass the king; to prevent his being slain by the partisans of Athaliah. 
 
  Within the ranges; the lines of guards.

title: II Kings 11:12
text:
The testimony; a copy of the law of Moses. Compare  Deuteronomy 17:18-20  
 
No king can be safe on his throne, or magistrate preserve his authority, without the providential care and gracious aid of God.

title: II Kings 11:14
text: That treatment which, without remorse, persons have unjustly shown towards others who were innocent, they are ready to stigmatize as enormous wickedness when justly shown towards themselves.

title: II Kings 11:20
text: When rulers receive their authority as from God, and use it according to his will, quietness, peace, and prosperity may be expected throughout the land.

title: II Kings 12:2
text:
Wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him; after the death of Jehoiada he was seduced by the princes of Judah into idolatry, as recorded in  II Chronicles 24:17-18 . 
 
When young rulers select pious counsellors and give due heed to their instructions, they may expect to prosper, and be instrumental of great good to the people.

title: II Kings 12:4
text:
Money of the dedicated things; literally, money of the holy things; that is, the various incomes immediately afterwards specified. 
 
  The money of every one that passeth the account; this is generally understood of the half-shekel that every Israelite who was numbered with the congregation was required to pay, and, as many think, annually. 
 
  Money that every man is set at; the redemption money to be paid, according to the estimation of the priest, for persons dedicated to the Lord, as prescribed in  Leviticus 27:34 . 
 
  Money that cometh into any man's heart to bring; that is, freewill offerings not prescribed by the law, but left to every man's choice.

title: II Kings 12:5
text: Every man of his acquaintance; as there was a large body of priests to receive, each would naturally take the above-named sums from those belonging to the circle of his acquaintance.  Besides, as we learn from  II Chronicles 24:5 , the priests and Levites were sent throughout all Israel, to stimulate the people to give, and to receive their gifts; and they would naturally go each to his own town and its vicinity.

title: II Kings 12:8
text:
Consented to receive no more money; they had before received what was offered, but had not appropriated it to the object for which it was given. 
 
Ministers of religion should either avoid receiving money for pious and charitable uses, or exercise the most conscientious fidelity in the appropriation of it.

title: II Kings 12:10
text:
And the high-priest; either personally, or by his officer.  See 2Ch 24.11. 
 
  Told the money; counted it, and stated the amount.

title: II Kings 12:13
text: Were not made--bowls--trumpets; that is, as we learn from  II Chronicles 24:14 , not till the work of repairing the temple was finished, when the rest of the money was devoted to the making of these vessels.

title: II Kings 12:15
text: All money received should be kept with care, and faithfully appropriated to the persons to whom it belongs, and for the objects for which it was given.

title: II Kings 12:17
text: Gath; a city of the Philistines that had been taken and was in possession of the Israelites.

title: II Kings 12:18
text:
Took all the hallowed things; this was after he had suffered a severe defeat, as we learn from  II Chronicles 24:23-24 . 
 
Though an enemy may sometimes be pacified by pecuniary contributions, it is ordinarily unwise to attempt to procure peace in that way; it may lead to increasing demands, till the whole is required to satisfy the rapacious invader.

title: II Kings 13:2
text: The sins of transgressors may be imitated long after they are dead, and be instrumental in the destruction of their distant posterity.

title: II Kings 13:4
text: Cries to the Lord for help may be the means of deliverance from evil and of the reception of temporal good, even where the heart is not right with him, nor the life devoted to his service.

title: II Kings 13:5
text: A savior; Joash the son of Jehoahaz, whose victories over the Syrians are recorded in the latter part of this chapter.

title: II Kings 13:11
text: No temporal favors, without the grace of God, will induce men to break off their sins, or lead them to walk in the ways of the Lord.

title: II Kings 13:14
text:
The chariot--and the horsemen; he who was the defence of Israel. See note to  II Kings 2:12 . 
 
The expected removal of the righteous is often lamented even by the wicked, under the conviction that their pious lives are a great blessing to mankind.

title: II Kings 13:17
text: Aphek; a city of Israel which the Syrians had taken.

title: II Kings 13:18
text:
He smote thrice; this marked the number of times that he would beat the Syrians. 
 
Strong confidence in God is needful in order to the reception, to the fullest extent, of his favors.   Mark 11:24 James 1:5-7

title: II Kings 13:20
text: Moabites; a people south-east of Judea.

title: II Kings 13:21
text:
A band; of the Moabites. 
 
  He revived; showing that God was with Elisha after his death, as really as before. 
 
The presence of God with his people is not confined to this life; and in answer to their prayers while here, he may after they are dead bestow great blessings on his people.

title: II Kings 13:23
text: Wicked men are often spared in life and made the recipients of many great and precious blessings, in consequence of the piety and benevolence of those who have gone before them.

title: II Kings 14:3
text:
That which was right; externally; in doing, at the commencement of his reign, many things which God had commanded. 
 
External obedience will be followed by temporal benefits; but if it be merely external, it will have no reward hereafter.

title: II Kings 14:6
text: That which is written;  Deuteronomy 24:1

title: II Kings 14:7
text:
The valley of salt; near the south end of the Dead sea. 
 
  Selah; a city of Edom, supposed to be Petra the capital of Edom, situated in a valley surrounded by precipitous rocks in an exceedingly strong position.  Compare  Jeremiah 49:16 Obadiah 1:3-4 . 
 
  Joktheel; signifying subdued by God.  In going to the war against Edom he had dismissed the large army of Israelites hired to help him, according to God's direction.   II Chronicles 25:7-10   In the name now given to Selah, he ascribes his victory over it to God's help.

title: II Kings 14:8
text:
Look one another in the face; engage in battle.  This challenge may have been provoked, in part at least, by the conduct of the Israelitish army which he had dismissed,  II Chronicles 25:13 .  But it clearly betrayed the pride of his heart in view of his victory over the Edomites, to which he added the sins of idolatry and contempt of God's prophet.  II Chronicles 25:14-16 II Chronicles 25:20  
 
That pride which leads to contention and bloodshed is the fruit of wickedness, the cause of many calamities, and often the forerunner of ruin.

title: II Kings 14:9
text:
The thistle; representing the kingdom of Judah. 
 
  The cedar; the kingdom of Israel.

title: II Kings 14:14
text: Hostages; some of the principal men of the city, as security that it would not again molest him.

title: II Kings 14:19
text:
Made a conspiracy against him; thus God, by the hand of wicked men, punished him for his disobedience.  Compare  II Chronicles 25:27 . 
 
  Lachish; in the south part of Judah.

title: II Kings 14:22
text:
Elath; at the head of the eastern branch of the Red sea. 
 
  The king; his father Amaziah.

title: II Kings 14:25
text:
Hamath; a city north of Palestine.  See note to  Judges 3:3 . 
 
  The sea of the plain; the Dead sea, at the south part of the country. 
 
  Gath-hepher; a town in the tribe of Zebulun. 
 
The Lord may govern nations by means of wicked rulers; may enlarge their borders, and thus fulfil his word and accomplish towards his people his own benevolent designs.

title: II Kings 14:28
text: Damascus, and Hamath; these cities, which were taken from the Syrians in the time of David and Solomon,  II Chronicles 8:3-4 , and had been retaken by the Syrians, were now taken from them again by Jeroboam, and restored to Israel.

title: II Kings 15:5
text:
Smote the king; for his pride and presumption in attempting to burn incense to the Lord in the temple.   II Chronicles 26:16-20  
 
  A several house; a retired building, where he was separated from the rest of the inhabitants.

title: II Kings 15:9
text: The sins of rulers and distinguished persons are often the means of destruction to their distant posterity, and to multitudes of others who imitate their wicked example.

title: II Kings 15:11
text: Zachariah; he was the fourth of the descendants of Jehu.  II Kings 15:12 II Kings 10:30

title: II Kings 15:14
text:
Menahem; supposed to have been one of the generals of Zachariah. 
 
  Tirzah; a city of the tribe of Ephraim, for a time the capital of the ten tribes.   I Kings 14:1-16:34

title: II Kings 15:16
text: Tiphsah; supposed to have been in Ephraim.  A place of this name was situated on the Euphrates, and was taken possession of by Solomon.

title: II Kings 15:29
text:
Ijon--Naphtali; the places here mentioned were in the north part of the land of Israel. 
 
When the people of God rebel against them, the wicked are suffered to overcome and oppress them; nor without repentance and reformation can they escape destruction.

title: II Kings 15:30
text: The twentieth year of Jotham; as Jotham reigned but sixteen years,  II Kings 15:33 , it has been supposed that the sacred writer here means, in the twentieth year from the time when Jotham came to the throne: Ahaz his successor not being named, because the history of his reign has not yet been reached.

title: II Kings 16:3
text:
Made his son to pass through the fire; burnt him in the fire as an offering to Moloch,  II Chronicles 28:3 . 
 
No advantages without the grace of God will overcome the wickedness of the human heart, or keep men from practising the vilest transgressions.

title: II Kings 16:5
text: Could not overcome him; could not take Jerusalem his capital,  Isaiah 7:1 Isaiah 7:6 .  They gained bloody victories over him and took many persons captive,  II Chronicles 28:6-15 .

title: II Kings 16:7
text:
The king of Syria--the king of Israel; the Edomites and Philistines had also invaded him on the south, as recorded in  II Chronicles 29:17-18 . 
 
The wicked will often bow in the most abject submission to their fellow men, and give up their choicest treasures to obtain help from them, when they will not humble themselves before God for their sins, and seek effectual help from him.

title: II Kings 16:9
text: Kir; a place in upper Media, west of the Caspian sea.

title: II Kings 16:10
text:
An altar; dedicated to idol gods. 
 
The trappings of idol worship and the splendors of heathen idolatry have sometimes more attractions for the human heart, than the pure and simple worship of Jehovah; and there have been not only kings, but priests and professed ministers of religion, who would exchange the one for the other.

title: II Kings 16:16
text: Wicked rulers have ordinarily been aided by wicked ecclesiastics, and the corrupt projects of the one been supported by the ready and zealous cooperation of the other.

title: II Kings 16:17
text:
The borders of the bases; the ornamental borders placed on them by Solomon,  I Kings 7:28-29 .  These as well as the things mentioned in  II Kings 16:18 , he seems to have taken as a present to the king of Assyria. 
 
  Removed the laver from off them; that is, each of the ten lavers from off its brazen base, when he had mutilated it by the removal of its border.

title: II Kings 16:18
text: Covert for the Sabbath; supposed by some to have been a canopy or covering, under which the king and his attendants went to the temple on the Sabbath-day.

title: II Kings 17:2
text:
Not as the kings of Israel; he did not so rigidly enforce idolatry. 
 
Some sinners are less atrociously wicked than others; yet none are so innocent as not to deserve all the evils they suffer in this world, and still more dreadful evils in the world to come.

title: II Kings 17:6
text:
Halah; probably one of the northern provinces of Assyria. 
 
  In Habor by the river of Gozan; or, by Habor, the river of Gozan. Habor is generally thought to be the ancient Chaboras, a river of Mesopotamia, which flows into the Euphrates, (the modern Khabur,) and Gozan, a province situated on this river.  Some, however, place Habor and Gozan farther east. 
 
Though God bears long with guilty nations, if they repent not of their iniquities he will eventually destroy them.

title: II Kings 17:9
text:
From the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city; that is, from the least to the greatest of their dwelling-places, the tower of the watchmen being a solitary building, where only the watchman and his dependents lived. 
 
Wicked as are the outward actions of men, their secret conduct is often much worse, and has greater influence in drawing down upon them the just judgments of heaven.

title: II Kings 17:10
text: Groves; here, as often elsewhere, the original word means an image of Astarte.  See  II Kings 17:16 II Kings 18:4 .

title: II Kings 17:13
text: Men do not go to destruction without warning from God, and their disregard of him and his threatenings is among the chief causes of their ruin.

title: II Kings 17:15
text: Vanity; here used, as frequently elsewhere, to describe idolatry.

title: II Kings 17:17
text: No wickedness is so great that it may not be committed by those who have light, but reject it; who know the will of God, and yet refuse to do it.

title: II Kings 17:18
text: The tribe of Judah only; comprehending at this time the tribe of Benjamin.

title: II Kings 17:24
text: Cuthah--Ava--Hamath--Sepharvaim; provinces of Assyria north-east of Palestine.

title: II Kings 17:25
text: Even the heathen, though not as guilty as sinners under the gospel, know, or have the means of knowing, enough of God to render them guilty in not obeying him.

title: II Kings 17:26
text: The manner of the God; the proper way of worshipping him.

title: II Kings 17:29
text: Though unconverted heathen may be brought to pay a kind of reluctant outward homage to Jehovah yet without his grace their hearts will cleave to their idols, and they will still make and worship the gods to which they have been accustomed.

title: II Kings 17:30
text:
vv 30-31. 
 
  Succoth-benoth--Nergal--Ashima--Nibhaz and Tartak; names of different heathen gods.

title: II Kings 17:33
text: Feared the Lord, and served their own gods; they feared Jehovah, not as the only true God, with filial reverence and obedience to all his commands, but only as one god--the god of that particular land--among many other gods.  Supposing that he had special power in his own land, they feared his wrath and sought to appease him with outward services, while they still clung each to the worship of his own god.

title: II Kings 17:34
text:
They fear not the Lord; not with a true fear and love, as the only true God. 
 
  After their statutes; after their own idolatrous statutes.  Their religion is neither the pure worship of Jehovah, nor pure idolatry, but a mixture of the two.  This people are supposed to have been the ancestors of the Samaritans mentioned in the New Testament.

title: II Kings 17:40
text: No instruction in the knowledge and worship of God will of itself lead men to love and obey him, or prevent them from practising those sins which provoke him to destroy them.

title: II Kings 18:2
