text: Twenty and five years old; he was, accordingly, born when Ahaz was eleven years old, or perhaps, making allowance for portions of years when he was twelve years old.  See 2Ki 16.2.  This is not impossible, though some think an error of transcribing has found its way into the account respecting either Ahaz or Hezekiah.

title: II Kings 18:4
text: Nehushtan; meaning a piece of brass.

title: II Kings 18:5
text: Confidence in God is the best safeguard in danger, and the surest means of all desirable prosperity and success.

title: II Kings 18:9
text: In the fourth year of king Hezekiah; if we suppose that the fourth year of Hezekiah fell partly in the sixth and partly in the seventh year of Hoshea, then the sixth year of Hezekiah would coincide with the last part of the eighth and the beginning of the ninth year of Hoshea.

title: II Kings 18:10
text: At the end of three years; not necessarily three complete years, but a space of time occupying one whole year and part of two others. Compare our Lord's declarations respecting the time that he should lie in the grave.   Matthew 12:40 Mark 8:31

title: II Kings 18:12
text: The wicked often succeed, not on account of their worthiness, but on account of the wickedness of those over whom they triumph.

title: II Kings 18:14
text: Lachish; a fortified city in the south part of Judah.

title: II Kings 18:17
text: The upper pool; on the west side of the city.

title: II Kings 18:22
text: Whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away; either through ignorance or malice he represents the reformation in religion that Hezekiah had effected as an affront to Jehovah, as if he had thus sought to diminish the honor paid to Him.

title: II Kings 18:25
text:
The Lord said to me; an impious falsehood, by which he sought to intimidate the people. 
 
Success emboldens men in transgression, and they sometimes claim that they please God, because he suffers them for a time to prosper in their sins.

title: II Kings 18:27
text: Eat their own dung; in the extremity of the famine which he threatened to bring upon them.

title: II Kings 18:35
text: Ascribing to creatures or to false gods what belongs only to Jehovah, and pretending that it is as vain to trust in him as in them, is a sure way to provoke his wrath.

title: II Kings 19:1
text: God is the unfailing resource of his people.  In times of trouble they repair to him, and find him to be a very present and all-sufficient helper.

title: II Kings 19:3
text: Come to the birth--not strength to bring forth; it is a day of prolonged anguish, from which we have no strength to deliver ourselves.

title: II Kings 19:4
text: Jehovah is a prayer hearing God; and his people not only call on him themselves, but desire the prayers of others, especially such are are distinguished by his presence and favor.

title: II Kings 19:6
text: Those who trust in the Lord, and so fear as to obey him, have no reason to fear any others, but may expect in due time his effectual aid.

title: II Kings 19:7
text: A blast; the original may mean either a wind, that is, a pestilential blast to destroy his army, or a spirit, that is, of consternation,  II Kings 19:9 .

title: II Kings 19:8
text: Libnah; one of the fortified cities of Judah.

title: II Kings 19:12
text: Because the idols in which the wicked trusted have not delivered them, some conclude that Jehovah will not deliver his people, and treat him as if he could do no more, for or against them, than gods of wood and of stone.

title: II Kings 19:19
text: Jehovah will show that he is the one only living and true God, and that those who exalt themselves he is able to abase; and will effectually protect and provide for all who trust in him.

title: II Kings 19:21
text: The daughter of Zion; the church of God that had its centre in Jerusalem.

title: II Kings 19:23
text:
Cut down the tall cedar-trees; the desolation of Lebanon, the most conspicuous object of Palestine, figuratively represents the conquest of the whole land, the desolation of its fenced cities, and the subjugation of its king and princes. 
 
  The lodgings of his borders; or, its extreme lodges, its most remote recesses. 
 
  The forest of his Carmel; the word Carmel here signifies a park of goodly trees, interspersed with fertile gardens.

title: II Kings 19:24
text:
Have digged--dried up; neither the want of water, as in marching through deserts, nor its abundance, as in the arms of the Nile, by which the cities of Egypt are defended, can arrest my course.  "Strange waters" are either wells in foreign lands which he will dig for his army, thus possessing himself of the country, or waters unknown to others. 
 
  All the rivers of besieged places; or, as we may render, all the canals of Egypt, which served for its defence.

title: II Kings 19:25
text:
I have done it; the Lord had suffered him to accomplish what he had done, and it was all in the fulfilment of the purposes of Jehovah. 
 
The exploits of the wicked are only a fulfilment of a part of the plan of Jehovah; and when he sees fit he can dash them in pieces as a potter's vessel, or cause them in his own way and time to come to an ignominious and miserable end.

title: II Kings 19:28
text: Will put my hook in thy nose; as men tame ferocious beasts and lead them at their pleasure.

title: II Kings 19:29
text:
A sign unto thee; to Hezekiah and his people. 
 
  This year--the second year; the land was possessed and desolated by the enemy.  Agriculture had been already interrupted for more than a year.  The present year there had been no seed-time, so that there would be no harvest for the following year. 
 
To his people God affords evidence that it is safe to trust in him, and to wait upon him in humble supplication; for in due time all his promises will be fulfilled.

title: II Kings 19:35
text:
They arose; those who were spared. 
 
  They were all dead; those who had, the night before, been smitten by the angel of the Lord. 
 
Armies are as dependent on God as individuals; he keeps the breath in their nostrils, and can at any time take it away and leave them all dead corpses.

title: II Kings 19:37
text: Nisroch; an idol god.

title: II Kings 20:1
text:
Sick unto death; with a deadly disease. 
 
In every situation men are liable to sickness and death.  The should therefore have all their affairs so arranged, as to be habitually prepared to leave this world and enter on the retributions of eternity.

title: II Kings 20:5
text: Prayer is often a means of removing sickness which would otherwise prove mortal, and inducing the Lord to continue life when he would otherwise have taken it away.

title: II Kings 20:7
text:
The boil; with which Hezekiah was aflicted, and which, if God had not interposed, would have been mortal. 
 
The fact that diseases are God's servants, and that they come and go at his bidding, should never supersede the use of appropriate means, or lead us in any measure to neglect them.

title: II Kings 20:9
text: The shadow; the shadow on the sun-dial,  II Kings 20:11 Isaiah 38:8 .

title: II Kings 20:11
text: The Lord gives abundant evidence of the truth of his promises, that his people may trust his word without fear of being disappointed.

title: II Kings 20:13
text:
Showed them all the house of his precious things--all that was found in his treasures; in this he was manifestly elated with vanity, and God accordingly forewarned him of the judgments that should come from Babylon upon his family.  Compare  II Chronicles 32:31 . 
 
Even good men are liable to be elated with their blessings, to seek applause, and so display their acquisitions as to displease the Lord.

title: II Kings 20:16
text: The Lord will effectually humble the pride of his people, take off their hearts from transitory, uncertain riches, and lead them to trust alone in Him who giveth them richly all things to enjoy, and who can at any time take away what his has given.

title: II Kings 20:18
text: Thy sons; that is, thy descendants.  The threatening was literally fulfilled in the case of Daniel and his companions, who were "of the king's seed."   Daniel 1:3

title: II Kings 20:19
text: However trying the dispensations of Providence, pious men will submit to them; knowing that God has the best of reasons for all which he does, and doeth all things well.

title: II Kings 21:2
text: Men from religious families sometimes commit wickedness far beyond others who have not had pious instruction and example.

title: II Kings 21:6
text: Observed times; or, practised divination.  Divination and witchcraft, in all their varied forms, were parts of the ancient system of idolatry, as they are of modern systems.

title: II Kings 21:9
text: Those who break over the restraints of a pious education and become abandoned in wickedness, often go to greater lengths in inquity than even the heathen, and ripen for more aggravated ruin.

title: II Kings 21:12
text: Both his ears shall tingle; at the dreadfulness of the judgments which God would bring upon them.

title: II Kings 21:13
text:
The line of Samaria, and the plummet of the house of Ahab; the line and the plummet are here the symbols of God's exact justice in the judgments he inflicts on the wicked.  Compare  Amos 7:7-9 .  The meaning of the figure is, that God will execute upon Judah and Jerusalem the same righteous judgments that he has sent upon Samaria and the house of Ahab. 
 
  Wipe Jerusalem; wipe out its inhabitants and its wealth, and utterly overturn it.

title: II Kings 21:21
text: The wickedness of fathers will be likely to be imitated by their children, and that of rulers by their people; and after having been tempters of each other in this world, they will, if they continue in sin, become tormentors of each other in the world to come.

title: II Kings 22:1
text: Though children may be expected generally to imitate their parents, a wicked child sometimes arises from a very pious family, and a pious child from a very wicked family; thus showing the power and the sovereignity of God in the bestowment of his grace.

title: II Kings 22:3
text: True piety will manifest itself in efforts to promote the salvation not only of him who has it, but of all who may feel his influence.

title: II Kings 22:8
text: The book of the law; this is supposed to have been the original copy of the law of Moses, written and deposited in the ark by himself. The book of the law, or a copy of it, had been used in the days of Jehoshaphat by those who were sent through the cities of Judah as religious teachers,  II Chronicles 17:9 .  But it seems to have been lost sight of some time before Josiah's reign.

title: II Kings 22:11
text: He rent his clothes; on account of the judgments denounced in the law against the people; and to which they were exposed on account of their idolatry.   II Kings 22:19

title: II Kings 22:12
text: A real belief of the threatenings of God against sin, will lead to the most earnest desire and diligent efforts to escape his wrath, and obtain his everlasting favor.

title: II Kings 22:14
text: In the college; literally, in the second, which seems to mean the second and newer part of the city, lying below Zion on the north.

title: II Kings 22:16
text: The piety of an individual, though it will avail to his salvation and his deliverance from many temporal evils, will not save others who continue in their sins, or avert from them ultimately the judgments of heaven.

title: II Kings 22:20
text: Death, though the consequence of sin, is through the grace of God sent in mercy to his people, and made the means of delivering them from the evils of this world, and introducing them to the perfect and unending joys of the world to come.

title: II Kings 23:3
text:
Stood to the covenant; accepted it and bound themselves to fulfil it. 
 
No repentance is genuine which does not lead to external reformation; and no reformation is accepted of God, but such as springs from the heart, and is persevered in to the end.

title: II Kings 23:4
text:
The grove; the wooden statue of Astarte. 
 
  Fields of Kidron; on the east side of Jerusalem, through which ran the brook of that name.   II Kings 23:6  
 
  Unto Bethel; which, as the chief seat of idolatry under the Israelitish kings, he purposed to defile in every way.  See  II Kings 23:15-16 .

title: II Kings 23:6
text:
The grove; see note to  II Kings 23:4 . 
 
Things which have been used as instruments, and which operate as incentives to evil, should be effectually removed, and either destroyed or so treated that their evil influence.

title: II Kings 23:8
text:
vv 8-9. 
 
  All the priests--came not up to the altar; these were Levitical priests who had been set apart to burn incense on the high places. Josiah, after he had taken away their unlawful office, would not allow them to minister any more at God's altar in Jerusalem, but granted them their regular portion which fell to them as priests forbidden to officiate.  Compare  Leviticus 21:21-22 .  Some suppose that they were the same as the idolatrous priests mentioned  II Kings 23:5 .  But there another word is used in the original, which is not elsewhere applied to Levitical priests. 
 
  Geba; in the north part of Judea. 
 
  Beer-sheba; in the south part of Judea.

title: II Kings 23:10
text: The valley of the children of Hinnom; a deep valley on the south-east side of Jerusalem, in which idolaters made their children pass through fire in honor of their idol gods.

title: II Kings 23:12
text: The altars--of Ahaz; which had been erected to idols.

title: II Kings 23:13
text:
Mount of corruption; supposed to be the mount of Olives. 
 
  Ashtoreth--Chemosh--Milcom; idol gods.

title: II Kings 23:15
text: The altar that was at Beth-el; consecrated to the worship of the golden calf set up by Jeroboam the son of Nebat,  I Kings 12:29 .  The kingdom of Israel no longer existed, but many of the Israelites remained in their own country.  Josiah found himself able to go through the cities of Samaria and destroy their idolatrous places without molestation from the distant Assyrian monarchs, who were already falling before the rising Chaldean empire.

title: II Kings 23:16
text:
The man of God;  I Kings 13:1-22:53 
 
Though the fulfilment of divine declarations may be long delayed, and many may conclude that they will never be accomplished, not one jot or tittle of them will fail to come to pass.

title: II Kings 23:17
text: Title; or, monument.

title: II Kings 23:22
text: Such a passover; with such solemnity, and in such strict accordance with the law of Moses, a copy of which had recently been found in the temple.

title: II Kings 23:25
text: No penitence on the part of individuals, and no external reformation of those over whom htey have influence, can save guilty nations who have sinned away ther day of grace, from meeting the retribution which they deserve.

title: II Kings 23:29
text:
Megiddo; near the Kishon, and on the border of the great plain of Esdraelon.  The highway from Egypt to Assyria led by this place. 
 
Though pious men may, through their own fault or the wickedness of others, come to an untimely and violent death, it will be well with them at last.

title: II Kings 23:33
text: Put him in bands at Riblah; after he had first deposed him from his kingly office in Jerusalem.   II Chronicles 36:3   The district of Hamath lay on the northern border of Palestine, and through it the armies of Egypt on the one side, and Assyria and Babylon on the other, passed in their wars with each other.

title: II Kings 24:2
text: The Lord is never at a loss for instruments to punish his rebellious people; and though the wicked act out their enmity to him in opposing them, yet through them he fulfils his declarations and accomplishes his wise and holy designs.

title: II Kings 24:3
text: Out of his sight; from the land where he had manifested his special presence and favor.

title: II Kings 24:10
text: The Lord sometimes permits one class of wicked men to prevail against his people, and at other times another; but their own sins are the cause of their troubles, and whoever may be their oppressors, he never suffers them to inflict evils greater than their iniquities deserve.

title: II Kings 24:12
text: In the eighth year of his reign; it is generally agreed that the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar is here reckoned from the time when his father invested him with supreme authority over his army, while, in  Daniel 2:1 , the date is reckoned more strictly from his ascension to the throne after his father's death.

title: II Kings 24:14
text: The poorest--of the land; from whom he had nothing to fear.

title: II Kings 24:16
text:
Men of might; the warriors. 
 
  Seven thousand--a thousand; the sacred writer specifies certain classes of the ten thousand before named.  The other two thousand may have been nobles and other principal men.  The number of ten thousand includes only adult males, the women and children that accompanied them not being reckoned. 
 
To whom much is given, of them much will be required; and those who are distinguished by outward privileges and blessings, if they abuse them will be distinguished in their punishment.

title: II Kings 25:3
text: No human power or skill can avail against the providence of God; and when he undertakes to punish guilty individuals or nations, without repentance and reformation there is no escape.

title: II Kings 25:4
text: Between two walls--by the king's garden; this gate was in the southern part of the city, near the pool of Siloam,  Nehemiah 3:15 .  The double wall here mentioned was probably built across the valley that lies between Zion adn Ophel, at the mouth of which valley is the pool of Siloam.

title: II Kings 25:5
text: The plains of Jericho; the deep valley through which the Jordan lows and in which the Dead sea lies.

title: II Kings 25:7
text: The obstinate wickedness of parents is often the occasion of ruin to their children; and those senses which have been inlets of iniquity, become inlets of torment.

title: II Kings 25:9
text: As a punishment to his people, the Lord sometimes suffers the wicked to abolish the observance of his own ordinances, and to carry away or destroy what has been most solemnly devoted to his service.

title: II Kings 25:10
text: Brake down the walls; to prevent the inhabitants of Jerusalem from giving the king of Babylon any further trouble.

title: II Kings 25:16
text:
The two pillars--sea--bases; see the description of these in  I Kings 7:15-47 . 
 
  Without weight; in such abundance, that the quantity and its value were not estimated.

title: II Kings 25:18
text: Those most intimately associated with the wicked in crime, are most exposed to be partakers with them in punishment.

title: II Kings 25:21
text: Slew them at Riblah; as special friends of Zedekiah and men of influence among the people.

title: II Kings 25:24
text: Supreme power is often greatly coveted, and no crimes are so base as not to be perpetrated to obtain it.  But the greater the power which is obtained by iniquity, the greater curse it will be to those who receive it.

title: II Kings 25:25
text: Mizpah; supposed to be a town in the tribe of Benjamin.

title: II Kings 25:27
text: The hearts of kings, and of all others, are in the hands of the Lord; and he can at any time incline them to favor even the most abject and distressed, and thus show them and others that they who truly seek the Lord shall not want any good thing.

title: II Kings 25:28
text: The kings; those who had been conquered by the Babylonians, and who were kept as prisoners at Babylon.

title: I Chronicles 10:1
text: Mount Gilboa; on the south of the valley of Esdraelon, sometimes called the valley of Jezreel.

title: I Chronicles 10:4
text: Those who have not chosen God as their portion and have no hope in his mercy, are often very miserable when they come to die; and sometimes are ready to hasten their death by their own hands.

title: I Chronicles 10:6
text: All his house; all the men belonging to his household who were present at the battle.  His son Ish-bosheth, called Esh-baal in  I Chronicles 8:33 I Chronicles 9:39 , survived him, and also Mephibosheth the son of Jonathan.  Ziba also, one of the servants belonging to Saul's house, is mentioned in  II Samuel 9:2 , etc.

title: I Chronicles 10:9
text: To carry tidings unto their idols; to whose aid they ascribed their victory.

title: I Chronicles 10:10
text: Fastened his head; his body had been fastened to the wall in Beth-shan.   I Samuel 31:10

title: I Chronicles 10:12
text: Jabesh; on the east of Jordan.

title: I Chronicles 10:14
text: To seek help from evil spirits is a great sin, and exposes those who do it to the just judgments of God.  Pretensions to converse with departed spirits dishonor him and his word, and should be refrained from and discountenanced.   Leviticus 19:26 Leviticus 19:31 Leviticus 20:27 Deuteronomy 18:11 Isaiah 8:19 Isaiah 8:20

title: I Chronicles 11:1
text:
All Israel gathered; this was after David had reigned over the tribe of Judah alone seven years and six months.   II Samuel 5:5   For the position of Hebron, see note to  II Samuel 2:1 . 
 
When the time comes, all persons and things conspire, as far as may be needful, to advance those who are selected of God for stations of honor and responsibility, and to fulfil his designs of love and mercy with regard to them.

title: I Chronicles 11:4
text: Jebus; the former name of Jerusalem.

title: I Chronicles 11:6
text: Chief and captain; that is, over the host.

title: I Chronicles 11:8
text: Millo; a fortified part of Jerusalem.

title: I Chronicles 11:9
text: The presence and favor of God will overcome all obstructions in the way of the advancement of those whom he delights to honor.

title: I Chronicles 11:11
text: Lifted up his spear against three hundred; see note to  II Samuel 23:8 .

title: I Chronicles 11:13
text: Though deliverance from evil comes from God, yet he works by means, and men must employ them according to his appointment in order to receive his help.

title: I Chronicles 11:14
text: They set themselves; Eleazar and his associates.  According to the opinion of some, his chief helper in this exploit was Shammah, to whom this victory is ascribed in  II Samuel 23:11 . A comparison of this list  I Chronicles 11:11-47  of David's heroes with that given in  II Samuel 23:1-39  shows several points of difference, which a fuller knowledge of the history of those times might help us to explain.  They relate wholly to names or circumstantial details.

title: I Chronicles 11:15
text: In the valley of Rephaim; south-west of Jerusalem.

title: I Chronicles 11:19
text: A generous man will not encourage others to expose their lives for his gratification, but will rather deny himself than be the means of such exposure to his fellow men.

title: I Chronicles 11:26
text: The valiant men of the armies; this list of David's mighty men is fuller than that contained in the corresponding list in  II Samuel 23:11-39 .

title: I Chronicles 12:1
text:
Ziklag; the town assigned by Achish, king of Gath, to David while he sojourned among the Philistines,  I Samuel 27:6 .  It lay south-west from Jerusalem. 
 
The hearts of all are in the hand of the Lord.  He endows them with qualities which fit them for the work to which they are called, and when he has need of them, uses them in advancing his cause.

title: I Chronicles 12:2
text: Of Saul's brethren of Benjamin; belonging to the tribe of Benjamin, which was Saul's tribe.  The list, 1Ch 12.3-7, apparently includes some of the tribe of Judah, as the Korhites, 1Ch 2.43, and those from Gedor,  I Chronicles 4:4 .

title: I Chronicles 12:15
text:
Went over Jordan; the Gadites dwelt on the eastern side of Jordan. Many suppose that the event recorded in this verse took place when they were on their way to join David in Ziklag. 
 
  The valleys; the valleys that lined the Jordan on either side.

title: I Chronicles 12:17
text: Servicesto be acceptable must be sincere; and what is done heartily, as unto the Lord, he will approve, and upon it bestow an abundant reward.

title: I Chronicles 12:19
text:
Came with the Philistines;  I Samuel 29:1 
  But they helped them not; David and his men helped not the Philistines against Saul.

title: I Chronicles 12:20
text:
Went to Ziklag; went back on his return from the army of the Philistines. 
 
  There fell to him of Manasseh; these seven men seem to be the same as those of Manasseh referred to in 1Ch 12.19.

title: I Chronicles 12:21
text: The band of the rovers; the Amalekites who had spoiled Ziklag,  I Samuel 30:31 .

title: I Chronicles 12:22
text:
The host of God; very numerous and powerful.  Compare  Psalms 65:9 ;  Psalms 104:16 . 
 
The Lord can touch the hearts of multitudes as well as of individuals, and can unite as many as he pleases in the promotion of his cause.

title: I Chronicles 12:27
text: The Aaronites; the priests of the house of Aaron.  This consisted of two main branches, the family of Eleazar, and that of Ithamar. Abiathar, the high-priest under David, was of the family of Ithamar; Zadok, here mentioned as "a young man might of valor," and the successor of Abiathar the son of Ahimelech in the office of high-priest,  I Kings 2:26-27 I Kings 2:35 , was of the line of Eleazar.  See  I Chronicles 24:3 .

title: I Chronicles 12:32
text: Men of understanding as well as of might are needed in the concerns of states and kingdoms; and when God raises them up and inclines them with one heart to engage in his service, it is an indication of mercy, and should call forth the devout thanksgiving of his people.

title: I Chronicles 12:33
text: Double heart; wavering, inconstant.

title: I Chronicles 12:38
text:
Perfect heart; united, single, and firm in their purpose to make David king. 
 
  All the rest also of Israel; who came not in person to Hebron.  For though the number assembled was very great, consisting of about three hundred and fifty thousand armed men, a very large number remained at home; and the representation from the different tribes, for reasons that are not explained, was very unequal.  See the account of the numbering of the Israelites near the close of David's reign, 1Ch 21.5. 
 
Union in the selection and support of good rulers, is an occasion of gratitude and joy to all who desire the honor of God and the prosperity of his people.

title: I Chronicles 13:1
text: When those in public stations propose to make changes, it is ordinarily wise to consult the leading men and secure their cooperation.  This will open the way to bring the subject before the people generally, and thus to unite them in it.

title: I Chronicles 13:3
text: The ark; this had been for a number of years at Kirjath-jearim, a city of the Gibeonites.

title: I Chronicles 13:5
text: Shihor; at the south-western, Hemath, at the north-eastern extremity of Palestine.

title: I Chronicles 13:8
text:
Played; danced, as an expression of his joy and gratitude to God.  I Chronicles 15:29 II Samuel 6:5 II Samuel 6:14 II Samuel 6:20 . 
 
Times of religious reformation are justly times of rejoicing.  The king and the beggar, if they love the Lord, will unite in praising him and rendering thanks for his approbation, or avoid his displeasure.

title: I Chronicles 13:10
text:
He put his hand to the ark; this was contrary to the divine command,  Numbers 4:15-20 . 
 
That reverential fear of God which leads to a careful regard to his commandments, is essential to secure his approbation, or avoid his displeasure.

title: I Chronicles 13:13
text: The city of David; Zion.

title: I Chronicles 14:2
text:
Lifted up on high; greatly strengthened and prospered. 
 
All blessings, temporal and spiritual, come from God.  When this is duly acknowledged, it honors him and prepares the way for the increase and continuance of his favors.

title: I Chronicles 14:8
text: Great mercies are often followed by great trials; but careful inquiry as to the will of God, adn a readiness when it is known to obey it, will secure his aid, and in due time give deliverance from trouble, and victory over every foe.

title: I Chronicles 14:9
text: The valley of Rephaim; near Jerusalem on the south-west.

title: I Chronicles 14:10
text: Go up; to the head-quarters of the Philistines, from which they spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.

title: I Chronicles 14:11
text: Baal-perazim; near the valley of Rephaim on the south.

title: I Chronicles 14:16
text:
Gibeon; in the tribe of Benjamin. 
 
  Gazer; one of the cities of the Philistines.

title: I Chronicles 15:2
text: Our mistakes in times past should make us wiser in future; should lead us to avoid the errors into which, from presumption, ignorance, or inattention, we may have fallen; and should engage us in the performance of all duties which we have neglected.

title: I Chronicles 15:5
text:
vv 5-7. 
 
  Kohath--Merari--Gershom; the three sons of Levi.   Exodus 6:16

title: I Chronicles 15:8
text:
vv 8-10. 
 
  Elizaphan--Hebron--Uzziel; Hebron and Uzziel were the sons of Kohath; Elizaphan, or Elzaphan, was the son of Ussiel, and the grandson of Kohath.   Exodus 6:18 Exodus 6:22

title: I Chronicles 15:11
text: Zadok and Abiathar; Zadok ministered as priest at Gibeon, where were the tabernacle, the brazen altar, and the daily sacrifice.  See  I Chronicles 16:39-40 .  Abiathar was the regular high-priest officiating at Jerusalem.  See note to  I Chronicles 12:27 .

title: I Chronicles 15:12
text:
Sanctify yourselves; by cleansing themselves from all ceremonial and moral pollution, and by the performance of those duties which God had prescribed for that purpose. 
 
Peculiar sanctity becomes the ministers of religion, and especially when engaged in religious duties; they should be watchful not to indulge in any thing offensive to God, or that tends to unfit them for his holy service.

title: I Chronicles 15:13
text: Made a breach upon us; in the destruction of Uzzah.

title: I Chronicles 15:16
text: Singing is an important part of divine worship, and when rightly performed is acceptable to God.  Those who engage in it should never forget that God looks upon the heart, and requires that those who worship him should worship him in spirit and in truth.

title: I Chronicles 15:26
text: Helped the Levites; by enabling them to carry the ark in safety to its place without suffering any calamity, such as that which had befallen Uzzah.

title: I Chronicles 15:28
text: Though that fervor of devotion which the Holy Spirit inspires, and which is manifested by those who are under his influence, is often despised and treated as degrading, especially to the rich, the great, and the powerful, this will not prevent true Christians from being zealous in the service of God.

title: I Chronicles 15:29
text: She despised him; she thought that he degraded himself, by thus joining with the priests and the people in their expressions of religious joy.

title: I Chronicles 16:2
text: Love to God and generosity to men go well together, and mutually aid each other.

title: I Chronicles 16:7
text:
This psalm; composed by David, and now first given to the musicians to be sung in public worship. 
 
Singing the praises of God and calling upon his name have ever formed an important part of his worship, and are well suited to the devotions of his people.

title: I Chronicles 16:12
text: The judgments of his mouth; those decisions and statutes which he had made known for the benefit of the people.

title: I Chronicles 16:14
text: In all the earth; the Lord reigns among all people, and so manifests himself by his providential dealings with men as to leave them without excuse if they do not love and obey him.

title: I Chronicles 16:15
text:
A thousand generations; a definite for a long indefinite period. 
 
The covenant which God hath made in Christ with his people, is an everlasting covenant, and its blessings are sure to all who put their trust in him.

title: I Chronicles 16:23
text: Praising God for his salvation, and praying that all may be made partakers of it, should form an important part of our daily duties.

title: I Chronicles 16:30
text: The world also shall be stable; in the original, the same as  Psalms 93:1 , "The world also is established, that it cannot be moved;" where see note  Psalms 93:1 .

title: I Chronicles 16:33
text: To judge the earth; deal righteously with men according to their character.

title: I Chronicles 16:34
text: The mercy of God in Christ is the only ground of hope for lost and guilty men.  On this they should depend, while they glory in him as their righteousness, wisdom, and strength.

title: I Chronicles 16:37
text: The ark; this was carried to Jerusalem; and a part of the priests resided there with David to minister before it.  Another part resided at Gibeon, where the tabernacle and brazen altar still remained, and where was offered the daily sacrifice.   I Chronicles 16:39-40 I Chronicles 21:29

title: I Chronicles 16:41
text: With them; with Zadok and his brethren at Gibeon.  See note to  I Chronicles 16:37 .

title: I Chronicles 16:43
text:
Bless his house; instruct and implore blessings upon his household, and engage with them in the worship of God. 
 
While the public worship of God should not be neglected, but statedly observed according to divine appointment, it should never supersede, or be suffered to hinder the regular observance of family duties.

title: I Chronicles 17:1
text:
As David sat in his house; for the exposition of this chapter, see the notes on  II Samuel 7:1-29 . 
 
A godly man is not content merely to receive blessings himself, but wishes to do all he can for the honor of God and the good of mankind.

title: I Chronicles 17:7
text: The elevation of rulers is from God; and the higher they are raised in power and influence, the greater is their obligation to love and serve him, and the greater will be their guilt, and the more dreadful their condemnation, if they rebel against him.

title: I Chronicles 17:16
text: The goodness of God to his people deeply humbles them on account of their unworthiness, and leads them to feel that for all their mercies they are indebted to the riches of his grace.

title: I Chronicles 17:24
text: The righteous wish to have the promises of God fulfilled, not merely that it may be well with them, but that he may be glorified, and multitudes be led to adore him for ever.

title: I Chronicles 18:1
text:
The narratives in this and the following chapter are for substance the same as those contained in  II Samuel 8:1-18 II Samuel 10:1-19 , and the reader is referred to the notes on these chapters. 
 
When a man's ways please the Lord, he often makes his enemies to be at peace with him, or gives him the victory over all his foes.

title: I Chronicles 18:3
text: As he went; the narrative leaves it doubtful whether it was David or Hadarezer who was on his way to the river Euphrates.

title: I Chronicles 18:8
text: The spoils of the enemies of the Lord when they come into the possession of his people, instead of being used for their own aggrandizement, should be consecrated to his service and to the good of mankind.

title: I Chronicles 18:12
text:
Abishai; in 2 Samuel, the victory is ascribed to David, because whatever was done by his servants was done by him.  In the title of Psalm 60, Joab is mentioned as the leader.  Perhaps Joab was the commander-in-chief of David's forces, while Abishai led the division that gained this victory. 
 
  Of the Edomites; in  II Samuel 8:13 , they are called Syrians. Probably the Syrians and Edomites were in alliance. 
 
  Eighteen thousand; in the title to Psalm 60, which seems plainly to refer to the same event, the number is given as twelve thousand.  It may be that twelve thousand were slain in one decisive battle, and six thousand more in one or more other engagements.  When the events of a whole campaign are crowded into single sentences, it is not surprising that in different narratives there should be apparent disagreements, which a full knowledge of the details would enable us to reconcile. "The valley of salt" here mentioned lies at the southern extremity of the Dead sea, where there is a salt mountain, and where the streams are salt as brine.
